title.zh: 卷七十二 董卓列傳
title.raw: 卷七十二 董卓列傳 Volume 72: Biography of Dong Zhuo

sentences.zh: 董卓字仲穎，

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo, courtesy name Zhongying,
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo, whose courtesy name was Zhongying,

sentences.zh: 〈《卓別傳》曰：「卓父君雅為穎川輪氏尉，生卓及弟旻，故卓字仲穎，旻字叔穎。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Separate Biography of Dong Zhuo states: "Zhuo's father Junya was commandant of Lunshi in Yingchuan; he begat Zhuo and his younger brother Min; therefore Zhuo's courtesy name was Zhongying and Min's was Shuying."〉
translations.idiomatic: A supplementary biography of Dong Zhuo records that his father Junya served as commandant of Lun County in Yingchuan and had two sons—Dong Zhuo and the younger Dong Min—which is why Zhuo took the courtesy name Zhongying and Min took Shuying, marking their birth order among brothers.

sentences.zh: 隴西臨洮人也。

translations.literal: He was a man of Lintao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Lintao in Longxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 性麤猛有謀。

translations.literal: In nature he was coarse and fierce and had stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he was blunt and fearless, yet shrewd.

sentences.zh: 少嘗游羌中，盡與豪帥相結。

translations.literal: In youth he once roamed in the midst of the Qiang, and entirely associated with their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he traveled among the Qiang and won the friendship of every tribal leader he met.

sentences.zh: 後歸耕於野，諸豪帥有來從之者，卓為殺耕牛，與共宴樂，豪帥感其意，歸相斂得雜畜千餘頭以遺之，由是以健俠知名。

translations.literal: Later he returned and plowed in the wilds; when various chieftains came to follow him, Zhuo for them slaughtered a plow-ox and together with them feasted and made merry; the chieftains were moved by his intent, returned and mutually collected more than a thousand head of miscellaneous livestock to present to him; by this means he became known as a stalwart knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he was farming in the countryside, tribal leaders who rallied to him found him slaughtering his draft ox to host them in revelry. Touched by his generosity, they went home and pooled more than a thousand head of mixed livestock as gifts. From that episode his name spread as a bold man of chivalrous repute.

sentences.zh: 為州兵馬掾，常徼守塞下。

translations.literal: He became aide for military horses of the province, and constantly patrolled and guarded below the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed aide in charge of the provincial army's horses and spent much of his time patrolling the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 〈《說文》曰：「徼，巡也。

translations.literal: 〈The Shuowen states: "Jiao means to patrol."
translations.idiomatic: The Shuowen dictionary glosses jiao as "to patrol."

sentences.zh: 」《前書》曰：「中尉巡徼京師。

translations.literal: " The Former Documents states: "The commandant of the capital patrolled and inspected the capital region."
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu notes that the metropolitan commandant conducted patrols throughout the capital region.

sentences.zh: 」《音義》曰：「所謂游徼，備盜賊。」〉

translations.literal: " The Sound and Meaning states: "What is called patrol officer is to prepare against bandits and thieves."〉
translations.idiomatic: A commentary on pronunciation and sense adds that such patrol officers were meant to guard against robbers and thieves.〉

sentences.zh: 卓膂力過人，雙帶兩鞬，左右馳射，

translations.literal: Zhuo's physical strength surpassed others; he doubly girded two quivers, and to left and right galloped and shot,
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's strength was extraordinary: he wore paired quivers at his belt and could shoot at full gallop to either side,

sentences.zh: 〈《方言》曰：「所以藏箭謂之服，藏弓謂之鞬。

translations.literal: 〈The Fangyan states: "That by which one stores arrows is called fu; that by which one stores a bow is called jian."
translations.idiomatic: The Fangyan distinguishes the case that holds arrows (fu) from the scabbard that sheathes the bow (jian).

sentences.zh: 」《左氏傳》云：「右屬櫜鞬。」〉

translations.literal: " The Zuo Tradition says: "On the right were attached quiver and bow-case."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo zhuan likewise speaks of quiver and bow-case hanging at the rider's right.〉

sentences.zh: 為羌胡所畏。

translations.literal: He was feared by the Qiang and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang and other frontier peoples held him in awe.

sentences.zh: 桓帝末，以六郡良家子為羽林郎，從中郎將張奐為軍司馬，共擊漢陽叛羌，破之，拜郎中，賜縑九千匹。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Huan's reign, by reason of being a good-family son of the Six Commanderies he became a gentleman-at-arms of the Feathered Forest; he followed General of the Gentlemen of the Household Zhang Huan as army major and together attacked the rebel Qiang of Hanyang, defeated them, was appointed gentleman of the interior, and was granted nine thousand bolts of plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the end of Emperor Huan's reign, Dong Zhuo entered the Feathered Forest guard as a youth of respectable families from the northwestern Six Commanderies. He served under General Zhang Huan as army major, helped crush the Qiang rebellion in Hanyang, was promoted to gentleman of the interior, and received a reward of nine thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 卓曰：「為者則己，有者則士。」

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "The doer is myself; the possessor is the officers."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo declared, "The credit for the deed is mine; the spoils belong to the troops."

sentences.zh: 〈為功者雖己，共有者乃士。〉

translations.literal: 〈The one who achieved the merit was although himself; those who shared in having it were the officers.〉
translations.idiomatic: The gloss explains that although Zhuo had earned the distinction, he treated the bounty as belonging collectively to his men.〉

sentences.zh: 乃悉分與吏兵，無所留。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entirely divided it among clerks and soldiers, keeping nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed the entire grant among officers and rank-and-file, keeping not a single bolt for himself.

sentences.zh: 稍遷西域戊己校尉，坐事免。

translations.literal: Gradually he was promoted to Colonel Protecting the Wu and Ji Regions of the Western Regions, and because of an affair was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Colonel of the Wu and Ji garrisons on the Western Regions frontier, then lost the office over an unspecified offense.

sentences.zh: 後為并州刺史，河東太守。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Bing province and Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as inspector of Bing province and as administrator of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年春，遣使者持節就長安拜張溫為太尉。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, an envoy bearing credentials went to Chang'an and invested Zhang Wen as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Zhongping, the court sent an envoy with imperial credentials to Chang'an to appoint Zhang Wen grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 三公在外，始之於溫。

translations.literal: Of the Three Dukes being outside, it began with Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen was the first of the Three Dukes to receive his seal of office outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 其冬，徵溫還京師，韓遂乃殺邊章及伯玉、文侯，擁兵十餘萬，進圍隴西。

translations.literal: That winter, Wen was summoned back to the capital; Han Sui thereupon killed Bian Zhang and Boyu and Wenhou, gathered troops of more than a hundred thousand, and advanced to besiege Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhang Wen was recalled to Luoyang. Han Sui then murdered his former allies Bian Zhang, Boyu, and Wenhou, rallied well over a hundred thousand men, and marched to lay siege to Longxi.

sentences.zh: 太守李相如反，與遂連和，共殺涼州刺史耿鄙。

translations.literal: Administrator Li Xiangru rebelled, allied with Sui, and together they killed Inspector of Liangzhou Geng Bi.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrator Li Xiangru rose in revolt, joined forces with Han Sui, and together they slew Geng Bi, the provincial inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 而鄙司馬扶風馬騰，

translations.literal: But Bi's major Ma Teng of Fufeng,
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bi's army major Ma Teng of Fufeng, meanwhile,

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：「騰字壽成，扶風茂陵人，馬援後也。

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe states: "Teng, courtesy name Shoucheng, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng, a descendant of Ma Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe identifies him as Ma Teng, courtesy name Shoucheng, a native of Maoling in Fufeng and a descendant of the general Ma Yuan.

sentences.zh: 長八尺餘，身體洪大，面鼻雄異，而性賢厚，人多敬之。」〉

translations.literal: He was more than eight chi in height, his body large and imposing, his face and nose strikingly unusual, yet his nature was worthy and generous, and many people respected him."〉
translations.idiomatic: He stood over eight chi tall, with a massive frame and striking features, yet his manner was open and kindly, which won him wide respect among the people."〉

sentences.zh: 亦擁兵反叛，又漢陽王國，自號「合眾將軍」，皆與韓遂合。

translations.literal: Also gathered troops and rebelled; moreover Wang Guo of Hanyang styled himself "General Who Unites the Host," and all united with Han Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng likewise took up arms in rebellion. Wang Guo of Hanyang declared himself "General Who Unites the Masses," and every faction entered Han Sui's coalition.

sentences.zh: 共推王國為主，悉令領其眾，寇掠三輔。

translations.literal: Together they promoted Wang Guo as lord and entirely ordered him to lead their hosts, raiding and plundering the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: They acknowledged Wang Guo as their overall leader and placed all their forces under his command, then swept eastward to pillage the capital region known as the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 五年，圍陳倉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, they besieged Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhongping they laid siege to Chencang.

sentences.zh: 乃拜卓前將軍，與左將軍皇甫嵩擊破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhuo was appointed General of the Van and together with General of the Left Huangfu Song smashed them.
translations.idiomatic: The court then named Dong Zhuo general of the van and, with General of the Left Huangfu Song, broke the rebel ring around the city.

sentences.zh: 韓遂等復共廢王國，而劫故信都令漢陽閻忠，

translations.literal: Han Sui and others again jointly deposed Wang Guo and coerced the former magistrate of Xindu Yan Zhong of Hanyang,
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui and his allies then deposed Wang Guo and seized Yan Zhong—a former magistrate of Xindu in Hanyang—to force him into their ranks,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：「王國等起兵，劫忠為主，統三十六部，號『車騎將軍』。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong ji states: "Wang Guo and others raised troops, coerced Zhong to be lord, commanded thirty-six divisions, and styled themselves 'Chariots and Cavalry General'."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong ji records that when Wang Guo's coalition first rose, they kidnapped Yan Zhong as figurehead, united thirty-six bands under one banner, and gave their leader the title chariots-and-cavalry general.〉

sentences.zh: 使督統諸部。

translations.literal: And made him supervise and command the various divisions.
translations.idiomatic: They compelled him to take overall command of the allied hosts.

sentences.zh: 忠恥為眾所脅，感恚病死。

translations.literal: Zhong was ashamed at being coerced by the host, felt resentment, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified at serving as a puppet, Yan Zhong sank into resentment, took sick, and died.

sentences.zh: 遂等稍爭權利，更相殺害，其諸部曲並各分乖。

translations.literal: Sui and others gradually contended for power and profit, mutually killed one another, and their various units each split apart in discord.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui's confederates soon quarreled over spoils and precedence, turned their blades on one another, and the coalition splintered into feuding bands.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵卓為少府，不肯就，上書言：「所將湟中義從及秦胡兵皆詣臣曰：『牢直不畢，稟賜斷絕，

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zhuo was summoned to be Minister of the Treasury; he was unwilling to take office and submitted a memorial stating: "The volunteer followers from the Huang region and the Qin and Hu troops whom I lead all came to me saying: 'The full ration pay is not completed, the grain allowances are cut off,'"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhongping the court summoned Dong Zhuo to the post of minister of the treasury. He refused the appointment and sent up a memorial in which he quoted his frontier troops—the Huang River volunteers and the mixed Qin and Hu soldiers—as complaining that their stipends were unpaid and their grain rations had stopped.

sentences.zh: 〈《前書音義》曰：「牢，稟食也。

translations.literal: 〈The Former Documents Sound and Meaning states: "Lao means grain ration."
translations.idiomatic: A Han shu commentary glosses lao as the soldiers' grain ration.

sentences.zh: 古者名稟為牢。」〉

translations.literal: In antiquity grain was called lao."〉
translations.idiomatic: Classical usage, it adds, often called issued grain lao.〉

sentences.zh: 妻子饑凍。

translations.literal: Wives and children are hungry and freezing.
translations.idiomatic: Their wives and children are starving and cold.

sentences.zh: 』牽挽臣車，使不得行。

translations.literal: ' They drag and pull my carriage so I cannot proceed.
translations.idiomatic: They have seized my carriage and will not let me move.

sentences.zh: 羌胡敝腸狗態，

translations.literal: The Qiang and Hu have rotten bowels and dog-like dispositions,
translations.idiomatic: These Qiang and Hu allies are coarse and fickle as curs,

sentences.zh: 〈言羌胡心腸敝惡，情態如狗也。

translations.literal: 〈It means the Qiang and Hu have rotten-evil hearts and intestines, and dispositions like dogs.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator explains that the phrase paints their hearts as corrupt and their temperaments as brutish as dogs'.

sentences.zh: 《續漢書》「敝」作「憋」。

translations.literal: The Continued Han Documents writes the character bie in place of bi.
translations.idiomatic: The Xù Han shu substitutes the graph bie (meaning surly, pent-up) for bi (worn, base) in this line.

sentences.zh: 《方言》云：「憋，惡也。

translations.literal: The Fangyan states: "Bi means evil."
translations.idiomatic: The Fangyan defines bi as "vicious" or "ill-natured."

sentences.zh: 」郭璞曰：「憋怤，急性也。

translations.literal: " Guo Pu states: "Bi-fu means acute temperament."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu glosses the compound as describing a hot-tempered disposition.

sentences.zh: 」憋音芳烈反，怤音芳于反。〉

translations.literal: " Bi is read fanglie fan; fu is read fangyu fan."〉
translations.idiomatic: The text supplies fanqie spellings for both syllables.〉

sentences.zh: 臣不能禁止，輒將順安慰。

translations.literal: Your subject cannot prohibit them; I have only led and consoled them in compliance.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot restrain them by force; I have done no more than humor them and try to calm the uproar.

sentences.zh: 增異復上。」

translations.literal: If they increase in different intent, I shall again report upward."
translations.idiomatic: Should their mood worsen, I will memorialize again without delay."

sentences.zh: 〈如其更增異志，當復聞上。〉

translations.literal: 〈If they further increase in different intent, he ought again to be heard above.〉
translations.idiomatic: The gloss clarifies that Dong Zhuo promises further memorials if the soldiers' disaffection deepens.〉

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能制，頗以為慮。

translations.literal: The court could not control him and was rather anxious about it.
translations.idiomatic: The court had no means to compel him and grew distinctly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 及靈帝寑疾，璽書拜卓為并州牧，令以兵屬皇甫嵩。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling lay gravely ill, an edict on imperial jade appointed Zhuo Governor of Bing province and ordered him to attach his troops to Huangfu Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ling took to his deathbed, an imperial rescript named Dong Zhuo governor of Bing province and instructed him to place his army under Huangfu Song's command.

sentences.zh: 卓復上書言曰：「臣既無老謀，又無壯事，天恩誤加，掌戎十年。

translations.literal: Zhuo again submitted a memorial stating: "Your subject has neither aged stratagems nor youthful deeds; Heaven's grace was mistakenly applied, and I have held the army for ten years."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo answered with another memorial: "I possess neither the cunning of age nor the vigor of youth, yet Heaven's favor misled you into leaving me at arms for a full decade."

sentences.zh: 士卒大小相狎彌久，戀臣畜養之恩，為臣奮一旦之命。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers, great and small, have been intimate with one another a long time; they cling to your subject's grace of nurturing and raising them, and for your subject they will exert a single morning's life.
translations.idiomatic: My officers and men have lived cheek by jowl so long that they cling to the kindness I have shown them in camp; they would lay down their lives for me in an instant.

sentences.zh: 乞將之北州，效力邊垂。

translations.literal: I beg to lead them to the northern province and exert strength on the border marches.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to march them north and spend what strength we have on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」於是駐兵河東，以觀時變。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he stationed troops in Hedong to observe the changes of the times.
translations.idiomatic: With that excuse he halted his host in Hedong and waited to see how events at court would unfold.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，大將軍何進、司隸校尉袁紹謀誅閹宦，而太后不許，乃私呼卓將兵入朝，以脅太后。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Grand General He Jin and Colonel Director of Retainers Yuan Shao plotted to execute the eunuch officials, but the empress dowager did not permit it; thereupon they privately summoned Zhuo to lead troops into court to coerce the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ling's death, General-in-chief He Jin and Colonel of the Metropolitan Region Yuan Shao plotted to exterminate the palace eunuchs. The empress dowager refused, so He Jin secretly summoned Dong Zhuo to march on the capital and intimidate her into consenting.

sentences.zh: 卓得召，即時就道。

translations.literal: When Zhuo received the summons, he immediately set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo accepted the call and set out at once.

sentences.zh: 並上書

translations.literal: And together submitted a memorial
translations.idiomatic: At the same time he forwarded a memorial

sentences.zh: 〈並猶兼也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Bing is like jian 'together with'.〉
translations.idiomatic: The particle bing here means "also" or "at the same time."〉

sentences.zh: 曰：「中常侍張讓等竊倖承寵，濁亂海內。

translations.literal: stating: "The palace attendants Zhang Rang and others by stealth and favor receive grace, and foul and disorder all within the seas."
translations.idiomatic: that read: "Attendants-in-ordinary such as Zhang Rang have wormed their way into favor and turned the realm upside down."

sentences.zh: 臣聞揚湯止沸，莫若去薪；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that to ladle soup to stop boiling is not as good as removing the firewood;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that ladling boiling water to cool it avails less than lifting the fuel from the fire;

sentences.zh: 〈前漢枚乘上書曰：「欲湯之滄，一人吹之，百人揚之，無益也。

translations.literal: 〈Former Han Mei Sheng submitted a memorial stating: "Desiring soup to be cold, one person blows it, a hundred persons ladle it—there is no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Mei Sheng of the Western Han once warned that a hundred men skimming the surface cannot cool a cauldron the way one man can by cutting off the heat—

sentences.zh: 不如絕薪止火而已。

translations.literal: It is not as good as cutting off firewood and stopping fire—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: nothing matches simply snuffing the blaze at its source."

sentences.zh: 」滄音測亮反，寒也。〉

translations.literal: " Cang is read celiang fan, meaning cold."〉
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes the rare character for "cold" and gives its fanqie reading.〉

sentences.zh: 潰癕雖痛，勝於內食。

translations.literal: Though bursting an abscess is painful, it is better than inward eating.
translations.idiomatic: Lancing a boil hurts, yet it is kinder than letting the poison eat you from within.

sentences.zh: 昔趙鞅興晉陽之甲，以逐君側之惡人。

translations.literal: In antiquity Zhao Yang raised the armor of Jinyang to expel the evil men at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhao Yang of Jin mobilized the garrison at Jinyang to drive the villains from his lord's flank.

sentences.zh: 〈《公羊傳》曰：「晉趙鞅取晉陽之甲以逐荀寅與士吉射。

translations.literal: 〈The Gongyang Tradition states: "Jin Zhao Yang took the armor of Jinyang to expel Xun Yin and Shi Jishe."
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang commentary recounts how Zhao Yang of Jin marched the troops of Jinyang against Xun Yin and Shi Jishe—

sentences.zh: 荀寅與士吉射者曷為者也？

translations.literal: As for Xun Yin and Shi Jishe—what sort were they?
translations.idiomatic: Who, the classic asks, were Xun Yin and Shi Jishe?

sentences.zh: 君側之惡人也。

translations.literal: Evil men at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: They were the evil counselors at the ruler's elbow.

sentences.zh: 此逐君側之惡人，曷為以叛言之？

translations.literal: This expelling evil men at the ruler's side—why is it spoken of in terms of rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao Yang was only purging his prince's enemies, why does the text call it rebellion?

sentences.zh: 無君命也。」〉

translations.literal: There was no ruler's command."〉
translations.idiomatic: Because he acted without a royal mandate."〉

sentences.zh: 今臣輒鳴鐘鼓如洛陽，

translations.literal: Now your subject rashly sounds bells and drums proceeding to Luoyang,
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I am beating drums and sounding bells as I advance on Luoyang—

sentences.zh: 〈鳴鍾鼓者，聲其罪也。

translations.literal: 〈To sound bells and drums is to proclaim their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual of bells and drums proclaims the culprits' guilt in public.

sentences.zh: 論語曰：「小子鳴鼓而攻之。

translations.literal: The Analects states: "Little ones, sound the drum and attack them."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius told his disciples to "beat the drum and assail" a man who had lost the Way—

sentences.zh: 」《典略》載卓表曰：「張讓等慆慢天常，擅操王命，父子兄弟並據州郡，一書出門，高獲千金，下數百萬膏腴美田，皆屬讓等。

translations.literal: " The Dianlüe records Zhuo's memorial stating: "Zhang Rang and others are dissolute and scornful of Heaven's constants, usurp and manipulate the kingly commands; fathers and sons and brothers together occupy provinces and commanderies; a single letter out the gate—at the top they obtain a thousand in gold, below millions; fertile beautiful fields all belong to Rang and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe preserves a longer version of Dong Zhuo's memorial accusing Zhang Rang of trampling natural order, hijacking imperial authority, planting kinsmen in every province, selling offices for fortunes large and small, and seizing the empire's richest farmland for himself and his clan.

sentences.zh: 使變氣上蒸，妖賊蜂起。」〉

translations.literal: They cause aberrant vapors to steam upward, and prodigious bandits swarm and arise."〉
translations.idiomatic: Their corruption rises like steam into Heaven itself, and omens of rebellion swarm like wasps."〉

sentences.zh: 請收讓等，以清姦穢。

translations.literal: I request to seize Rang and others, in order to clear away treacherous filth.
translations.idiomatic: I ask permission to arrest Zhang Rang and his confederates and scour this filth from the court."

sentences.zh: 」卓未至而何進敗，虎賁中郎將袁術乃燒南宮，欲討宦官，而中常侍段珪等

translations.literal: " Before Zhuo arrived, He Jin was defeated; Colonel of the Rapid as Tigers Yuan Shu thereupon burned the Southern Palace, intending to attack the eunuch officials, but the palace attendants Duan Gui and others
translations.idiomatic: Before Dong Zhuo reached the capital, He Jin fell in a coup. Colonel Yuan Shu set fire to the Southern Palace in a bid to flush out the eunuchs, who—led by the attendant Duan Gui—

sentences.zh: 〈《山陽公載記》「段」字作「殷」。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Annals of the Duke of Shanyang writes the character for Duan as Yin.〉
translations.idiomatic: One variant text writes the eunuch's surname as Yin instead of Duan.〉

sentences.zh: 劫少帝及陳留王夜走小平津。

translations.literal: seized the young emperor and the Prince of Chenliu and by night fled to Xiaoping Ford.
translations.idiomatic: abducted the young emperor and the Prince of Chenliu and fled with them by night toward Xiaoping Ford.

sentences.zh: 卓遠見火起，引兵急進，未明到城西，聞少帝在北芒，因往奉迎。

translations.literal: Zhuo from afar saw fires rise, led troops in hasty advance, before dawn arrived west of the city, heard the young emperor was at Beimang, and therefore went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the glow of Yuan Shu's fires from miles away, Dong Zhuo pressed his column forward and reached the west wall of Luoyang before dawn. Learning that the young emperor had fled toward Beimang, he rode out to "rescue" him.

sentences.zh: 帝見卓將兵卒至，恐怖涕泣。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Zhuo's soldiers arrive suddenly, was frightened, wept, and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor burst into frightened tears when Dong Zhuo's armored host suddenly surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：「帝望見卓涕泣，羣公謂卓有詔却兵。

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe states: "The emperor looked and saw Zhuo and wept; the host of nobles said Zhuo had an edict to withdraw troops."
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe adds that the courtiers, seeing the emperor weep at the sight of Dong Zhuo, assumed an edict had ordered the warlord to halt—

sentences.zh: 卓曰：『公諸人為國大臣，不能匡正王室，至使國家播蕩，何却兵之有？

translations.literal: Zhuo said: 'You gentlemen are great ministers for the state, yet could not rectify and correct the royal house, to the extent of causing the state to be shaken and tossed—what withdrawal of troops is there?'
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo retorted, 'You call yourselves pillars of the state, yet you let the house of Han come to this pass—what business have you asking me to turn back?'

sentences.zh: 』遂俱入城。」〉

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they all entered the city together."〉
translations.idiomatic: With that he escorted the whole party through the gates into Luoyang."〉

sentences.zh: 卓與言，不能辭對；

translations.literal: Zhuo spoke with him; he could not reply with words;
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo questioned him, the emperor was too terrified to string a sentence together;

sentences.zh: 與陳留王語，遂及禍亂之事。

translations.literal: speaking with the Prince of Chenliu, they then reached matters of disaster and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: yet with the Prince of Chenliu he could hold a coherent conversation about the crisis that had engulfed the capital.

sentences.zh: 卓以王為賢，且為董太后所養，卓自以與太后同族，有廢立意。

translations.literal: Zhuo considered the prince worthy, and moreover he had been reared by Empress Dowager Dong; Zhuo himself thought he was of the same clan as the empress dowager, and had the intent to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo decided the prince was the abler of the two boys, remembered that Empress Dowager Dong had raised him, and—fancying himself kin to that same Dong clan—began to contemplate deposing one brother in favor of the other.

sentences.zh: 卓遷太尉，領前將軍事，加節傳斧鉞虎賁，更封郿侯。

translations.literal: Zhuo was promoted to Grand Commandant, concurrently held the affairs of General of the Van, was granted credentials, tally, axe and halberd, and Rapid as Tigers, and was further enfeoffed as Marquis of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to grand commandant with continuing command of the van, invested with the full insignia of a frontier marshal—imperial tally, ceremonial axe, and an imperial guard of picked champions—and enfeoffed afresh as marquis of Mei.

sentences.zh: 〈傳音陟戀反。

translations.literal: 〈Chuan is read zhilian fan.
translations.idiomatic: The tally (chuan) is glossed with the fanqie spelling zhilian.

sentences.zh: 郿，今岐州縣。〉

translations.literal: Mei is now a county of Qi prefecture."〉
translations.idiomatic: Mei corresponds to a county in modern Qizhou.〉

sentences.zh: 卓乃與司徒黃琬、司空楊彪，俱帶鈇鑕詣闕上書，追理陳蕃、竇武及諸黨人，以從人望。

translations.literal: Zhuo then together with Minister of Education Huang Wan and Minister of Works Yang Biao, all wearing axes and executioner's blocks, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, retrospectively vindicating Chen Fan, Dou Wu, and the various faction men, in order to comply with people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Next Dong Zhuo marched to the palace gates with Ministers Huang Wan and Yang Biao, all three wearing the ceremonial axe and manacles of a man offering his life for his plea. They demanded posthumous justice for Chen Fan, Dou Wu, and the victims of the partisan proscriptions, winning an instant surge of popular approval.

sentences.zh: 於是悉復蕃等爵位，擢用子孫。

translations.literal: Thereupon all restored Fan and others' noble ranks and promoted and employed sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored their titles, recalled their exiled kin, and appointed their descendants to office.

sentences.zh: 尋進卓為相國，入朝不趨，劔履上殿。

translations.literal: Soon Zhuo was advanced to Chancellor of State, entering court without hastening, sword and shoes on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named chancellor of state with the old tyrants' privileges: he might enter the throne hall without quickening his step, wearing sword and shoes.

sentences.zh: 封母為池陽君，置丞令。

translations.literal: His mother was enfeoffed as Lady of Chiyang, and chancellors and magistrates were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: His mother received the title lady of Chiyang, complete with her own household staff of chancellor and county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 是時洛中貴戚室第相望，金帛財產，家家殷積。

translations.literal: At this time in Luoyang noble relatives' mansions looked upon one another, gold, silk, and property—every household was abundantly piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's great families lived in mansions that crowded one another along every boulevard, each vault overflowing with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 卓縱放兵士，突其廬舍，淫略婦女，剽虜資物，謂之「搜牢」。

translations.literal: Zhuo unleashed soldiers, burst into their huts and houses, violated and seized women, plundered and captured goods, calling it "search the stronghold."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo gave his troops free rein to smash into those houses, rape the women, and cart off valuables in raids they cynically nicknamed "searching the stronghold."

sentences.zh: 〈言牢固者皆搜索取之也。

translations.literal: 〈It means whatever is firm and strong, all are searched and taken.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase implies looting every household that still had anything left worth taking.

sentences.zh: 一曰牢，漉也。

translations.literal: One explanation: lao means to strain.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss derives lao from "to strain" or "to sieve," as if wringing the city dry.

sentences.zh: 二字皆從去聲，今俗有此言。〉

translations.literal: Both graphs are read in the departing tone; vulgar speech today still has this saying.〉
translations.idiomatic: Both words are read in the fourth tone; the expression survives in colloquial speech even now.〉

sentences.zh: 人情崩恐，不保朝夕。

translations.literal: Human feelings collapsed in terror; they could not secure morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Terror unmanned the populace; families no longer counted on living from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 及何后葬，開文陵，

translations.literal: When Empress He was buried, they opened the Wenling mausoleum,
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager He was laid to rest, the workmen broke open Emperor Ling's mausoleum, the Wen tumulus,

sentences.zh: 〈靈帝陵。〉

translations.literal: 〈Emperor Ling's tomb.〉
translations.idiomatic: that is, Emperor Ling's burial mound.〉

sentences.zh: 卓悉取藏中珍物。

translations.literal: Zhuo entirely took the precious objects in the vaults.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo looted every treasure cached inside.

sentences.zh: 又姦亂公主，妻略宮人，虐刑濫罰，睚眦必死，群僚內外莫能自固。

translations.literal: Moreover he debauched princesses, seized palace women as wives, cruel punishments and excessive penalties—at a sidelong glance one was sure to die; hosts of officials within and without none could secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He raped imperial princesses, carried off palace ladies as concubines, and ruled by torture and whim: a single hard look could mean death. High and low, inside the court and out, no one could feel safe in his own skin.

sentences.zh: 卓嘗遣軍至陽城，時人會於社下，悉令就斬之，駕其車重，載其婦女，以頭系車轅，歌呼而還。

translations.literal: Zhuo once dispatched troops to Yangcheng; at the time people were assembled below the altars of the soil god; he entirely ordered them to go and behead them, drove their carts and baggage, loaded their women, tied heads to cart yokes, and singing and shouting returned.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent soldiers to Yangcheng, where villagers had gathered for the spring sacrifice at the earth god's shrine. His men cut every celebrant down, piled the dead onto captured wagons, heaped the women aboard, and tied severed heads to the axles while they sang their way back to camp.

sentences.zh: 又壞五銖錢，更鑄小錢，悉取洛陽及長安銅人、鐘虡、飛廉、銅馬之屬，以充鑄焉。

translations.literal: Moreover he destroyed the five-zhu cash, recast small coins, entirely took the bronze men of Luoyang and Chang'an, bell-stands, Flying-Lian, bronze horses, and the like, to supply casting.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the old five-zhu coinage and ordered tiny, debased cash struck instead, melting down the great bronze statues, bell racks, Flying-Lian spirits, and bronze horses of both capitals to feed the furnaces.

sentences.zh: 〈鍾虡以銅為之，故賈山上書云「懸石鑄鍾虡」。

translations.literal: 〈Bell-stands are made of bronze; therefore Jia Shan in his memorial said "suspend stones and cast bell-stands."
translations.idiomatic: The bell racks were cast in bronze—hence Jia Shan's memorial spoke of "hanging stone" and "casting bell-stands."

sentences.zh: 前書《音義》曰：「虡，鹿頭龍身，神獸也。

translations.literal: The Former Documents Sound and Meaning states: "The ju is deer-head dragon-body, a divine beast."
translations.idiomatic: A Han shu commentary describes the ju stand as a mythical creature with a deer's head and dragon's body.

sentences.zh: 」《說文》：「鍾鼓之跗，以猛獸為飾也。

translations.literal: " The Shuowen: "The bases of bells and drums, using fierce beasts as ornament."
translations.idiomatic: The Shuowen defines them as the pedestals of bells and drums, ornamented with savage beasts.

sentences.zh: 」武帝置飛廉館。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu established the Flying-Lian lodge."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had built a hall named for the Flying-Lian spirit.

sentences.zh: 《音義》云：「飛廉，神禽，身似鹿，頭如爵，有角，蛇尾，文如豹文。

translations.literal: The Sound and Meaning states: "Flying-Lian is a divine bird; its body resembles a deer, its head like a finch, it has horns, snake tail, markings like leopard markings."
translations.idiomatic: Commentaries picture Flying-Lian as a sacred bird—deer-like body, finch-like head, horned, serpent-tailed, dappled like a leopard.

sentences.zh: 」明帝永平五年，長安迎取飛廉及銅馬置上西門外，名平樂館。

translations.literal: " In Emperor Ming's fifth Yongping year, Chang'an welcomed and took Flying-Lian and the bronze horse and placed them outside the Upper West Gate, naming them the Pingle lodge."
translations.idiomatic: In 62 CE the court moved the Flying-Lian figure and the bronze horses to a site outside Chang'an's Upper West Gate and called the complex the Pingle gallery.

sentences.zh: 銅馬則東門京所作，致於金馬門外者也。

translations.literal: The bronze horses were what Dongmen Jing made, brought and placed outside the Golden Horse Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The bronze horses were the work of the craftsman Dongmen Jing, set long ago outside the Golden Horse Gate.

sentences.zh: 張璠《紀》曰：「太史靈臺及永安候銅蘭楯，卓亦取之。」〉

translations.literal: Zhang Fan's Annals states: "The Grand Clerk's spirit terrace and the bronze orchid shields of Yong'an Marquis—Zhuo also took them."〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's chronicle adds that Dong Zhuo even stripped the observatory's spirit terrace and the bronze "orchid" shields from Yong'an's watchtowers.〉

sentences.zh: 故貨賤物貴，穀石數萬。

translations.literal: Therefore goods were cheap and commodities dear; grain per shi was several myriads.
translations.idiomatic: Money became worthless while grain soared to tens of thousands of cash a bushel.

sentences.zh: 又錢無輪郭文章，不便人用。

translations.literal: Moreover the coins lacked rims and inscriptions and patterns, inconvenient for people to use.
translations.idiomatic: The new coins lacked raised rims and legible inscriptions, so they were clumsy in trade.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰：「卓鑄小錢，大五分，無文章，肉好無輪郭，不磨鑢。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states: "Zhuo cast small coins, large as five fen, without inscriptions, flesh and hole without rim, not polished."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wei zhi notes that Dong Zhuo's tokens were barely five fen across, blank on both faces, without the usual rim or milling.〉

sentences.zh: 時人以為秦始皇見長人於臨洮，乃鑄銅人。

translations.literal: People of the time thought that Qin Shihuang saw a tall man at Lintao, thereupon cast bronze men.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries remembered how the First Emperor, after sighting giants at Lintao, had ordered the twelve bronze giants cast—and shuddered.

sentences.zh: 〈《三輔舊事》曰：「秦王立二十六年，初定天下，稱皇帝。

translations.literal: 〈The Old Matters of the Three Adjuncts states: "The King of Qin, having established twenty-six years, first settled all under Heaven, styled himself emperor."
translations.idiomatic: The Sanfu jiushi recalls that in the twenty-sixth year of his reign the King of Qin unified the realm and took the title emperor—

sentences.zh: 大人見臨洮，身長五丈，跡長六尺，作銅人以厭之，立在阿房殿前。

translations.literal: A great man appeared at Lintao, body five zhang in height, footprints six chi long; he made bronze men to suppress them, standing in front of the Epang hall.
translations.idiomatic: when a giant appeared at Lintao—five zhang tall, leaving six-chi footprints—he cast bronze colossi to lay the omen and set them before Epang Palace.

sentences.zh: 漢徙長樂宮中大夏殿前。

translations.literal: Han moved them before the Great Summer hall in the Eternal Joy palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Han later moved the statues to the Great Summer Hall in the Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 」史記曰：「始皇鑄天下兵器為十二金人。」〉

translations.literal: " The Records of the Historian states: "The First Emperor cast the weapons of all under Heaven into twelve metal men."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Shiji famously says he melted down every weapon in the empire to forge twelve golden giants."〉

sentences.zh: 卓，臨洮人也，而今毀之。

translations.literal: Zhuo was a man of Lintao, yet now destroys them.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo himself was a son of Lintao; now he was tearing down what the First Emperor had raised.

sentences.zh: 雖成毀不同，凶暴相類焉。

translations.literal: Although completion and destruction differ, ferocious cruelty was alike.
translations.idiomatic: Different though their ends were, the two men matched each other in savagery.

sentences.zh: 初，靈帝末，黃巾餘黨郭太等復起西河白波谷，轉寇太原，遂破河東，百姓流轉三輔，號為「白波賊」，眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning, at the end of Emperor Ling, Yellow Turban remnant party Guo Tai and others again rose in the Baibo valley of Xihe, turned to raid Taiyuan, thereupon broke Hedong, common people drifted and circulated in the Three Adjuncts, styled "Baibo bandits," hosts of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Ling's reign the Yellow Turban holdout Guo Tai (written Tai in some texts) rallied the "White Wave" rebels in the Baibo ravines of Xihe. They swept through Taiyuan, overran Hedong, and drove refugees by the tens of thousands into the capital region, where the band came to be known as the White Wave army—more than a hundred thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 卓遣中郎將牛輔擊之，不能却。

translations.literal: Zhuo sent General of the Gentlemen of the Household Niu Fu to strike them; he could not repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent General Niu Fu against them, but Fu could not drive them back.

sentences.zh: 及聞東方兵起，懼，乃鴆殺弘農王，欲徙都長安。

translations.literal: When he heard eastern troops had risen, he was afraid, thereupon poison-killed the Prince of Hongnong, and wished to move the capital to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that eastern coalition armies were on the march, panic seized him: he had the deposed emperor—the Prince of Hongnong—put to death with poisoned wine and resolved to move the court west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 會公卿議，太尉黃琬﹑司徒楊彪廷爭不能得，而伍瓊﹑周珌又固諫之。

translations.literal: He convened the dukes and ministers to deliberate; Grand Commandant Huang Wan and Minister of Education Yang Biao disputed in court but could not prevail, while Wu Qiong and Zhou Bi again firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the high ministers to endorse the move. Grand Commandant Huang Wan and Minister Yang Biao argued themselves hoarse in open court, while Wu Qiong and Zhou Bi pleaded with equal stubbornness—all to no avail.

sentences.zh: 卓因大怒曰：「卓初入朝，二子勸用善士，故相從，而諸君到官，舉兵相圖。

translations.literal: Zhuo thereupon greatly angered said: "When Zhuo first entered court, you two urged employing good gentlemen; therefore I followed you, yet you gentlemen having reached office, raised troops and plotted against one another."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo exploded: "When I first came to Luoyang, you two urged me to appoint worthy men, and I listened. Yet the moment you took your posts you raised armies against one another!"

sentences.zh: 此二君賣卓，卓何用相負！

translations.literal: These two lords have sold Zhuo—what use has Zhuo for betraying them!
translations.idiomatic: Those two have sold me out—why should I owe them any loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 」遂斬瓊﹑珌。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beheaded Qiong and Bi.
translations.idiomatic: With that he had Wu Qiong and Zhou Bi executed.

sentences.zh: 而彪﹑琬恐懼，詣卓謝曰：「小人戀舊，非欲沮國事也，請以不及為罪。

translations.literal: But Biao and Wan in fear went to Zhuo and apologized saying: "We petty men cling to the old, not wishing to obstruct state affairs; we request to take 'not reaching' as crime."
translations.idiomatic: Shaking with terror, Yang Biao and Huang Wan went to Dong Zhuo to apologize: "We are small men, attached to the old capital; we never meant to block state policy. Punish us for our shortsightedness."

sentences.zh: 」卓既殺瓊﹑珌，旋亦悔之，故表彪﹑琬為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " Zhuo, having already killed Qiong and Bi, soon also regretted it, therefore memorialized Biao and Wan as Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Almost as soon as the heads fell, regret set in; he memorialized both survivors as grand masters of splendid happiness to smooth things over."

sentences.zh: 於是遷天子西都。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved the Son of Heaven to the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then bundled off to the western capital.

sentences.zh: 初，長安遭赤眉之亂，宮室營寺焚滅無餘，是時唯有高廟﹑京兆府舍，遂便時幸焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Chang'an had suffered the Red Eyebrows' disorder; palaces, barracks, and temples were burned and extinguished without remainder; at this time there were only the High Temple and the Jingzhao government offices; thereupon they then for the time favored there.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an had been gutted generations earlier by the Red Eyebrows: almost every palace and monastery lay in ashes. Only the dynastic High Temple and the Jingzhao governor's compound still stood, so the court provisionally lodged the emperor there.

sentences.zh: 〈便時謂時日吉便。〉

translations.literal: 〈Bianshi means the time and day were auspiciously convenient.〉
translations.idiomatic: The phrase means they chose an auspicious day for the move.〉

sentences.zh: 後移未央宮。

translations.literal: Later they moved to the Weiyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court shifted into the Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 於是盡徙洛陽人數百萬口於長安，步騎驅蹙，更相蹈藉，飢餓寇掠，積尸盈路。

translations.literal: Thereupon they entirely moved the people of Luoyang, several million mouths, to Chang'an; infantry and cavalry drove and pressed them; mutually they trampled one another; hunger and banditry piled corpses filling the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Several million Luoyang residents were herded west at spearpoint. Cavalry rode down anyone who faltered; the dying trampled the dead; famine and roadside banditry left corpses stacked along every highway.

sentences.zh: 卓自屯留畢圭苑中，悉燒宮廟官府居家，二百里內無復孑遺。

translations.literal: Zhuo himself encamped and stayed in the Bigui imperial park, entirely burned palaces, temples, government offices, and dwellings; within two hundred li none survived.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo made his headquarters in the Bigui hunting park outside Luoyang while his men torched every palace, shrine, yamen, and private house for two hundred li around, leaving not a roof standing.

sentences.zh: 又使呂布發諸帝陵，及公卿已下冢墓，收其珍寶。

translations.literal: Moreover he ordered Lü Bu to open the various imperial mausolea, and from dukes and ministers downward tombs, collecting their precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lü Bu to rifle the imperial tombs and, descending rank by rank through the nobility, every family vault, stripping gold and jade from the dead.

sentences.zh: 時長沙太守孫堅亦率豫州諸郡兵討卓。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Administrator of Changsha Sun Jian also led the troops of the various commanderies of Yu province to attack Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Sun Jian, the grand administrator of Changsha, marched the allied forces of Yu province east against Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓先遣將徐榮、李蒙四出虜掠。

translations.literal: Zhuo first dispatched generals Xu Rong and Li Meng on four sides to capture and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo had already sent Xu Rong and Li Meng on wide-ranging raids.

sentences.zh: 榮遇堅於梁，

translations.literal: Rong encountered Jian at Liang,
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rong intercepted Sun Jian at Liang—

sentences.zh: 〈故城在今汝州梁縣西南。〉

translations.literal: 〈The old walled city is now southwest of Liang county in Ru prefecture.〉
translations.idiomatic: the old town southwest of present-day Liang County in Ruzhou.〉

sentences.zh: 與戰，破堅，生禽穎川太守李旻，亨之。

translations.literal: fought with him, defeated Jian, alive captured Grand Administrator of Yingchuan Li Min, and boiled him.
translations.idiomatic: defeated him in battle, took Grand Administrator Li Min of Yingchuan alive, and boiled him alive.

sentences.zh: 卓所得義兵士卒，皆以布纏裹，倒立於地，熱膏灌殺之。

translations.literal: Righteous-army soldiers whom Zhuo captured were all wrapped in cloth, hung upside down on the ground, and scalding grease poured to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Coalition prisoners were swathed in cloth, strung head-down from frames, and killed by pouring boiling oil over them.

sentences.zh: 時河內太守王匡

translations.literal: At the time Grand Administrator of Henei Wang Kuang
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Kuang, the grand administrator of Henei,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：「匡字公節，泰山人。

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong ji states: "Kuang, courtesy name Gongjie, was a man of Taishan."
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong ji gives his style as Gongjie and his home as Taishan—

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，以任俠聞。」〉

translations.literal: He was light with wealth and fond of giving, and by knight-errantry was heard of."〉
translations.idiomatic: a man who scattered his fortune in charity and was known as a chivalrous adventurer."〉

sentences.zh: 屯兵河陽津，將以圖卓。

translations.literal: encamped troops at Heyang ford, intending thereby to plot against Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: had camped his army at the Heyang crossing, intending to strike at Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓遣疑兵挑戰，而潛使銳卒從小平津過津北，破之，死者略盡。

translations.literal: Zhuo sent decoy troops to challenge, while secretly ordering picked soldiers from Xiaoping ford to cross north of the ford, defeated them, and the dead were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo offered a feint to draw their fire, then slipped crack troops across the Yellow River at Xiaoping Ford, fell on Wang Kuang from the rear, and slaughtered his army almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 明年，孫堅收合散卒，進屯梁縣之陽人。

translations.literal: The next year, Sun Jian gathered and united scattered troops, advanced and encamped at Yangren in Liang county.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sun Jian rallied his broken units and advanced to Yangren in Liang County.

sentences.zh: 〈梁縣屬河南郡，今汝州縣也。

translations.literal: 〈Liang county belonged to Henan commandery; it is now a county of Ru prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang County lay in Henan commandery—present-day Ruzhou—

sentences.zh: 陽人，聚，故城在梁縣西。〉

translations.literal: Yangren is a settlement; the old walled city is west of Liang county.〉
translations.idiomatic: while Yangren was a hamlet whose old walls stood west of the county seat.〉

sentences.zh: 卓遣將胡軫、呂布攻之，布與軫不相能，軍中自驚恐，士卒散亂。

translations.literal: Zhuo sent generals Hu Zhen and Lü Bu to attack them; Bu and Zhen were not mutually capable; within the army there was self-panic and terror, soldiers scattered in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo dispatched Hu Zhen and Lü Bu against him, but the two generals despised each other; their camps panicked without cause and the assault dissolved in confusion.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：「卓以東郡太守胡軫為大督，呂布為騎督。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiuzhou chunqiu states: "Zhuo made Grand Administrator of Dong commandery Hu Zhen grand marshal and Lü Bu cavalry marshal."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiuzhou chunqiu explains that Dong Zhuo named Hu Zhen, the grand administrator of Dong commandery, overall commander and Lü Bu chief of cavalry—

sentences.zh: 軫性急，豫宣言『今此行也，要當斬一青綬，乃整齊耳』。

translations.literal: Zhen's nature was hasty; he beforehand declared 'On this expedition, I must behead one green-ribbon man, then there will be order.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhen, a hothead, had boasted publicly, "On this march I mean to take the head of at least one man with the green ribbon of a full two-thousand-dan official—that will restore discipline."

sentences.zh: 布等惡之，宣言相警云『賊至』，軍衆大亂奔走。」〉

translations.literal: Bu and others hated him, declared warnings to each other saying 'Bandits have come,' and the army hosts in great disorder fled."〉
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu and his officers, taking the remark as a threat against themselves, spread a false alarm of "enemy attack" and stampeded their own men in the night."〉

sentences.zh: 堅追擊之，軫、布敗走。

translations.literal: Jian pursued and struck them; Zhen and Bu were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian pursued and routed them; Hu Zhen and Lü Bu fled the field.

sentences.zh: 卓遣將李傕詣堅求和，堅拒絕不受，進軍大谷，距洛九十里。

translations.literal: Zhuo sent general Li Jue to Jian to seek peace; Jian refused and did not accept, advanced the army to Dagu, ninety li from Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent Li Jue to sue for peace; Sun Jian spurned the offer and marched to Dagu Pass, ninety li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 〈大谷口在故嵩陽西北三十五里，北出對洛陽故城。

translations.literal: 〈The mouth of Great Valley is thirty-five li northwest of old Songyang; northward it faces the old city of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The pass lies thirty-five li northwest of old Songyang and opens north toward ruined Luoyang—

sentences.zh: 張衡《東京賦》云「盟津達其後，大谷通其前」是也。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital states "Meng ford reaches its rear, Great Valley opens its front"—this is it.
translations.idiomatic: as Zhang Heng wrote in his Eastern Capital rhapsody: "Meng Ford at its back, Great Valley before its gates."

sentences.zh: 距，至也。〉

translations.literal: Ju means to arrive.〉
translations.idiomatic: Here ju means "to reach."〉

sentences.zh: 卓自出與堅戰於諸陵墓閒，卓敗走，却屯黽池，聚兵於陝。

translations.literal: Zhuo himself came out and with Jian fought among the various mausolea; Zhuo was defeated and fled, withdrew and encamped at Mianchi, gathered troops at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo rode out to meet Sun Jian among the imperial tombs, was beaten, fell back to Mianchi, and concentrated reinforcements at Shan.

sentences.zh: 堅進洛陽宣陽城門，

translations.literal: Jian advanced to Luoyang's Xuanyang city gate,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian entered Luoyang through the Xuanyang Gate—

sentences.zh: 〈《洛陽記》洛陽城南面有四門，從東第三門。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Luoyang Record: Luoyang's south face has four gates; from the east it is the third gate.〉
translations.idiomatic: the third gate from the east on the city's south wall, according to the Luoyang ji.〉

sentences.zh: 更擊呂布，布復破走。

translations.literal: Further he struck Lü Bu; Bu again was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: turned and struck Lü Bu again, putting him to flight a second time.

sentences.zh: 堅乃埽除宗廟，平塞諸陵，分兵出函谷關，至新安、黽池閒，以𢧵卓後。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon swept the ancestral temples, leveled and blocked the various mausolea, divided troops out Hangu pass, reaching between Xin'an and Miankchi, to cut off Zhuo's rear.
translations.idiomatic: He swept the imperial shrines, secured the tombs, and detached a column through Hangu Pass toward Xin'an and Mianchi to threaten Dong Zhuo's retreat.

sentences.zh: 卓謂長史劉艾曰：「關東諸將數敗矣，無能為也。

translations.literal: Zhuo said to chief clerk Liu Ai: "The eastern-pass generals have repeatedly been defeated; they can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo told his chief clerk Liu Ai, "The lords east of the passes have been whipped again and again; they are spent.

sentences.zh: 唯孫堅小戇，

translations.literal: Only Sun Jian is a little dull-witted,
translations.idiomatic: Only Sun Jian shows a little stubborn fight—

sentences.zh: 〈《說文》曰：「戇，愚也。

translations.literal: 〈The Shuowen states: "Zhuang means foolish."
translations.idiomatic: The Shuowen glosses zhuang as "obtuse" or "pigheaded."

sentences.zh: 」音都降反。〉

translations.literal: " It is read dujiang fan."〉
translations.idiomatic: The commentary gives the fanqie spelling dujiang.〉

sentences.zh: 諸將軍宜慎之。

translations.literal: The various generals ought to be careful of him.
translations.idiomatic: Tell every general to watch him closely."

sentences.zh: 」乃使東中郎將董越屯黽池，中郎將段煨屯華陰，

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the East Dong Yue to encamp at Miankchi, General of the Gentlemen of the Household Duan Wei to encamp at Huayin,
translations.idiomatic: He then posted General Dong Yue at Mianchi, General Duan Wei at Huayin,

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：「煨在華陰，特修農事。

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe states: "Wei at Huayin especially cultivated agricultural affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe notes that Duan Wei made Huayin a model of orderly farming—

sentences.zh: 天子東遷，煨迎，貢饋周急。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven moved east, Wei welcomed him, presented tribute and gifts, and relieved urgency.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor fled eastward, Wei met him with supplies and emergency rations.

sentences.zh: 」《魏志》曰：「武威人也。

translations.literal: " The Wei Records states: "He was a man of Wuwei."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei zhi identifies him as a native of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 」煨音壹回反。〉

translations.literal: " Wei is read yihui fan."〉
translations.idiomatic: The name Wei is spelled with the fanqie yihui.〉

sentences.zh: 中郎將牛輔屯安邑，其餘中郎將、校尉布在諸縣，以禦山東。

translations.literal: General of the Gentlemen of the Household Niu Fu encamped at Anyi; the remaining generals of the gentlemen of the household and colonels were spread through the various counties, to ward off Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: stationed Niu Fu at Anyi, and scattered other household generals and colonels through the counties to block any thrust from the east.

sentences.zh: 卓諷朝廷使光祿勳宣璠

translations.literal: Zhuo indirectly prompted the court to have Superintendent of the Household Xuan Fan
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo then manipulated the court into dispatching Superintendent of the Household Xuan Fan

sentences.zh: 〈璠音煩，又音甫袁反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Fan is read fan, also read fuyuan fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The graph Fan is glossed fan or fuyuan in fanqie.〉

sentences.zh: 持節拜卓為太師，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: bearing credentials invest Zhuo as Grand Tutor, rank above the feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: with credentials to invest him as grand tutor, a title that outranked every prince of the blood.

sentences.zh: 乃引還長安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thus bolstered, he withdrew to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 百官迎路拜揖，卓遂僭擬車服，乘金華青蓋，爪畫兩轓，時人號「竿摩車」，言其服飾近天子也。

translations.literal: The hundred officials on the road bowed in greeting; Zhuo thereupon presumptuously imitated carriage and apparel, rode gold-flowered green canopy, claw-painted two chariot-side boards; people of the time called it "pole-rubbing carriage," meaning his clothing and adornments neared the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The whole bureaucracy lined the road in obeisance as Dong Zhuo rolled west in regalia fit for an emperor: gilt lotus motifs on a green silk canopy, taloned dragons painted on both chariot rails. Onlookers jeered that he rode a "canopy-scraping carriage," so close had his trappings crept to the Son of Heaven's own.

sentences.zh: 〈金華，以金為華飾車也。

translations.literal: 〈Gold flower means using gold as flowery ornament on the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: "Gold flowers" were gold appliqués on the chariot—

sentences.zh: 爪者，蓋弓頭為爪形也。

translations.literal: Claw means the canopy-rib ends are made claw-shaped.
translations.idiomatic: while "claws" referred to canopy spokes carved like raptor talons.

sentences.zh: 轓音甫袁反。

translations.literal: Fan is read fuyuan fan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan "sideboard" is read fuyuan in fanqie.

sentences.zh: 《廣雅》云：「車箱也。

translations.literal: The Guangya states: "It is the chariot box."
translations.idiomatic: The Guangya defines it as the chariot's side panel.

sentences.zh: 」畫為文彩。

translations.literal: " They were painted as patterned colors.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's were painted with polychrome designs.

sentences.zh: 《續漢志》曰：「轓長六尺，下屈，廣八寸。

translations.literal: The Continued Han Treatise states: "The fan is six chi long, bent downward, eight cun wide."
translations.idiomatic: The Xù Han zhi gives their length as six chi, eight cun wide, curving downward.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「皇太子青蓋金華蚤畫轓。

translations.literal: " It also states: "The heir apparent has green canopy, gold flowers, claw-patterned fan."
translations.idiomatic: The same text reserves green canopy, gold flowers, and claw-patterned sideboards for the crown prince alone.

sentences.zh: 」竿摩謂相逼近也。

translations.literal: " Ganmo means mutually pressing close.
translations.idiomatic: Ganmo "pole rubbing" meant riding so high that one's canopy poles brushed the imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 今俗以事干人者，謂之「相竿摩」。〉

translations.literal: In vulgar speech today, one who by affairs importunes people is called 'mutually pole-rubbing.'"〉
translations.idiomatic: Later slang used the same phrase for anyone who importunes the powerful."〉

sentences.zh: 以弟旻為左將軍，封鄠侯，兄子璜為侍中、中軍校尉，皆典兵事。

translations.literal: He made his younger brother Min General of the Left and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Hu; his elder brother's son Huang was palace attendant and colonel of the central army—all managed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He named his brother Dong Min general of the left and marquis of Hu, his nephew Dong Huang palace attendant and colonel of the central army—every kinsman holding real military power.

sentences.zh: 於是宗族內外，並居列位。

translations.literal: Thereupon clan kin inside and outside together occupied ranked positions.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the palace, the Dong clan monopolized every chair of consequence.

sentences.zh: 其子孫雖在髫齔，男皆封侯，女為邑君。

translations.literal: His sons and grandsons, although in swaddling and cutting teeth, males all were enfeoffed marquises, females became district ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Even infants still in swaddling clothes received marquisates; every girl was made a district lady.

sentences.zh: 數與百官置酒宴會，淫樂縱恣。

translations.literal: Repeatedly with the hundred officials he set wine feasts, wanton music and unrestrained indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he forced the high ministers into debauched banquets of music and excess.

sentences.zh: 乃結壘於長安城東以自居。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built fortifications east of Chang'an city to dwell himself.
translations.idiomatic: East of the capital he threw up a fortified camp where he kept his own headquarters.

sentences.zh: 又築塢於郿，高厚七丈，號曰「萬歲塢」。

translations.literal: Moreover he built a fortified village at Mei, high and thick seven zhang, styled "Long-Life Fort."
translations.idiomatic: Near Mei he raised a private fortress seven zhang high and thick, which he arrogantly named the Fort of Ten Thousand Years.

sentences.zh: 〈今案：塢舊基高一丈，周迴一里一百步。〉

translations.literal: 〈Now investigated: the fort's old base is one zhang high, perimeter one li and a hundred bu.〉
translations.idiomatic: A later survey found the surviving foundation about one zhang high, with a circuit of just over a li.〉

sentences.zh: 積穀為三十年儲。

translations.literal: He piled grain as thirty years' store.
translations.idiomatic: He stockpiled enough grain to feed an army for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 自云：「事成，雄據天下；

translations.literal: He himself said: "If the affair succeeds, I will heroically occupy all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: He boasted, "If fortune favors me, I will rule the realm;

sentences.zh: 不成，守此足以畢老。

translations.literal: if it does not succeed, guarding this is sufficient to finish old age."
translations.idiomatic: if not, this fort alone will let me live out my days."

sentences.zh: 」嘗至郿行塢，公卿已下祖道於橫門外。

translations.literal: " He once went to Mei to inspect the fort; from dukes and ministers downward they performed the road-offering rite outside the Heng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to inspect the Mei fortress, the entire bureaucracy turned out to stage a farewell banquet for him outside the Heng Gate.

sentences.zh: 〈橫音光。〉

translations.literal: 〈Heng is read guang.〉
translations.idiomatic: The gate name is read with the guang pronunciation.〉

sentences.zh: 卓施帳幔飲設，誘降北地反者數百人，於坐中殺之。

translations.literal: Zhuo spread curtains and hangings and drink provisions, lured to surrender several hundred rebels of Beidi, and in the midst of the seating killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Under draped tents he laid a feast, lured several hundred surrendered rebels from Beidi to their seats, then butchered them in cold blood.

sentences.zh: 先斷其舌，次斬手足，次鑿其眼目，以鑊煑之。

translations.literal: First he cut their tongues, next severed hands and feet, next gouged their eyes, and with a cauldron boiled them.
translations.idiomatic: First their tongues were cut out, then their limbs, then their eyes were gouged, and finally they were boiled alive in cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 未及得死，偃轉柸案閒。

translations.literal: Before they could obtain death, they writhed and turned among cups and tables.
translations.idiomatic: Still not dead, they writhed across the banquet tables and cups.

sentences.zh: 會者戰慄，亡失匕箸，而卓飲食自若。

translations.literal: Those at the meeting trembled in battle, lost spoons and chopsticks, yet Zhuo ate and drank as if normal.
translations.idiomatic: The guests shook until spoons and chopsticks clattered to the floor; Dong Zhuo went on eating and drinking as though nothing were amiss.

sentences.zh: 諸將有言語蹉跌，便戮於前。

translations.literal: If generals had slips of speech, he at once executed them before him.
translations.idiomatic: Any general who misspoke in his presence was cut down on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又稍誅關中舊族，陷以叛逆。

translations.literal: Moreover he gradually executed old clans of Guanzhong, trapping them with rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Bit by bit he exterminated the great houses of the Guanzhong heartland on trumped-up charges of treason.

sentences.zh: 時太史望氣，言當有大臣戮死者。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Clerk observed vapors and said there ought to be a great minister killed by execution.
translations.idiomatic: The court astrologers read omens in the clouds and warned that a great minister would die by violence.

sentences.zh: 卓乃使人誣衛尉張溫與袁術交通，遂笞溫於市，殺之，以塞天變。

translations.literal: Zhuo thereupon had people falsely accuse Commandant of the Guards Zhang Wen of communicating with Yuan Shu, thereupon flogged Wen in the market and killed him, to block Heaven's anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo framed Commandant Zhang Wen for colluding with Yuan Shu, had him publicly flogged to death in the marketplace, and called it appeasing Heaven's wrath.

sentences.zh: 前溫出屯美陽，令卓與邊章等戰無功，溫召又不時應命，既到而辭對不遜。

translations.literal: Earlier when Wen went out to encamp at Meiyang, he ordered Zhuo to fight Bian Zhang and others without success; Wen summoned him and he did not timely respond to the command; when he arrived his replies were not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: The grudge was old: at Meiyang Zhang Wen had ordered Dong Zhuo against Bian Zhang's rebels; Zhuo had failed, ignored repeated summons, and when he finally appeared he answered his superior with open insolence.

sentences.zh: 時孫堅為溫參軍，勸溫陳兵斬之。

translations.literal: At the time Sun Jian was Wen's army adviser and urged Wen to deploy troops and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian, then serving as Zhang Wen's adviser, had urged his chief to draw up the army and execute Dong Zhuo for it.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「卓有威名，方倚以西行。

translations.literal: Wen said: "Zhuo has a fearsome name; I am just now relying on him for the western campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen had refused: "Dong Zhuo's name carries weight in the west; I still need him for the campaign."

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「明公親帥王師，威振天下，何恃於卓而賴之乎？

translations.literal: " Jian said: "My lord personally leads the king's army; awe shakes all under Heaven—why depend on Zhuo and rely on him?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian had answered, "You command the imperial host in person and awe the empire—why lean on a man like Dong Zhuo?"

sentences.zh: 堅聞古之名將，杖鉞臨眾，未有不斷斬以示威武者也。

translations.literal: Jian has heard that ancient famous generals, staff and axe in hand facing the host, there were none who did not decisively behead to display martial awe.
translations.idiomatic: The famous generals of old, halberd in hand before the ranks, never hesitated to take a head when discipline required it."

sentences.zh: 故穰苴斬莊賈，

translations.literal: Therefore Rangju beheaded Zhuang Jia,
translations.idiomatic: That is why Tian Rangju executed Zhuang Jia—

sentences.zh: 〈《史記》齊景公時，晉伐阿、鄄而燕侵河上，以司馬穰苴為將軍，使寵臣莊賈監軍。

translations.literal: 〈The Records of the Historian: In Duke Jing of Qi's time, Jin attacked E and Juan while Yan invaded the Yellow River region; he made Sima Rangju general and sent favorite minister Zhuang Jia to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: the Shiji tells how Duke Jing of Qi appointed Sima Rangju general against Jin and Yan and sent the favorite Zhuang Jia to oversee him—

sentences.zh: 賈期後至，穰苴斬以徇三軍，鄄音絹。〉

translations.literal: Jia was late to the rendezvous; Rangju beheaded him to display to the three armies; Juan is read juan."〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Jia arrived late, and Rangju had him executed before the whole army as a warning. (Juan is read juan.)"〉

sentences.zh: 魏絳戮楊干。

translations.literal: Wei Jiang executed Yang Gan.
translations.idiomatic: and why Wei Jiang of Jin slew the charioteer of Prince Yang Gan.

sentences.zh: 〈魏絳，晉大夫。

translations.literal: 〈Wei Jiang was a great officer of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiang was a senior minister of Jin—

sentences.zh: 楊干，晉公弟。

translations.literal: Yang Gan was the younger brother of the Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gan a younger brother of the duke—

sentences.zh: 會諸侯於曲梁，楊干亂行，魏絳戮其僕。

translations.literal: Meeting the feudal lords at Quliang, Yang Gan disordered the ranks; Wei Jiang executed his driver.
translations.idiomatic: who broke formation at the league of Quliang, so Wei Jiang executed his charioteer to restore order.

sentences.zh: 事在《左傳》。〉

translations.literal: The affair is in the Zuo Tradition."〉
translations.idiomatic: The story is in the Zuo zhuan."〉

sentences.zh: 今若縱之，自虧威重，後悔何及！

translations.literal: Now if you indulge him, you yourself injure awesome dignity—what reach will regret have!
translations.idiomatic: Spare him now and you gut your own authority—you will regret it too late!"

sentences.zh: 」溫不能從，而卓猶懷忌恨，故及於難。

translations.literal: " Wen could not follow, yet Zhuo still harbored jealousy and hatred; therefore he reached disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen did not act on the advice, and Dong Zhuo nursed the grudge until it cost Wen his life."

sentences.zh: 溫字伯慎，

translations.literal: Wen, courtesy name Boshen,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen, courtesy name Boshen,

sentences.zh: 〈《漢官儀》曰：「溫，穰人。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Han Official Precedents states: "Wen was a man of Rang."〉
translations.idiomatic: the Han guan yi identifies as a native of Rang.〉

sentences.zh: 少有名譽，累登公卿，亦陰與司徒王允共謀誅卓，事未及發而見害。

translations.literal: In youth he had fame and reputation, repeatedly ascended to duke and minister ranks, and also secretly with Minister of Education Wang Yun jointly plotted to execute Zhuo; the affair had not yet reached execution when he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen young to high renown and climbed step by step to the summit of official rank. He had also joined Minister Wang Yun's secret plot to kill Dong Zhuo, but was murdered before the coup could be launched.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉汝南伍孚

translations.literal: Colonel of the Agile Cavalry Wu Fu of Runan
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Wu Fu of Runan—

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書曰：「孚字德瑜，汝南吳房人。

translations.literal: 〈Xie Cheng's Book states: "Fu, courtesy name Deyu, was a man of Wufang in Runan."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng's history gives his style as Deyu and his home as Wufang in Runan—

sentences.zh: 質性剛毅，勇壯好義，力能兼人。」〉

translations.literal: His substance and nature were firm and resolute, brave and stalwart, fond of righteousness; his strength could match others."〉
translations.idiomatic: a man of iron nerve, dauntless courage, and strength greater than most."〉

sentences.zh: 忿卓凶毒，志手刃之，乃朝服懷佩刀以見卓。

translations.literal: Indignant at Zhuo's fierce poison, he resolved to hand-blade him; thereupon in court robes he hid a belt knife and went to see Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Burning at Dong Zhuo's cruelties, he resolved to stab the tyrant with his own hand. He donned full court dress, concealed a dagger at his belt, and asked for an audience.

sentences.zh: 孚語畢辭去，卓起送至閤，以手撫其背，孚因出刀刺之，不中。

translations.literal: When Fu had finished speaking and took leave, Zhuo rose and escorted him to the gate-tower, stroked his back with his hand; Fu thereupon drew the knife and stabbed him, but did not hit.
translations.idiomatic: When the interview ended, Dong Zhuo walked him to the door and clapped him paternally on the back. Wu Fu spun about and drove his blade at the tyrant's breast—but missed.

sentences.zh: 卓自奮得免，急呼左右執殺之，而大詬

translations.literal: Zhuo by his own exertion escaped, urgently called attendants left and right to seize and kill him, and greatly cursed
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo twisted free and screamed for his guards to seize the assassin. He rained abuse—

sentences.zh: 〈詬，罵也，音許豆反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Gou means to revile; it is read xudou fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The graph gou means "to revile," read xudou in fanqie.〉

sentences.zh: 曰：「虜欲反耶！

translations.literal: saying: "Do the captives wish to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: "So the barbarian slave would rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」孚大言曰：「恨不得磔裂姦賊於都市，

translations.literal: " Fu in a loud voice said: "I hate that I could not dismember the treacherous villain in the capital market,
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fu shouted back, "My only regret is that I could not tear the traitor limb from limb in the public square—

sentences.zh: 〈磔，車裂之也，音丁格反。

translations.literal: 〈Zhe means to chariot-tear him; it is read dingge fan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe means execution by tearing apart with chariots, read dingge—

sentences.zh: 獻帝春秋「磔」作「車」。〉

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian writes zhe as che."〉
translations.idiomatic: though the Xiandi chunqiu manuscript writes the word as che instead."〉

sentences.zh: 以謝天地！

translations.literal: to apologize to Heaven and Earth!"
translations.idiomatic: and so offer Heaven and Earth their due!"

sentences.zh: 」言未畢而斃。

translations.literal: " Before his words were finished he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He died mid-sentence under the guards' blades."

sentences.zh: 時王允與呂布及僕射士孫瑞謀誅卓。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Yun with Lü Bu and Supervisor of the Household Shisun Rui plotted to execute Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Minister Wang Yun, Lü Bu, and Supervisor Shisun Rui were laying plans to murder Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 〈《三輔決錄》曰：「瑞字君榮，扶風人，博達無不通。

translations.literal: 〈The Sanfu Judgment Record states: "Rui, courtesy name Junrong, was a man of Fufeng, broadly learned with nothing he did not master."
translations.idiomatic: The Sanfu juelu describes Shisun Rui, style Junrong, of Fufeng, as a scholar without a blind spot—

sentences.zh: 天子都許，追論瑞功，封子萌津亭侯。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven capitalled Xu, they retrospectively discussed Rui's merit and enfeoffed his son Meng as Marquis of Jinting.
translations.idiomatic: when the court moved to Xu, his son Meng was enfeoffed marquis of Jinting in posthumous honor of his father's service.

sentences.zh: 萌字文始，有才學，與王粲善，粲作詩贈萌。」〉

translations.literal: Meng, courtesy name Wenshi, had talent and learning, was on good terms with Wang Can; Can composed a poem presented to Meng."〉
translations.idiomatic: Meng, style Wenshi, was a gifted writer and friend of Wang Can, who composed verse in his praise."〉

sentences.zh: 有人書「呂」字於布上，負而行於市，歌曰：「布乎！

translations.literal: Someone wrote the character "Lü" on cloth, carried it on his back and walked in the market, singing: "Cloth!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone daubed the characters for "Lü" on a sheet, paraded it through the market on his back, and chanted, "Lü—cloth!"

sentences.zh: 」有告卓者，卓不悟。

translations.literal: " There was one who informed Zhuo; Zhuo did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Informants brought the riddle to Dong Zhuo, who failed to grasp that it named Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：「有道士書布為『呂』字，將以示卓，卓不知其為呂布也。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong ji states: "There was a Daoist who wrote on cloth the character 'Lü' and was about to show it to Zhuo; Zhuo did not know it referred to Lü Bu."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong ji says a Daoist priest wrote the character on cloth for Dong Zhuo to see, yet the tyrant still did not connect it with Lü Bu.〉

sentences.zh: 三年四月，帝疾新愈，大會未央殿。

translations.literal: In the third year, fourth month, the emperor's illness was newly healed; there was a great assembly in the Weiyang hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Chuping the emperor, recovered from a recent illness, held a great court in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 卓朝服升車，既而馬驚墯泥，還入更衣。

translations.literal: Zhuo in court robes mounted the carriage; soon the horses were startled and fell in mud; he returned inside to change robes.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo mounted his chariot in full court dress, but his horses shied and threw him into the mud; he went back inside to change.

sentences.zh: 其少妻止之，卓不從，遂行。

translations.literal: His young wife stopped him; Zhuo did not follow, and thereupon proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: His young concubine begged him not to go; he brushed her aside and set out anyway.

sentences.zh: 乃陳兵夾道，自壘及宮，左步右騎，屯衛周帀，令呂布等扞衛前後。

translations.literal: Thereupon he deployed troops along both sides of the road, from fort to palace, infantry on the left cavalry on the right, encamped guards all around, ordered Lü Bu and others to shield front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: He lined the route from his fortress to the palace with alternating foot and horse, ringed the precinct with guards, and ordered Lü Bu to screen him fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 王允乃與士孫瑞密表其事，使瑞自書詔以授布，令騎都尉李肅

translations.literal: Wang Yun thereupon with Shisun Rui secretly memorialized the affair, had Rui himself write the edict to hand to Bu, ordered Chief of Cavalry Li Su
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun and Shisun Rui secretly memorialized the plot, had Rui draft the edict in his own hand for Lü Bu, and assigned Chief of Cavalry Li Su

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝紀》曰：「肅，呂布同郡人也。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian states: "Su was a fellow-countryman of Lü Bu."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi ji notes that Li Su came from the same commandery as Lü Bu.〉

sentences.zh: 與布同心勇士十餘人，偽著衛士服於北掖門內以待卓。

translations.literal: together with Bu more than ten warriors of one mind, falsely wearing guardsmen's clothing inside the north Ye gate to await Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: to pick a dozen trusted fighting men who donned fake palace-guard uniforms inside the north Ye gate and waited for Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓將至，馬驚不行，怪懼欲還。

translations.literal: When Zhuo was about to arrive, the horses were startled and would not go; strangely afraid he wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: As he approached, his horses balked again; uneasy, he ordered the driver to turn back.

sentences.zh: 呂布勸令進，遂入門。

translations.literal: Lü Bu urged him to advance; thereupon he entered the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu urged him forward, and the chariot passed the gate.

sentences.zh: 肅以戟刺之，卓衷甲不入，傷臂墯車，顧大呼曰：「呂布何在？

translations.literal: Su with a halberd stabbed him; Zhuo wore armor beneath and it did not enter; wounded in the arm he fell from the carriage, turned his head and loudly cried: "Where is Lü Bu?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Su drove a halberd at his breast, but the hidden mail turned the blow aside—only an arm was gashed and Dong Zhuo tumbled from the car, roaring, "Where is Lü Bu?"

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「有詔討賊臣。

translations.literal: " Bu said: "There is an edict to strike the treacherous minister."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu answered, "An edict commands us to punish the traitor."

sentences.zh: 」卓大罵曰：「庸狗敢如是邪！

translations.literal: " Zhuo greatly cursed saying: "Base cur, dare you be thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo howled, "Miserable cur—how dare you!"

sentences.zh: 」布應聲持矛刺卓，趣兵斬之。

translations.literal: " Bu responding to the voice grasped a spear and stabbed Zhuo; hastening troops beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu drove his spear home and signaled the soldiers to finish the work with the sword."

sentences.zh: 〈趣音促。

translations.literal: 〈The character qu (urge) is here read like cu in cu "urgent".〉
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes that qu in this sense is read like the word cu, "urgent."〉

sentences.zh: 《九州春秋》曰：「布素使秦誼、陳衞、李黑等偽作宮門衞士，持長戟。

translations.literal: The Jiuzhou chunqiu states: "Bu had long ordered Qin Yi, Chen Wei, Li Hei and others falsely to act as palace gate guards, holding long halberds."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiuzhou chunqiu adds that Lü Bu had long stationed Qin Yi, Chen Wei, Li Hei, and others disguised as gate guards with long halberds—

sentences.zh: 卓到宮門，黑等以長戟俠叉卓車，或叉其馬。

translations.literal: When Zhuo reached the palace gate, Hei and others with long halberds flanked and forked Zhuo's carriage, or forked his horses.
translations.idiomatic: who crossed their halberds to pin Dong Zhuo's carriage and horses when he reached the gate.

sentences.zh: 卓驚呼布，布素施鎧於衣中，持矛，即應聲刺卓，墜於車。」〉

translations.literal: Zhuo startled cried to Bu; Bu had long worn armor inside his clothing, grasped a spear, immediately responding to the voice stabbed Zhuo, and he fell from the carriage."〉
