translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo screamed for him, Lü Bu—mail already under his robe—thrust with his spear and pitched the tyrant from the chariot."〉

sentences.zh: 主簿田儀

translations.literal: Registrar Tian Yi
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Tian Yi

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》「儀」字作「景」。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Jiuzhou chunqiu writes the character for Yi as Jing.〉
translations.idiomatic: One text writes his name as Tian Jing instead of Tian Yi.〉

sentences.zh: 及卓倉頭前赴其尸，布又殺之。

translations.literal: And when Zhuo's household slave rushed forward to his corpse, Bu again killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When a household slave of Dong Zhuo's ran to the body, Lü Bu cut him down as well.

sentences.zh: 馳繼赦書，以令宮陛內外。

translations.literal: Galloping followed the amnesty document to command inside and outside the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Riders galloped the amnesty edict through every corridor of the palace.

sentences.zh: 士卒皆稱萬歲，百姓歌舞於道。

translations.literal: Soldiers all cried "Ten thousand years"; common people sang and danced in the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The troops roared long life to the emperor while commoners danced in the streets.

sentences.zh: 長安中士女賣其珠玉衣裝市酒肉相慶者，填滿街肆。

translations.literal: In Chang'an gentlemen and women who sold their pearls and jade and clothing to buy wine and meat to congratulate one another filled the streets and markets.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and townsfolk pawned jewels and silks for wine and meat until every lane was jammed with revelers.

sentences.zh: 使皇甫嵩攻卓弟旻於郿塢，殺其母妻男女，盡滅其族。

translations.literal: He ordered Huangfu Song to attack Zhuo's younger brother Min at the Mei fort, killed his mother, wife, sons and daughters, and entirely exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Song was sent to storm the Mei fortress where Dong Min held out; mother, wives, children, and every Dong clansman were put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：「卓母年九十，走至塢門，曰：『乞脫我死。

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong ji states: "Zhuo's mother, ninety years old, ran to the fort gate and said: 'Beg to release me from death.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong ji records that Dong Zhuo's ninety-year-old mother crawled to the gate crying, "Spare an old woman's life—

sentences.zh: 』即時斬首。」〉

translations.literal: ' They at once beheaded her."〉
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded her on the spot."〉

sentences.zh: 乃尸卓於市。

translations.literal: Thereupon they exposed Zhuo's corpse in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's corpse was displayed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 天時始熱，卓素充肥，脂流於地。

translations.literal: The season was beginning to grow hot; Zhuo had always been abundantly fat; grease flowed on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Heat was setting in, and Dong Zhuo's obese frame began to melt until fat pooled on the ground.

sentences.zh: 守尸吏然火置卓臍中，光明達曙，如是積日。

translations.literal: The corpse-guarding clerk lit fire and placed it in Zhuo's navel; the light reached dawn; thus for accumulated days.
translations.idiomatic: The warden lit a wick in the tyrant's navel like a lamp; its flame burned clear to dawn, night after night.

sentences.zh: 諸袁門生又聚董氏之尸，焚灰揚之於路。

translations.literal: Disciples of the various Yuans again gathered the Dong clan corpses, burned the ashes and scattered them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Yuan clan heaped the Dong dead, reduced them to ash, and scattered the dust in the streets.

sentences.zh: 塢中珍藏有金二三萬斤，銀八九萬斤，錦綺繢縠紈素奇玩，積如丘山。

translations.literal: Treasures stored in the fort had gold two or three myriads of jin, silver eight or nine myriads of jin, brocades, figured silks, fine silks, plain silks, and curious playthings, piled like hills and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the fortress lay twenty or thirty thousand jin of gold, eighty or ninety thousand of silver, and treasure-mountains of brocade, damask, gauze, and curios.

sentences.zh: 李傕、郭汜

translations.literal: Li Jue, Guo Si
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si

sentences.zh: 初，卓以牛輔子婿，素所親信，使以兵屯陝。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Zhuo because Niu Fu was his son-in-law, whom he always trusted and favored, ordered him with troops to encamp at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dong Zhuo had posted his son-in-law Niu Fu—a man he trusted implicitly—with an army at Shan.

sentences.zh: 輔分遣其校尉李傕﹑郭汜﹑張濟將步騎數萬，

translations.literal: Fu separately dispatched his colonels Li Jue, Guo Si, and Zhang Ji to lead several myriads of infantry and cavalry,
translations.idiomatic: Niu Fu detached his colonels Li Jue, Guo Si, and Zhang Ji at the head of several tens of thousands of foot and horse—

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》：「傕，北地人。

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong ji: "Jue was a man of Beidi."
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong ji calls Li Jue a native of Beidi—

sentences.zh: 」劉艾《獻帝紀》曰：「傕字稚然。

translations.literal: " Liu Ai's Annals of Emperor Xian states: "Jue, courtesy name Zhiran."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ai's Xiandi ji gives his courtesy name as Zhiran—

sentences.zh: 汜，張掖人。」〉

translations.literal: Si was a man of Zhangye."〉
translations.idiomatic: and Guo Si as a man of Zhangye."〉

sentences.zh: 擊破河南尹朱儁於中牟。

translations.literal: They defeated and broke Grand Administrator of Henan Zhu Jun at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: who crushed Grand Administrator Zhu Jun of Henan at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 因掠陳留﹑穎川諸縣，殺略男女，所過無復遺類。

translations.literal: Thereupon they plundered Chenliu and Yingchuan various counties, killed and seized men and women; wherever they passed none of their kind survived.
translations.idiomatic: They swept through Chenliu and Yingchuan, slaughtering and dragging off the population until no living thing remained in their path.

sentences.zh: 呂布乃使李肅以詔命至陝討輔等，輔等逆與肅戰，肅敗走弘農，布誅殺之。

translations.literal: Lü Bu thereupon ordered Li Su with edict command to reach Shan to attack Fu and others; Fu and others went against Su and fought; Su was defeated and fled to Hongnong; Bu executed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu then sent Li Su with forged orders to demand Niu Fu's submission at Shan. Fu attacked instead; Su fled in defeat to Hongnong, where Lü Bu had him executed.

sentences.zh: 其後牛輔營中無故大驚，輔懼，乃齎金寶踰城走。

translations.literal: Afterward in Niu Fu's camp without cause there was great alarm; Fu was afraid, thereupon carrying gold and treasures climbed the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Niu Fu's camp panicked in the night for no clear reason. Terrified, Fu loaded gold and jewels, scaled the wall, and fled alone.

sentences.zh: 左右利其貨，斬輔，送首長安。

translations.literal: Those at his side coveted his goods, beheaded Fu, and sent his head to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His bodyguards murdered him for the treasure and carried his head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝紀》曰：「輔帳下支胡赤兒等，素待之過急，盡以家寶與之，自帶二十餘餅金、大白珠瓔。

translations.literal: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian states: "Fu's tent followers, the branch Hu Chier and others, he had always treated too harshly; he entirely gave them his household treasures, himself carrying more than twenty ingots of gold and great white pearl neck-strings."
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi ji explains that Niu Fu's Qiang follower Chier and the rest had long resented his harshness. Fu tried to buy their silence with his whole hoard—over twenty gold ingots and ropes of great pearls—

sentences.zh: 胡謂輔曰：『城北已有馬，可去也。

translations.literal: The Hu said to Fu: 'North of the wall horses are already there; you may go.'"
translations.idiomatic: while the Qiang told him, "Horses wait beyond the north wall—flee now."

sentences.zh: 』以繩繫輔腰，踰城懸下之，未及地丈許放之，輔傷腰不能行，諸胡共取其金并珠，斬首詣長安。」〉

translations.literal: ' They tied a rope around Fu's waist, crossed the wall and lowered him suspended; before reaching the ground by about a zhang they released him; Fu injured his waist and could not walk; the various Hu together took his gold and pearls, beheaded him, and went to Chang'an."〉
translations.idiomatic: They tied a rope around his waist to lower him from the wall, cut it when he was still a man's height above the ground, crippled him with the fall, seized gold and pearls, and decapitated him for the reward at Chang'an."〉

sentences.zh: 傕﹑汜等以王允﹑呂布殺董卓，故忿怒并州人，并州人其在軍者男女數百人，皆誅殺也。

translations.literal: Jue, Si and others because Wang Yun and Lü Bu killed Dong Zhuo, therefore were angry at Bingzhou people; Bingzhou people who were in the army, men and women several hundred persons, were all executed and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si blamed the men of Bing province for Dong Zhuo's death; every soldier from Bingzhou in their camps—several hundred men and women—was massacred.

sentences.zh: 牛輔既敗，眾無所依，欲各散去。

translations.literal: Niu Fu having already been defeated, the host had nothing to rely on and wished each to scatter and depart.
translations.idiomatic: With Niu Fu dead, the army had no leader and prepared to break up.

sentences.zh: 傕等恐，乃先遣使詣長安，求乞赦免。

translations.literal: Jue and others were afraid; thereupon they first sent envoys to Chang'an, begging to seek amnesty and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his confederates panicked and sent envoys ahead to Chang'an pleading for a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 王允以為一歲不可再赦，不許之。

translations.literal: Wang Yun held that within one year amnesty cannot twice be granted, and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun insisted that the empire could not issue two general amnestes in a single year and refused.

sentences.zh: 傕等益懷憂懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: Jue and others increasingly harbored worry and fear, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his allies grew desperate, with no plan left but the sword.

sentences.zh: 武威人賈詡時在傕軍，說之

translations.literal: Jia Xu of Wuwei was at that time in Jue's army, and persuaded them
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu of Wuwei was attached to Li Jue's command and urged them

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰：「卓之入洛陽，詡以太尉掾為平津尉，遷討虜校尉。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states: "When Zhuo entered Luoyang, Xu as Grand Commandant aide became Pingjin commandant, was promoted to Colonel Who Strikes the Barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei zhi notes that when Dong Zhuo seized Luoyang, Jia Xu served as an aide to the grand commandant, then as commandant of Pingjin, and rose to colonel who strikes the barbarians—

sentences.zh: 」牛輔屯陝，詡在輔軍。

translations.literal: Niu Fu encamped at Shan; Xu was in Fu's army.
translations.idiomatic: while Niu Fu held Shan, Jia Xu served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 輔旣死，故詡在傕軍。〉

translations.literal: Fu having died, therefore Xu was in Jue's army.〉
translations.idiomatic: After Niu Fu's death Jia Xu fell in with Li Jue's host.〉

sentences.zh: 曰：「聞長安中議欲盡誅涼州人，諸君若弃軍單行，則一亭長能束君矣。

translations.literal: saying: "I hear that in Chang'an they deliberate intending entirely to execute Liangzhou men; gentlemen, if you abandon the army and go alone, then a single village chief can bind you.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Word from the capital is that they mean to wipe out every man from the northwest. If you drop your arms and flee alone, a single post-station chief could clap you in fetters.

sentences.zh: 不如相率而西，以攻長安，為董公報仇。

translations.literal: It is better mutually to lead westward and attack Chang'an, to avenge Lord Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Better march west together, storm Chang'an, and avenge Dong Zhuo."

sentences.zh: 事濟，奉國家以正天下；

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, uphold the state and set right all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: If you win, you can restore the throne and set the realm to rights;

sentences.zh: 若其不合，走未後也。

translations.literal: if it does not fit, fleeing is not yet too late.
translations.idiomatic: if you fail, you can still run for the border before the end."

sentences.zh: 」傕等然之，各相謂曰：「京師不赦我，我當以死決之。

translations.literal: " Jue and others approved it; each said to the other: "The capital will not pardon us; we ought to decide it with death.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed. "The capital will never forgive us," they said; "we stake everything on one throw."

sentences.zh: 若攻長安克，則得天下矣；

translations.literal: If we attack Chang'an and conquer, then we obtain all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: If we take Chang'an, the empire is ours;

sentences.zh: 不克，則鈔三輔婦女財物，西歸鄉里，尚可延命。

translations.literal: if we do not conquer, then we plunder the Three Adjuncts' women and goods, return west to our villages, and can still prolong life.
translations.idiomatic: if not, we strip the capital region of women and loot, ride home to the west, and live out our lives as bandit kings."

sentences.zh: 」眾以為然，於是共結盟，率軍數千，晨夜西行。

translations.literal: " The host thought it right; thereupon they jointly swore alliance, led several thousand troops, and marched west day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The army took the oath and, a few thousand strong, struck west without pause.

sentences.zh: 王允聞之，乃遣卓故將胡軫﹑徐榮擊之於新豐。

translations.literal: Wang Yun heard of it and thereupon sent Zhuo's former generals Hu Zhen and Xu Rong to strike them at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun dispatched Dong Zhuo's old officers Hu Zhen and Xu Rong to intercept them at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：「胡文才、楊整脩皆涼州人，王允素所不善也。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiuzhou chunqiu states: "Hu Wencai and Yang Zhengxiu were both Liangzhou men, whom Wang Yun had never favored.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiuzhou chunqiu adds that Hu Wencai and Yang Zhengxiu, both northwesterners whom Wang Yun had always disliked,

sentences.zh: 及李傕之叛，乃召文才、整脩，使東曉喻之。

translations.literal: When Li Jue rebelled, he then summoned Wencai and Zhengxiu and ordered them east to enlighten and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: were summoned when Li Jue rose and sent east to "reason" with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 不假借以溫顏，謂曰：『關東鼠子欲何為乎？

translations.literal: He did not lend them kindly mien but said to them: "What do the eastern-pass ratlings intend to do?
translations.idiomatic: Yun offered no courtesy. "What do those rats beyond the pass think they are doing?" he demanded.

sentences.zh: 卿往曉之。

translations.literal: You go enlighten them.
translations.idiomatic: Go and talk sense into them."

sentences.zh: 』於是二人往，實召兵而還。」〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon the two men went and in truth summoned troops and returned."〉
translations.idiomatic: The two went—and used the mission to raise troops for Li Jue instead."〉

sentences.zh: 榮戰死，軫以眾降。

translations.literal: Rong died in battle; Zhen with the host surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rong fell fighting; Hu Zhen surrendered his command to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 傕隨道收兵，比至長安，已十餘萬，與卓故部曲樊稠﹑李蒙等合，

translations.literal: Jue along the road gathered troops; by the time he reached Chang'an there were already more than a hundred thousand, and he joined with Zhuo's former subordinate officers Fan Chou, Li Meng, and others,
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue swept up recruits along the march until his column topped a hundred thousand men, then merged with Dong Zhuo's old officers Fan Chou and Li Meng,

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《紀》曰：「蒙後為傕所殺。」〉

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Annals states: "Meng was later killed by Jue."〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong's chronicle notes that Li Meng was later murdered by Li Jue.〉

sentences.zh: 圍長安。

translations.literal: and besieged Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: and together they ringed Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 城峻不可攻，守之八日，呂布軍有叟兵內反，

translations.literal: The walls were steep and could not be attacked; having guarded eight days, in Lü Bu's army there were Shu soldiers who rebelled within,
translations.idiomatic: The walls were too high for a quick storm. On the eighth day of the siege Shu auxiliaries in Lü Bu's ranks turned traitor,

sentences.zh: 〈叟兵即蜀兵也。

translations.literal: 〈Shu soldiers are Shu troops.
translations.idiomatic: The term "Shu soldiers" means troops from Ba-Shu—

sentences.zh: 漢代謂蜀為叟。〉

translations.literal: In Han times Shu was called Sou.〉
translations.idiomatic: Han usage often called the region Sou.〉

sentences.zh: 引傕眾得入。

translations.literal: leading Jue's host to be able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: and opened the gates to Li Jue's horde.

sentences.zh: 城潰，放兵虜掠，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: The city collapsed; they unleashed troops to capture and plunder; the dead were more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. The invaders looted at will and left more than ten thousand corpses in the streets.

sentences.zh: 殺衛尉种拂等。

translations.literal: They killed Commandant of the Guards Zhong Fu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Among the slain was Commandant of the Guards Zhong Fu and many others.

sentences.zh: 呂布戰敗出奔。

translations.literal: Lü Bu was defeated in battle and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was beaten and fled the capital.

sentences.zh: 王允奉天子保宣平城門樓上。

translations.literal: Wang Yun escorted the Son of Heaven to hold the Xuanyi Gate tower on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun shepherded the emperor onto the tower above the Xuanyi Gate.

sentences.zh: 〈《三輔黃圖》曰：「長安城東面北頭門號宣平門。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Sanfu Huangtu states: "On Chang'an's east face the northernmost gate is styled Xuanyi Gate."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Sanfu huangtu identifies Xuanyi as the northern gate on the east wall of Chang'an.〉

sentences.zh: 於是大赦天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon there was a great amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The court then proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 李傕﹑郭汜﹑樊稠等皆為將軍。

translations.literal: Li Jue, Guo Si, Fan Chou, and others all became generals.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, Guo Si, Fan Chou, and their confederates were all enfeoffed as generals.

sentences.zh: 〈袁山松書曰「允謂傕等曰：『臣無作威作福，將軍乃放縱，欲何為乎？

translations.literal: Yuan Shansong's Book states "Yun said to Jue and others: 'Your subject has not made awe and made blessing; you generals are wanton and unrestrained—what do you intend to do?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shansong records Wang Yun rebuking them: "I never abused my power; you generals run wild—what do you mean by it?"

sentences.zh: 』傕等不應。

translations.literal: Jue and others did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: They answered him with silence.

sentences.zh: 自拜署傕為揚武將軍，汜為揚烈將軍，樊稠等皆為中郎將」也。〉

translations.literal: He himself appointed and sealed Jue as General Who Displays Martial Might, Si as General Who Displays Fierce Might, Fan Chou and others all as generals of the gentlemen of the household" as well.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yun then himself named Li Jue general who displays martial might, Guo Si general who displays fierce might, and Fan Chou and the rest generals of the household—so runs another account.〉

sentences.zh: 遂圍門樓，共表請司徒王允出，問「太師何罪」？

translations.literal: Thereupon they surrounded the gate tower and jointly memorialized begging Minister of Education Wang Yun to come out, asking "What crime had the Grand Tutor?"
translations.idiomatic: They surrounded the tower and demanded that Minister Wang Yun descend, shouting, "What crime had the grand tutor?"

sentences.zh: 允窮蹙乃下，後數日見殺。

translations.literal: Yun was cornered and thereupon came down; after several days he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped, Wang Yun came down; within days they murdered him.

sentences.zh: 傕等葬董卓於郿，並收董氏所焚尸之灰，合斂一棺而葬之。

translations.literal: Jue and others buried Dong Zhuo at Mei, and together gathered the ash of the Dong clan corpses that had been burned, combined them in one coffin and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: They reburied Dong Zhuo at Mei, scraped together the ashes of his clan from the pyres, and interred all in a single coffin.

sentences.zh: 葬日，大風雨，霆震卓墓，流水入藏，漂其棺木。

translations.literal: On the burial day there were great wind and rain; thunder shook Zhuo's tomb; flowing water entered the vault and floated away the coffin wood.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day a tempest broke; lightning struck the mound; floodwater poured into the crypt and washed the coffin away.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：「冢戶開，大風暴雨，水土流入，抒出之。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi qiju zhu states: "The tomb door opened; great wind and violent rain; earth and water flowed in; they bailed it out.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial diary says the tomb mouth gaped, storms drove mud and water inside, and workmen tried to bail it out—

sentences.zh: 棺向入，輒復風雨，水溢郭戶，如此者三四。

translations.literal: When the coffin was about to enter, again there were wind and rain; water overflowed the outer wall opening—thus three or four times.
translations.idiomatic: each time they lowered the coffin, wind and rain redoubled until water lapped the outer gate—three or four rounds of this.

sentences.zh: 冢中水半所，稠等共下棺，天風雨益暴甚，遂閉戶。

translations.literal: Water in the tomb reached half its depth; Chou and others together lowered the coffin; Heaven's wind and rain grew even more violent, and they closed the door.
translations.idiomatic: When the crypt was half full of water, Fan Chou and the rest tried again; the storm raged worse than ever and they sealed the doors.

sentences.zh: 戶閉，大風復破其冢。」〉

translations.literal: When the door was closed, great wind again broke open the tomb."〉
translations.idiomatic: The wind then burst the sealed tomb open again."〉

sentences.zh: 傕又遷車騎將軍，開府，領司隸校尉，假節。

translations.literal: Jue was further promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry, opened a bureau, concurrently held Colonel Director of Retainers, and was given credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue was raised to general of chariots and cavalry with his own bureau, concurrent colonel of the metropolitan region, and imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 汜後將軍，稠右將軍，張濟為鎮東將軍，並封列侯。

translations.literal: Si became General of the Rear, Chou General of the Right, Zhang Ji General Who Guards the East, and all were enfeoffed full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si became general of the rear, Fan Chou general of the right, Zhang Ji general who guards the east; each received a full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 傕、汜、稠共秉朝政。

translations.literal: Jue, Si, and Chou together grasped court government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, Guo Si, and Fan Chou divided civil power among themselves.

sentences.zh: 濟出屯弘農。

translations.literal: Ji went out to encamp at Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji withdrew to camp at Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 以賈詡為左馮翊，欲侯之。

translations.literal: They made Jia Xu Administrator of Left Fengyi and wished to enfeoff him marquis.
translations.idiomatic: They named Jia Xu administrator of left Fengyi and offered him a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 詡曰：「此救命之計，何功之有！

translations.literal: Xu said: "This was a plan to save our lives—what merit is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu replied, "That was a stratagem to save our necks, not an exploit fit for noble rank."

sentences.zh: 」固辭乃止。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined and thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He refused until they dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 更以為尚書典選。

translations.literal: They changed him to be Supervisor of the Masters of Writing in charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they made him supervisor of writing in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，大雨晝夜二十餘日，漂沒人庶，又風如冬時。

translations.literal: The next summer, great rain day and night for more than twenty days, floated and drowned common people, and the wind was like winter season.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer brought twenty days and nights of rain that drowned thousands and winds as cold as midwinter.

sentences.zh: 帝使御史裴茂訊詔獄，原繫者二百餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Imperial Clerk Pei Mao to examine the edict-prison and release more than two hundred who were bound.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Imperial Clerk Pei Mao to review the imperial prison and free over two hundred inmates.

sentences.zh: 其中有為傕所枉繫者，傕恐茂赦之，乃表奏茂擅出囚徒，疑有姦故，請收之。

translations.literal: Among them were some whom Jue had wrongly imprisoned; Jue feared Mao would pardon them, thereupon memorialized accusing Mao of presumptuously releasing convicts, suspecting treacherous intent, and requesting to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Some were men Li Jue had jailed on false charges. Fearing Pei Mao would liberate them, Li Jue memorialized that Mao had illegally emptied the prisons and should be arrested.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「災異屢降，陰雨為害，使者銜命宣佈恩澤，原解輕微，庶合天心。

translations.literal: The edict stated: "Portents and anomalies have repeatedly descended; yin rain does harm; the envoy bears the charge to proclaim and spread grace, pardon and release the light and slight, hoping thereby to accord with Heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read, "Disasters have piled up and endless rain has scourged the land. The envoy was sent to spread mercy and free minor offenders so as to please Heaven.

sentences.zh: 欲釋冤結而復罪之乎！

translations.literal: Do you wish to loosen wrongful bonds yet again make them guilty!"
translations.idiomatic: Would you undo one injustice only to invent another?"

sentences.zh: 一切勿問。」

translations.literal: Let all matters go unquestioned."
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter drop entirely."

sentences.zh: 初，卓之入關，要韓遂﹑馬騰共謀山東。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Zhuo entered the passes, he summoned Han Sui and Ma Teng to jointly plot against the east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo first entered the passes he had summoned Han Sui and Ma Teng to join him against the coalition east of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝傳》曰：「騰父平，扶風人。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi zhuan states: "Teng's father Ping was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi zhuan says Ma Teng's father Ping came from Fufeng—

sentences.zh: 為天水蘭干尉，失官，遂留隴西，與羌雜居。

translations.literal: He was commandant of Langan in Tianshui, lost office, thereupon stayed in Longxi, and dwelt mixed with the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: served as commandant of Langan in Tianshui, lost his post, and stayed in Longxi among the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 家貧無妻，遂取羌女，生騰。」〉

translations.literal: The family was poor and had no wife; thereupon he took a Qiang woman and begat Teng."〉
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to marry a Chinese wife, he took a Qiang woman and fathered Ma Teng."〉

sentences.zh: 遂、騰見天下方亂，亦欲倚卓起兵。

translations.literal: Sui and Teng saw that all under Heaven was just in disorder, and also wished to rely on Zhuo to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm dissolve into chaos, Han Sui and Ma Teng had likewise looked to Dong Zhuo as their patron for raising troops.

sentences.zh: 興平元年，馬騰從隴右來朝，進屯霸橋。

translations.literal: In the first Xingping year, Ma Teng came from Longyou to court, advanced and encamped at Ba Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingping Ma Teng rode in from Longyou for an audience and camped his host at Ba Bridge.

sentences.zh: 時騰私有求於傕，不獲而怒，遂與侍中馬宇﹑右中郎將劉範﹑

translations.literal: At the time Teng privately had requests of Jue that were not granted, and he was angry; thereupon with Palace Attendant Ma Yu, General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the Right Liu Fan,
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng had asked private favors of Li Jue and, when refused, flew into a rage. He joined Palace Attendant Ma Yu, General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the Right Liu Fan,

sentences.zh: 〈焉之子。〉

translations.literal: 〈Yan's son.〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan was the son of Liu Yan.〉

sentences.zh: 前涼州刺史种劭﹑中郎將杜稟

translations.literal: former Inspector of Liangzhou Zhong Shao, General of the Gentlemen of the Household Du Bing
translations.idiomatic: former inspector of Liangzhou Zhong Shao, and General of the Gentlemen of the Household Du Bing

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝紀》曰：「稟與賈詡有隙，脅扶風吏人為騰守槐里，欲共攻傕。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi ji states: "Bing had a rift with Jia Xu, coerced the officials and people of Fufeng to hold Huali for Teng, wishing together to attack Jue.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi ji notes that Du Bing hated Jia Xu, forced the people of Fufeng to hold Huali for Ma Teng, and planned to strike Li Jue—

sentences.zh: 傕令樊稠及兄子利數萬人攻圍槐里，夜梯城，城陷，斬稟梟首。」〉

translations.literal: Jue ordered Fan Chou and his elder brother's son Li with several tens of thousands to attack and besiege Huali, scaled the city by night, the city fell, beheaded Bing and displayed the head."〉
translations.idiomatic: until Li Jue sent Fan Chou and his nephew Li with tens of thousands to storm Huali by night, took the town, and beheaded Du Bing."〉

sentences.zh: 合兵攻傕，連日不決。

translations.literal: They united troops to attack Jue; for successive days it was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Their combined forces besieged Li Jue for days without victory.

sentences.zh: 韓遂聞之，乃率眾來欲和騰﹑傕，既而復與騰合。

translations.literal: Han Sui heard of it, thereupon led his host to come wishing to reconcile Teng and Jue, but afterward again united with Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui marched in hoping to mediate between Ma Teng and Li Jue, then sided with Ma Teng after all.

sentences.zh: 傕使兄子利共郭汜﹑樊稠與騰等戰於長平觀下。

translations.literal: Jue ordered his elder brother's son Li together with Guo Si and Fan Chou to fight Teng and others below the Changping Watch.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue sent his nephew Li with Guo Si and Fan Chou to give battle to Ma Teng below the Changping Watch.

sentences.zh: 〈前書音義曰：「長平，阪名也，在池陽南。

translations.literal: 〈The Former Documents Sound and Meaning states: "Changping is a slope name south of Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han shu commentaries place the Changping slope south of Chiyang—

sentences.zh: 有長平觀，去長安五十里。」〉

translations.literal: There is a Changping Watch fifty li from Chang'an."〉
translations.idiomatic: with a watchtower fifty li from Chang'an."〉

sentences.zh: 遂﹑騰敗，斬首萬餘級，种劭﹑劉範等皆死。

translations.literal: Sui and Teng were defeated; beheaded heads exceeded ten thousand; Zhong Shao, Liu Fan, and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui and Ma Teng were routed with more than ten thousand heads counted; Zhong Shao and Liu Fan fell among the dead.

sentences.zh: 遂﹑騰走還涼州，稠等又追之。

translations.literal: Sui and Teng fled back to Liangzhou; Chou and others again pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors bolted for Liangzhou while Fan Chou pressed the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 韓遂使人語稠曰：「天下反覆未可知，相與州裡，今雖小違，要當大同，欲共一言。

translations.literal: Han Sui sent a man to speak to Chou saying: "All under Heaven turns and reverses and cannot be known; we are from the same province; though now slightly at odds, in the end we must greatly agree—I wish to speak one word with you.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui sent word to Fan Chou: "The world is chaos—we hail from the same commandery. Though we fight today, we may need each other tomorrow. Let us talk.

sentences.zh: 」乃駢馬交臂相加，

translations.literal: " Thereupon they rode paired horses with arms interlocked,
translations.idiomatic: They rode stirrup to stirrup, arms linked,

sentences.zh: 〈駢，並也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Pian means side by side.〉
translations.idiomatic: pian meaning "abreast."〉

sentences.zh: 笑語良久。

translations.literal: laughed and talked a long while.
translations.idiomatic: and laughed and talked for a long while.

sentences.zh: 軍還，利告傕曰：「樊﹑韓駢馬笑語，不知其辭，而意愛甚密。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Li reported to Jue saying: "Fan and Han rode paired horses laughing and talking; I did not know their words, but their intent and affection were very intimate.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched back, Li Jue's nephew Li whispered, "Fan Chou and Han Sui rode laughing together like brothers—I could not hear their words, but their fondness looked dangerously close.

sentences.zh: 」於是傕﹑稠始相猜疑。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jue and Chou began mutually to suspect.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Li Jue and Fan Chou nursed mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 猶加稠及郭汜開府，與三公合為六府，皆參選舉。

translations.literal: Still they further granted Chou and Guo Si opened bureaus, joining the Three Dukes to make six bureaus, all participating in selection.
translations.idiomatic: Nonetheless Li Jue let Fan Chou and Guo Si open their own bureaus alongside the three dukes—six personnel offices in all, each naming its own men.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：「傕等各欲用其所舉，若壹違之，便忿憤恚怒。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi qiju zhu states: "Jue and each wished to employ those whom he nominated; if once opposed them, they were resentful and furious.
translations.idiomatic: The court diary complains that each warlord insisted on appointing only his own nominees and flew into a rage at every objection—

sentences.zh: 主者患之，乃以次第用其所舉，先從傕起，汜次之，稠次之。

translations.literal: The presiding officials worried over it; thereupon by order of rank they employed those whom each nominated, beginning with Jue, Si next, Chou next.
translations.idiomatic: so the clerks rotated strictly in order: Li Jue's list first, then Guo Si's, then Fan Chou's.

sentences.zh: 三公所舉，終不見用。」〉

translations.literal: What the Three Dukes nominated was in the end not employed."〉
translations.idiomatic: Candidates put forward by the three dukes were ignored altogether."〉

sentences.zh: 時長安中盜賊不禁，白日虜掠，傕﹑汜﹑稠乃參分城內，各備其界，猶不能制，而其子弟縱橫，侵暴百姓。

translations.literal: At the time in Chang'an bandits were unchecked; in broad daylight they plundered; Jue, Si, and Chou thereupon tripartitioned the city interior, each guarding his own zone, yet still could not control it, while their sons and younger kin ran rampant, encroaching on and brutalizing the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry ran unchecked in broad daylight. Li Jue, Guo Si, and Fan Chou carved Chang'an into three zones, each policing his own third, yet could not stop the mayhem as their kinsmen preyed on the populace.

sentences.zh: 是時穀一斛五十萬，豆麥二十萬，人相食啖，

translations.literal: At this time grain was five hundred thousand cash per hu, beans and wheat two hundred thousand; people mutually ate one another,
translations.idiomatic: Grain hit five hundred thousand cash a hu, beans and wheat two hundred thousand; neighbors fed on neighbors' flesh—

sentences.zh: 〈啖音徒敢反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Dan is read tugan fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: dan "devour" is read tugan in fanqie.〉

sentences.zh: 白骨委樍，臭穢滿路。

translations.literal: white bones piled in heaps; stench and filth filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: bones heaped like cordwood and stench choking every road.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍御史侯汶

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Attending Imperial Clerk Hou Wen
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Attending Imperial Clerk Hou Wen

sentences.zh: 〈音問。〉

translations.literal: 〈read like wen.〉
translations.idiomatic: the name read like the word "ask."〉

sentences.zh: 出太倉米豆為饑人作糜，經日而死者無降。

translations.literal: to take out from the Grand Granary rice and beans to make gruel for the starving; after a full day those who died did not decrease.
translations.idiomatic: to issue grain and beans from the imperial granary as gruel for the starving, yet after a full day the death toll did not fall.

sentences.zh: 帝疑賦恤有虛，

translations.literal: The emperor suspected that distribution and relief had falsity,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected embezzlement in the relief effort,

sentences.zh: 〈賦，布也。

translations.literal: 〈Fu means to distribute.
translations.idiomatic: Fu means to distribute,

sentences.zh: 卹，憂也。〉

translations.literal: Xu means to care for.〉
translations.idiomatic: xu to show compassion.〉

sentences.zh: 乃親於御前自加臨檢。

translations.literal: thereupon personally in front of the imperial seat added his own inspection.
translations.idiomatic: and personally ladled porridge beside the throne to test the ration.

sentences.zh: 既知不實，使侍中劉艾出讓有司。

translations.literal: Having learned it was untrue, he ordered Palace Attendant Liu Ai to go forth and reprove the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the fraud proved, he sent Palace Attendant Liu Ai to rebuke the ministers in charge.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書令以下皆詣省閣謝，奏收侯汶考實。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Supervisor of the Masters of Writing downward all went to the gate complex to apologize, memorializing to seize Hou Wen and examine the truth.
translations.idiomatic: From the supervisor of writing down, the whole secretariat presented itself to apologize and asked that Hou Wen be arrested and interrogated.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「未忍致汶于理，可杖五十。

translations.literal: The edict stated: "I have not the heart to subject Wen to the law; he may be caned fifty strokes."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript spared him execution: fifty strokes of the heavy stick would suffice.

sentences.zh: 」自是後多得全濟。

translations.literal: " From this time onward many more were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: After that, far more famine victims actually survived the relief.

sentences.zh: 明年春，傕因會刺殺樊稠於坐，

translations.literal: The next spring, Jue at a meeting stabbed Fan Chou to death in his seat,
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Li Jue assassinated Fan Chou at a banquet,

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝紀》曰：「傕見稠果勇而得衆心，疾害之，醉酒，潛使外生騎都尉胡封於坐中拉殺稠。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi ji states: "Jue saw that Chou was truly brave and won the host's hearts, envied and harmed him, got him drunk, secretly ordered his sister's son Chief of Cavalry Hu Feng in the midst of the seating to throttle and kill Chou."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi ji says Li Jue resented Fan Chou's popularity, plied him with wine, and had his nephew Hu Feng strangle him in his chair.〉

sentences.zh: 由是諸將各相疑異，傕﹑汜遂復理兵相攻。

translations.literal: Thereby the various generals each mutually suspected difference; Jue and Si thereupon again readied troops and attacked each other.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual suspicion split the warlord clique, and Li Jue and Guo Si went back to open war.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《紀》曰「李傕數設酒請汜，或留汜止宿。

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Annals states "Li Jue repeatedly set wine feasts and invited Si, sometimes detaining Si to lodge overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong records that Li Jue kept inviting Guo Si to drinking parties and sometimes kept him overnight—

sentences.zh: 汜妻懼與傕婢妾私而奪己愛，思有以離閒之。

translations.literal: Si's wife feared that with Jue's maids and concubines he would privately seize her husband's love, and thought how to alienate them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si's wife suspected her husband was sleeping with Li Jue's women and set out to turn him against his ally.

sentences.zh: 會傕送饋，汜妻乃以豉為藥。

translations.literal: When Jue sent provisions, Si's wife then took fermented beans for poison.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jue sent gifts of food, she sprinkled the dish with beans to make it look drugged.

sentences.zh: 汜將食，妻曰：『食從外來，儻或有故？

translations.literal: Si was about to eat; his wife said: "Food that comes from outside—perhaps there is reason to beware?"
translations.idiomatic: As Guo Si lifted his chopsticks she cried, "Food from outside—who knows what they mixed into it?"

sentences.zh: 』遂摘藥示之，曰：『一栖不兩雄，我固疑將軍之信李公也。

translations.literal: Thereupon she picked out the "poison" to show him, saying: "One roost holds no two cocks—I always doubted the general's trust in Lord Li.
translations.idiomatic: She fished out the beans as "proof" and said, "Two cocks cannot share one perch—I knew you trusted Li Jue too much."

sentences.zh: 』他日傕請汜，大醉，汜疑傕藥之，絞糞汁飲之乃解，於是遂相猜疑」也。〉

translations.literal: " Another day Jue invited Si; he was greatly drunk; Si suspected Jue had drugged him, wrung dung juice and drank it before he recovered; thereupon they mutually suspected."〉
translations.idiomatic: Another night Li Jue got Guo Si blind drunk; Si thought he had been poisoned and drank fecal broth as an emetic—after that the two were enemies."〉

sentences.zh: 安西將軍楊定者，故卓部曲將也。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Yang Ding was formerly Zhuo's subordinate officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding, the general who pacifies the west, had been an officer under Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 懼傕忍害，乃與汜合謀迎天子幸其營。

translations.literal: Fearing Jue's cruel harm, he thereupon with Si jointly plotted to welcome the Son of Heaven to favor his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified of Li Jue, he conspired with Guo Si to abduct the emperor into his own lines.

sentences.zh: 傕知其計，即使兄子暹

translations.literal: Jue learned of their plan and immediately ordered his elder brother's son Xian
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue learned of it and sent his nephew Li Xian

sentences.zh: 〈音纖。〉

translations.literal: 〈read like xian.〉
translations.idiomatic: the name read xian, "fine silk."〉

sentences.zh: 將數千人圍宮。

translations.literal: to lead several thousand men and surround the palace.
translations.idiomatic: with several thousand men to surround the palace.

sentences.zh: 以車三乘迎天子﹑皇后。

translations.literal: With three carriages he welcomed the Son of Heaven and the empress.
translations.idiomatic: He brought three chariots to carry away the emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 太尉楊彪謂暹曰：「古今帝王，無在人臣家者。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yang Biao said to Xian: "Of ancient and modern emperors and kings, none has dwelt in a subject's house.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yang Biao told Li Xian, "No true Son of Heaven has ever lodged in a minister's camp.

sentences.zh: 諸君舉事，當上順天心，柰何如是！

translations.literal: Gentlemen, when you raise affairs, ought you not to accord with Heaven's mind—how can you act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to move the throne, at least do it with Heaven's blessing—how can you behave like bandits?"

sentences.zh: 」暹曰：「將軍計決矣。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "The general's plan is already decided."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian answered, "My uncle's mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 」帝於是遂幸傕營，彪等皆徒從。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon favored Jue's camp; Biao and the rest all followed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was marched to Li Jue's fortress; Yang Biao and the courtiers had to trail behind on foot.

sentences.zh: 亂兵入殿，掠宮人什物，傕又徙御府金帛乘輿器服，而放火燒宮殿官府居人悉盡。

translations.literal: Rebel troops entered the halls, plundered palace women and goods; Jue also moved the imperial treasury gold, silks, chariots, vessels, and robes, and set fire so that palaces, government offices, and dwellings of residents were utterly burned.
translations.idiomatic: Rioters looted the harem while Li Jue carted off the imperial treasury and torched palace, yamen, and private house until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 帝使楊彪與司空張喜等十餘人和傕﹑汜，汜不從，遂質留公卿。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yang Biao and Minister of Works Zhang Xi and more than ten others to reconcile Jue and Si; Si would not follow, thereupon detained the dukes and ministers as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yang Biao, Minister Zhang Xi, and a dozen others to mediate; Guo Si refused and took the high ministers hostage.

sentences.zh: 彪謂汜曰：「將軍達人閒事，柰何君臣分爭，一人劫天子，一人質公卿，此可行邪？

translations.literal: Biao said to Si: "General, you are a man who understands human affairs—how can lord and minister wrangle so that one seizes the Son of Heaven and one holds the dukes and ministers hostage—can this be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao demanded of Guo Si, "You know the world—how can one warlord kidnap the emperor while his rival holds the whole cabinet for ransom?"

sentences.zh: 」汜怒，欲手刃彪。

translations.literal: " Si was angry and wished to hand-kill Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si drew his sword to strike Yang Biao down.

sentences.zh: 彪曰：「卿尚不奉國家，吾豈求生邪！

translations.literal: " Biao said: "You still do not serve the state—do I seek to preserve life!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao retorted, "You no longer serve the Han—do you think I cling to mine?"

sentences.zh: 」左右多諫，汜乃止。

translations.literal: " Many at his sides remonstrated, and Si thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants talked Guo Si out of the murder.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵攻傕，矢及帝前，

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops to attack Jue; arrows reached before the emperor,
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted Li Jue's lines until arrows whistled past the emperor's ear—

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝紀》曰：「汜與傕將張苞、張龍謀誅傕，汜將兵夜攻傕門。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi ji states: "Si plotted with Jue's officers Zhang Bao and Zhang Long to kill Jue; Si led troops by night to attack Jue's gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi ji says Guo Si conspired with Li Jue's officers Zhang Bao and Zhang Long for a night attack on Li Jue's camp—

sentences.zh: 候開門內汜兵，苞等燒屋，火不然。

translations.literal: They waited for the gate to open and admit Si's soldiers; Bao and others burned houses, but the fire would not catch.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si's men slipped inside, yet the planned fire failed to spread.

sentences.zh: 汜兵弓弩並發，矢及天子樓帷簾中。」〉

translations.literal: Si's troops crossbows shot together; arrows reached the Son of Heaven's tower curtains within."〉
translations.idiomatic: A volley from Guo Si's archers punched bolts through the curtains of the imperial tower."〉

sentences.zh: 又貫傕耳。

translations.literal: They also pierced Jue's ear.
translations.idiomatic: One bolt grazed Li Jue's ear.

sentences.zh: 傕將楊奉本白波賊帥，乃將兵救傕，於是汜眾乃退。

translations.literal: Jue's officer Yang Feng had originally been a White Wave bandit chief; he thereupon led troops to rescue Jue, whereupon Si's host thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue's officer Yang Feng, once a White Wave chieftain, rode to Li Jue's rescue and drove Guo Si back.

sentences.zh: 是日，傕復移帝幸其北塢，唯皇后﹑宋貴人俱。

translations.literal: That day, Jue again moved the emperor to favor his northern fort; only the empress and Honored Lady Song accompanied.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Jue dragged the court to his northern redoubt, leaving only the empress and Lady Song at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 傕使校尉監門，隔絕內外。

translations.literal: Jue ordered colonels to guard the gates and cut off inside from outside.
translations.idiomatic: He posted colonels at every gate to seal the compound.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝紀》曰：「傕令門設反關，校尉守察。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi ji states: "Jue ordered the gates fitted with reverse bars, colonels to guard and watch.
translations.idiomatic: The diary records barred gates, colonels on watch—

sentences.zh: 盛夏炎暑，不能得冷水，飢渴流離。

translations.literal: In midsummer blazing heat they could not obtain cold water; hungry and thirsty they drifted apart.
translations.idiomatic: and in midsummer heat no clean water—hunger, thirst, and misery.

sentences.zh: 上以前移宮人及侍臣，不得以穀米自隨，入門有禁防，不得出市，困乏，使就傕索粳米五斛，牛骨五具，欲為食賜宮人左右。

translations.literal: Because earlier when moving palace the palace women and attending ministers could not bring grain and rice with them, entering the gate there were prohibitions and they could not go out to market; distressed, he ordered them to go to Jue and beg five hu of polished rice and five sets of ox bones, wishing to make food to bestow on palace attendants left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier moves had stripped the court of provisions; the gates were locked so none could buy food. The emperor begged Li Jue for five hu of rice and five ox skeletons to feed his starving household—

sentences.zh: 傕不與米，取乆牛肉牛骨給，皆已臭蟲，不可啖食。」〉

translations.literal: Jue did not give rice but took long-stored beef and ox bones to supply them—all already stinking with maggots, inedible."〉
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue sent rotten meat and worm-eaten bones instead."〉

sentences.zh: 尋復欲徙帝於池陽黃白城，

translations.literal: Soon he again wished to move the emperor to the Huangbai walled town in Chiyang,
translations.idiomatic: He next threatened to march the throne to the Huangbai stockade in Chiyang—

sentences.zh: 〈池陽，縣，故城在今涇陽縣西北。〉

translations.literal: 〈Chiyang is a county; the old walled city is now northwest of Jingyang county.〉
translations.idiomatic: modern northwest of Jingyang County.〉

sentences.zh: 君臣惶懼。

translations.literal: Lord and ministers were frightened.
translations.idiomatic: court and emperor were terrified.

sentences.zh: 司徒趙溫深解譬之，乃止。

translations.literal: Minister Zhao Wen deeply explained and admonished him, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhao Wen argued him out of it.

sentences.zh: 詔遣謁者僕射皇甫酈和傕﹑汜。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Supervisor of the Household Huangfu Li to reconcile Jue and Si.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Huangfu Li, supervisor of the household, to mediate between Li Jue and Guo Si.

sentences.zh: 酈先譬汜，汜即從命。

translations.literal: Li first admonished Si; Si immediately followed the command.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Li won over Guo Si first; he yielded at once.

sentences.zh: 又詣傕，傕不聽。

translations.literal: He also went to Jue; Jue would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue would not hear him out.

sentences.zh: 曰：「郭多，盜馬虜耳，何敢欲與我同邪！

translations.literal: He said: "Guo Duo is a horse-thieving captive—how dare he wish to be my equal!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue snarled that "Guo Duo"—Guo Si—was a horse-thieving captive who dared rival him,

sentences.zh: 必誅之。

translations.literal: I must execute him.
translations.idiomatic: and must die for it,

sentences.zh: 君觀我方略士眾，足辦郭多不？

translations.literal: Sir, look at my strategy and soldiers—are they enough to deal with Guo Duo or not?"
translations.idiomatic: then dared Huangfu Li to judge whether his host could crush Guo Si.

sentences.zh: 多又劫質公卿。

translations.literal: Duo again has seized the dukes and ministers hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si had taken ministers hostage,

sentences.zh: 所為如是，而君苟欲左右之邪！」

translations.literal: He acts thus, yet you, sir, care to assist him on both sides!"
translations.idiomatic: yet Li accused the envoy of siding with the villain."

sentences.zh: 〈左右，助也，音佐又。〉

translations.literal: 〈Zuo-you means to assist; read zuo you again.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zuo-you here means "to favor" or "assist."〉

sentences.zh: 汜一名多。

translations.literal: Si's other name was Duo.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si's childhood name was Duo.

sentences.zh: 酈曰：「今汜質公卿，而將軍脅主，誰輕重乎？

translations.literal: Li said: "Now Si holds the dukes and ministers hostage while the general coerces the master—which side is lighter or heavier?"
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Li shot back, "Guo Si holds hostages while you hold the emperor—which is the graver crime?"

sentences.zh: 」傕怒，呵遣酈，因令虎賁王昌追殺之。

translations.literal: " Jue was angry, shouted to dismiss Li, and thereupon ordered Rapid as Tigers Wang Chang to pursue and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue raged, ordered Huangfu Li driven off, and sent guards to kill him.

sentences.zh: 昌偽不及，酈得以免。

translations.literal: Chang feigned not to overtake him; Li thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang deliberately let him escape.

sentences.zh: 傕乃自為大司馬。

translations.literal: Jue thereupon himself became Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue then named himself grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：「傕性喜鬼怪左道之術，常有道人及女巫歌謳擊鼓下神祭，六丁符劾厭勝之具，無所不為。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi qiju zhu states: "Jue's nature delighted in ghostly left-path arts; constantly there were Daoists and witch women singing, beating drums, descending gods, sacrificing, six-ding talismans, spell-binding, apotropaics—nothing he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: The court diary describes Li Jue's obsession with shamans, witches, six-ding charms, and every species of occult trick—

sentences.zh: 又於朝廷省門外為董卓作神坐，數以牛羊祠之。

translations.literal: Moreover outside the court hall gate he made a spirit seat for Dong Zhuo and repeatedly sacrificed oxen and sheep to him.
translations.idiomatic: outside the ministry gates he even set up a spirit throne to Dong Zhuo and sacrificed cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 天子使左中郎將李國持節拜傕為大司馬，在三公之右。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the Left Li Guo bearing credentials to invest Jue as Grand Marshal, to the right of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was forced to send Li Guo with the seal of grand marshal, ranking Li Jue above the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 傕自以為得鬼神之助，乃厚賜諸巫。」〉

translations.literal: Jue himself thought he had obtained the ghosts' and spirits' aid, and thereupon richly rewarded the various shamans."〉
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue believed the spirits favored him and heaped gold on his witches."〉

sentences.zh: 與郭汜相攻連月，死者以萬數。

translations.literal: He and Guo Si attacked each other for successive months; the dead numbered in the myriads.
translations.idiomatic: Their civil war raged for months and cost tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 張濟自陝來和解二人，仍欲遷帝權幸弘農。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji came from Shan to reconcile the two men, and still wished to move the emperor by authority to favor Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji rode from Shan to broker peace and urged moving the court east toward Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 帝亦思舊京，因遣使敦請傕求東歸，十反乃許。

translations.literal: The emperor also longed for the old capital; thereupon he sent envoys earnestly requesting Jue to seek eastward return; after ten rounds he consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself longed for Luoyang and sent ten embassies before Li Jue agreed to let the cortège leave.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《紀》曰：「濟使太官令孫篤、校尉張式宣諭十反。」〉

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Annals states: "Ji ordered Grand Provisioner Sun Du and Colonel Zhang Shi to proclaim and instruct ten times."〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong records that Zhang Ji had Sun Du and Zhang Shi repeat the plea ten times.〉

sentences.zh: 車駕即日發邁。

translations.literal: The carriage host that day set out.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train set out the same day.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：「初，天子出，到宣平門，當度橋，汜兵數百人遮橋曰：『是天子非？

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi qiju zhu states: "At first when the Son of Heaven went out, reaching Xuanyi Gate, about to cross the bridge, several hundred of Si's soldiers blocked the bridge saying: 'Is this the Son of Heaven or not?
translations.idiomatic: The diary describes the cortège halted at Xuanyi Gate by hundreds of Guo Si's men shouting, "Is this really the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 』車不得前。

translations.literal: The carriage could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The chariots could not pass.

sentences.zh: 傕兵數百人皆持大戟在乘輿車前，侍中劉艾大呼云：『是天子也！

translations.literal: Several hundred of Jue's soldiers all grasped great halberds before the imperial carriage; Palace Attendant Liu Ai loudly cried: "It is the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue's halberdiers ringed the imperial car while Liu Ai roared, "It is the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 』使侍中楊琦高舉車帷。

translations.literal: He ordered Palace Attendant Yang Qi to raise high the carriage curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yang Qi was told to lift the curtain so all could see the imperial face.

sentences.zh: 帝言諸兵：『汝却，何敢迫近至尊邪！

translations.literal: The emperor addressed the various soldiers: "You withdraw—how dare you press close on the supreme one!"
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor leaned out and shouted, "Stand back—you dare crowd your sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 』汜等兵乃却。

translations.literal: Si's soldiers thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si's men fell back.

sentences.zh: 旣度橋，士衆咸稱萬歲。」〉

translations.literal: Having crossed the bridge, soldiers and hosts all cried "Ten thousand years.""〉
translations.idiomatic: Once the bridge was crossed the whole army shouted long life."〉

sentences.zh: 李傕出屯曹陽。

translations.literal: Li Jue went out to encamp at Caoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue encamped at Caoyang.

sentences.zh: 以張濟為驃騎將軍，復還屯陝。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji was made General of Agile Cavalry and again returned to encamp at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji was named general of agile cavalry and went back to Shan.

sentences.zh: 遷郭汜車騎將軍，楊定後將軍，楊奉興義將軍。

translations.literal: Guo Si was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Yang Ding General of the Rear, Yang Feng General Who Raises Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si became general of chariots and cavalry, Yang Ding general of the rear, Yang Feng general who raises righteousness.

sentences.zh: 又以故牛輔部曲董承為安集將軍。

translations.literal: Also Niu Fu's former subordinate Dong Cheng was made General Who Pacifies and Gathers.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng, once Niu Fu's officer, was named general who pacifies and gathers.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀志》曰：「承，獻帝舅也。

translations.literal: 〈The Shu Records states: "Cheng was the Son of Heaven's uncle by marriage."
translations.idiomatic: The Shu zhi calls Dong Cheng the emperor's uncle by marriage—

sentences.zh: 」裴松之注曰：「承，靈帝母太后之姪。」〉

translations.literal: " Pei Songzhi's note states: "Cheng was the nephew of Empress Dowager Dong, the Lingdi emperor's mother."〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi identifies him as a nephew of Empress Dowager Dong."〉

sentences.zh: 汜等並侍送乘輿。

translations.literal: Si and the others together attended and escorted the carriage host.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si and the other warlords escorted the train.

sentences.zh: 汜遂復欲脅帝幸郿，定﹑奉﹑承不聽。

translations.literal: Si thereupon again wished to coerce the emperor to favor Mei; Ding, Feng, and Cheng would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si tried again to drag the court toward Mei; Yang Ding, Yang Feng, and Dong Cheng blocked him.

sentences.zh: 汜恐變生，乃弃軍還就李傕。

translations.literal: Si feared change would arise; thereupon abandoned the army and returned to join Li Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a coup, Guo Si abandoned his command and fled back to Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 車駕進至華陰。

translations.literal: The carriage host advanced to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial procession reached Huayin.

sentences.zh: 〈《帝王紀》曰：「帝以尚書郎郭溥喻汜，汜以屯部未定，乞須留之。

translations.literal: 〈The Diwang ji states: "The emperor ordered Masters of Writing Gentleman Guo Pu to instruct Si; Si said his encampment was not yet settled and begged to detain him awhile.
translations.idiomatic: The Diwang ji says the emperor sent Guo Pu to reason with Guo Si, who asked for more time to break camp—

sentences.zh: 溥因罵汜曰：『卿真庸人賤夫，為國上將，今天子有命，何須留之？

translations.literal: Pu thereupon reviled Si saying: "You are truly a base fellow and mean man; as a general of the state, when the Son of Heaven has a command, why must you detain him?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu called him a craven who disobeyed an imperial order,

sentences.zh: 吾不忍見卿所行，請先殺我，以章卿惡。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to see what you do—I beg first to kill me, to display your wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: begging Guo Si to kill him instead to expose his villainy,

sentences.zh: 』汜得溥言切，意乃少喻。」〉

translations.literal: Si, obtaining Pu's cutting words, his intent was somewhat enlightened."〉
translations.idiomatic: until Guo Si, stung by the rebuke, relented slightly."〉

sentences.zh: 寧輯將軍段煨乃具服御及公卿以下資儲，請帝幸其營。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies and Harmonizes Duan Wei thereupon fully provided carriages and horses and supplies for the emperor down to the dukes and ministers, begging the emperor to favor his camp.
translations.idiomatic: General Duan Wei offered full transport and provisions for emperor and ministers and invited the court into his camp.

sentences.zh: 初，楊定與煨有隙，遂誣煨欲反，乃攻其營，十餘日不下。

translations.literal: At the beginning Yang Ding had a rift with Wei; thereupon slandered Wei as wishing to rebel, thereupon attacked his camp; more than ten days and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding, who hated Duan Wei, accused him of treason and besieged his camp for ten days without success.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《紀》曰：「煨與楊定有隙，煨迎乘輿，不敢下馬，揖馬上。

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Annals states: "Wei and Yang Ding had a rift; when Wei welcomed the carriage host he did not dare dismount but bowed from the horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong notes that Duan Wei, feuding with Yang Ding, greeted the emperor from horseback—

sentences.zh: 侍中种輯素與定親，乃言曰：『段煨欲反。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhong Ji, who had always been intimate with Ding, thereupon spoke saying: 'Duan Wei wishes to rebel.'
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhong Ji, Yang Ding's friend, whispered that Duan Wei meant treason,

sentences.zh: 』上曰：『煨屬來迎，何謂反？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Wei has come to welcome—why call it rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: but the emperor answered, "He came to welcome us—where is the treason?"

sentences.zh: 』對曰：『迎不至界，拜不下馬，其色變，必有異心。

translations.literal: He replied: 'He did not come to the border to meet you, did not dismount from his horse to bow, his expression changed—he must harbor a different mind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ji said he had not met the train at the border, had not dismounted, and his face betrayed guilt,

sentences.zh: 』太尉楊彪等曰：『煨不反，臣等敢以死保，車駕可幸其營。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yang Biao and others said: 'Wei does not rebel—we dare guarantee it with our lives; the carriage host may favor his camp.
translations.idiomatic: while Yang Biao swore with his life that Duan Wei was loyal and safe to join,

sentences.zh: 』董承、楊定言曰：『郭汜今且將七百騎來入煨營。

translations.literal: Dong Cheng and Yang Ding said: 'Guo Si is about to lead seven hundred cavalry into Wei's camp.'
translations.idiomatic: until Dong Cheng and Yang Ding lied that Guo Si was riding in with seven hundred horse to attack Duan Wei,

sentences.zh: 』天子信之，遂露次於道南，奉、承、定等功也。」〉

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven believed it, thereupon bivouacked in the open south of the road—the achievement of Feng, Cheng, and Ding."〉
translations.idiomatic: which frightened the emperor into camping in the open—the work of Yang Feng, Dong Cheng, and Yang Ding."〉

sentences.zh: 而煨猶奉給御膳，稟贍百官，終無二意。

translations.literal: Yet Wei still supplied imperial meals and issued rations to the hundred officials, to the end without a second intent.
translations.idiomatic: Through it all Duan Wei fed the emperor and paid the ministers, never wavering in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 李傕、郭汜既悔令天子東，乃來救段煨，因欲劫帝而西，楊定為汜所遮，亡奔荊州。

translations.literal: Li Jue and Guo Si, having regretted letting the Son of Heaven go east, thereupon came to rescue Duan Wei and by the way wished to seize the emperor to go west; Yang Ding was blocked by Si and fled to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si regretted releasing the court, marched to "relieve" Duan Wei, and tried to drag the emperor west again; Yang Ding, cut off by Guo Si, fled to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 而張濟與楊奉﹑董承不相平，乃反合傕﹑汜，共追乘輿，大戰於弘農東澗。

translations.literal: But Zhang Ji was not on good terms with Yang Feng and Dong Cheng; thereupon he reversed and united with Jue and Si, together pursuing the carriage host, and fought a great battle at the eastern ravine of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, feuding with Yang Feng and Dong Cheng, switched sides to Li Jue and Guo Si; together they overtook the imperial train and fought a great battle in the eastern defile of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 承﹑奉軍敗，百官士卒死者不可勝數，皆弃其婦女輜重，御物符策典籍，略無所遺。

translations.literal: Cheng and Feng's army was defeated; officials and soldiers who died could not be counted; all abandoned their women, baggage trains, imperial goods, tallies, registers, and canonical texts—almost nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng and Yang Feng were routed. Officials and troops died in heaps, abandoning women, wagons, regalia, tallies, and books until scarcely a scrap was left.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝傳》曰：「掠婦女衣被，遲違不時解，即斫刺之。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi zhuan states: "They plundered women's clothing and quilts; if they were slow and did not promptly strip them, they hacked and stabbed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi zhuan says the victors stripped women of their clothes and murdered any who hesitated—

sentences.zh: 有美髮者斷取。

translations.literal: Those with beautiful hair they cut and took.
translations.idiomatic: those with fine hair had it sheared off as trophies—

sentences.zh: 凍死及嬰兒隨流而浮者塞水。」〉

translations.literal: Those frozen to death and infants floating with the current filled the water."〉
translations.idiomatic: while frozen corpses and baby bodies choked the stream."〉

sentences.zh: 射聲校尉沮儁被創墜馬。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at a Sound Ju Jun, wounded, fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Jun, colonel of the archers who shoot at a sound, was wounded and tumbled from the saddle.

sentences.zh: 李傕謂左右曰：「尚可活不？

translations.literal: Li Jue said to those at his side: "Can he still be kept alive?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue asked his men whether Ju Jun could still be saved.

sentences.zh: 」儁罵之曰：「汝等凶逆，逼迫天子，亂臣賊子，未有如汝者！

translations.literal: Jun reviled them saying: "You are fierce rebels, coercing the Son of Heaven—disorderly ministers and villainous sons—none have been like you!
translations.idiomatic: Ju Jun cursed them: "You are traitors who bully the Son of Heaven—there has never been a viler pack of rebel ministers!"

sentences.zh: 」傕使殺之。

translations.literal: " Jue ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue had him executed.

sentences.zh: 〈袁山松《書》曰：「儁年二十五，其督戰訾寶負其尸而瘞之。」〉

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Shansong's Book states: "Jun was twenty-five years old; his battle supervisor Zi Bao bore his corpse away and buried him."〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shansong records that Ju Jun was twenty-five and that his adjutant Zi Bao recovered and buried his body.〉

sentences.zh: 天子遂露次曹陽。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven thereupon bivouacked in the open at Caoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was forced to camp in the open at Caoyang.

sentences.zh: 承、奉乃譎傕等與連和，而密遣閒使至河東，招故白波帥李樂、韓暹、胡才及南匈奴右賢王去卑，並率其眾數千騎來，與承、奉共擊傕等，大破之，斬首數千級，乘輿乃得進。

translations.literal: Cheng and Feng then deceived Jue and others into joining peace, while secretly sending a secret envoy to Hedong to summon the former White Wave chiefs Li Le, Han Xian, Hu Cai, and the Southern Xiongnu Worthy King of the Right Qubiji, who together led their hosts of several thousand cavalry to come; together with Cheng and Feng they struck Jue and others, greatly defeated them, beheading several thousand levels, and the carriage host was then able to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng and Yang Feng feigned a truce while secret messengers brought Li Le, Han Xian, Hu Cai, and the Xiongnu Worthy King Qubiji from Hedong with thousands of horsemen. With them they shattered Li Jue's army, took thousands of heads, and the imperial train rolled forward again.

sentences.zh: 董承、李樂擁衛左右，胡才、楊奉、韓暹、去卑為後距。

translations.literal: Dong Cheng and Li Le hugged and guarded left and right; Hu Cai, Yang Feng, Han Xian, and Qubiji formed the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng and Li Le shielded the flanks while Hu Cai, Yang Feng, Han Xian, and Qubiji covered the rear.

sentences.zh: 傕等復來戰，奉等大敗，死者甚於東澗。

translations.literal: Jue and others again came to fight; Feng and the others were greatly defeated; the dead were even more than at the eastern ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue counterattacked; Yang Feng's coalition collapsed with even heavier losses than at the eastern defile.

sentences.zh: 自東澗兵相連綴四十里中，方得至陝，乃結營自守。

translations.literal: From the eastern ravine soldiers strung together for forty li in the middle, only then did they reach Shan; thereupon they bound camps and guarded themselves.
translations.idiomatic: For forty li the retreating column was strung out under fire until it straggled into Shan, where the survivors threw up palisades.

sentences.zh: 時殘破之餘，虎賁羽林不滿百人，皆有離心。

translations.literal: At the time, in the aftermath of destruction, Rapid as Tigers and Feathered Forest did not fill a hundred men, and all had thoughts of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial bodyguard counted fewer than a hundred effectives, every man ready to desert.

sentences.zh: 承、奉等夜乃潛議過河，

translations.literal: Cheng, Feng, and others by night then secretly deliberated crossing the river,
translations.idiomatic: That night Dong Cheng, Yang Feng, and their allies plotted a secret crossing of the Yellow River,

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏紀曰：「傕、汜繞營叫呼，吏士失色，各有分散意。

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Annals states: "Jue and Si circled the camp shouting; clerks and soldiers lost color, each having thoughts of scattering.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong records Li Jue and Guo Si howling around the camp until the troops panicked—

sentences.zh: 李樂懼，欲令車駕御舡過砥柱，出盟津。

translations.literal: Li Le was afraid and wished to order the carriage host to take boats across the Zhuzhu pillar rocks and exit at Meng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Li Le wanted to float the court through the Zhuzhu rapids and out at Meng Ford—

sentences.zh: 楊彪曰：『臣弘農人也。

translations.literal: Yang Biao said: 'Your subject is a man of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao protested, "I am a son of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 自此以東，有三十六難，非萬乘所當登。

translations.literal: From here eastward there are thirty-six perils—not what a ten-thousand-chariot ruler ought to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: East of here lie thirty-six treacherous reaches—no place for an emperor's barge."

sentences.zh: 』宗正劉艾亦曰：『臣前為陝令，知其危險。

translations.literal: ' Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Ai also said: 'Your subject formerly was magistrate of Shan and knows its dangers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ai, director of the imperial clan, added, "I once governed Shan—I know those waters."

sentences.zh: 舊故河師，猶時有傾危，況今無師。

translations.literal: Even the old river pilots from time to time had overturning peril—how much more now with no pilots.
translations.idiomatic: Even veteran boatmen sometimes wreck there, let alone with none aboard."

sentences.zh: 太尉所慮是也。』」〉

translations.literal: What the Grand Commandant worries over is right.'"〉
translations.idiomatic: The grand commandant's fear is well founded.""〉

sentences.zh: 使李樂先度具舟舡，舉火為應。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Le first to cross and prepare boats and ships, raising fire as signal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Le was sent ahead to ready boats and signal with beacon fires.

sentences.zh: 帝步出營，臨河欲濟，岸高十餘丈，乃以絹縋而下。

translations.literal: The emperor on foot went out of the camp; coming to the river he wished to ford; the bank was more than ten zhang high; thereupon with silk cords they lowered him down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor walked out of the camp to the river, where banks rose ten zhang above the water; attendants lowered him on silk ropes.

sentences.zh: 〈縋音直類反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Zhui is read zhilei fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhui "lower on ropes" is read zhilei in fanqie.〉

sentences.zh: 餘人或匍匐岸側，或從上自投，死亡傷殘，不復相知。

translations.literal: The rest either crawled at the bank's side or threw themselves from above; dead, wounded, and maimed no longer knew one another.
translations.idiomatic: Others crawled along the cliff or leaped to their deaths until the living and dead could not be told apart.

sentences.zh: 爭赴舡者，不可禁制，董承以戈擊披之，斷手指於舟中者可掬。

translations.literal: Those who scrambled for the boats could not be restrained; Dong Cheng with a halberd struck and slashed them; severed fingers in the boat could be scooped up.
translations.idiomatic: A mob stormed the boats until Dong Cheng hacked at them with a halberd; severed fingers littered the hulls by the handful.

sentences.zh: 同濟唯皇后、宋貴人、

translations.literal: Those who crossed together were only the empress and Honored Lady Song,
translations.idiomatic: Only the empress and Honored Lady Song reached the far bank—

sentences.zh: 〈宋貴人名都，常山太守泓之女也。

translations.literal: 〈Honored Lady Song's name was Du; she was the daughter of Grand Administrator Hong of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Lady Song—personal name Du—was a daughter of Grand Administrator Hong of Changshan—

sentences.zh: 見獻帝起居注。〉

translations.literal: See the Xiandi qiju zhu.〉
translations.idiomatic: according to the imperial diary.〉

sentences.zh: 楊彪、董承及后父執金吾伏完等數十人。

translations.literal: Yang Biao, Dong Cheng, and the empress's father Bearer of the Gilded Mace Fu Wan and several tens of others.
translations.idiomatic: together with Yang Biao, Dong Cheng, and the empress's father Fu Wan, bearer of the gilded mace, and a few dozen courtiers.

sentences.zh: 其宮女皆為傕兵所掠奪，凍溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The palace women were all plundered by Jue's soldiers; those who froze or drowned were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Every palace woman left behind was seized by Li Jue's men; countless froze or drowned.

sentences.zh: 既到大陽，止於人家，

translations.literal: Having reached Dayang, they stopped in a commoner's house,
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Dayang in a private home,

sentences.zh: 〈大陽，縣，屬河東郡。

translations.literal: 〈Dayang is a county belonging to Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dayang County lay in Hedong—

sentences.zh: 前書音義曰「在大河之陽」也。

translations.literal: The Former Documents Sound and Meaning says "on the great river's north [yang] side."
translations.idiomatic: the Han shu gloss explains the name as "north of the great river."

sentences.zh: 即今陝州河北縣是也。

translations.literal: It is now Hebei county in Shan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is Hebei County on the north shore of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 《十三州記》曰：「傅巖在其界，今住穴尚存。」〉

translations.literal: The Record of the Thirteen Provinces states: "Fu Yan is within its border; the dwelling cave still exists today."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Shisan zhou ji notes that Fu Yan's cliff is in the same district, with his cave still visible."〉

sentences.zh: 然後幸李樂營。

translations.literal: Only then did he favor Li Le's camp.
translations.idiomatic: From there the emperor moved to Li Le's camp.

sentences.zh: 百官飢餓，河內太守張楊

translations.literal: The hundred officials were hungry; Grand Administrator of Henei Zhang Yang
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were starving when Grand Administrator Zhang Yang of Henei

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰：「楊字稚叔，雲中人。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states: "Yang, courtesy name Zhishu, was a man of Yunzhong."〉
translations.idiomatic: the Wei zhi describes as Zhang Yang, style Zhishu, from Yunzhong—〉

sentences.zh: 使數千人負米貢餉。

translations.literal: sent several thousand men carrying rice to present as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: sent several thousand porters with grain as tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝乃御牛車，因都安邑。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon rode an ox cart and thereby made his capital at Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode in an oxcart to Anyi, which became the temporary capital.

sentences.zh: 河東太守王邑奉獻綿帛，悉賦公卿以下。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Hedong Wang Yi presented tribute of floss silk and silk; all was distributed to the dukes and ministers downward.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Wang Yi of Hedong sent silk, which was shared out among the high ministers down to the lowest rank.

sentences.zh: 封邑為列侯，

translations.literal: Yi was enfeoffed full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was enfeoffed as a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 〈邑字文都，北地涇陽人，鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: 〈Yi, courtesy name Wendu, was a man of Jingyang in Beidi, General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was Wang Yi, style Wendu, of Jingyang in Beidi, later general who guards the north—

sentences.zh: 見同歲名。〉

translations.literal: See the tongsui ming register.〉
translations.idiomatic: listed in the alumni roster of his examination year.〉

sentences.zh: 拜胡才征東將軍，張楊為安國將軍，皆假節、開府。

translations.literal: Hu Cai was appointed General Who Strikes the East; Zhang Yang was made General Who Pacifies the State; both were given credentials and opened bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Cai was named general who strikes the east, Zhang Yang general who pacifies the state; each received credentials and his own bureau.

sentences.zh: 其壘壁群豎，競求拜職，刻印不給，至乃以錐畫之。

translations.literal: The chiefs of stockades and ramparts vied to seek appointments; carving seals could not keep up—to the extent of scratching them with an awl.
translations.idiomatic: Every petty warlord clamored for a commission; seal engravers could not keep pace and scratched titles with awls.

sentences.zh: 或齎酒肉就天子燕飲。

translations.literal: Some carried wine and meat to join the Son of Heaven in feasting and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Some shouldered wine and meat into the emperor's presence for drunken revels.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰「乘輿時居棘籬中，門戶無關閉，天子與羣臣會，兵士伏籬上觀，互相鎮壓以為笑。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states "The carriage host at times dwelt inside a thorn hedge; doors and gates had no bars; the Son of Heaven met with the host of nobles while soldiers lay atop the hedge watching, mutually pressing one another for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei zhi says the court huddled inside a briar fence with unbarred doors while soldiers sprawled on the hedge to gawk and jostle for sport—

sentences.zh: 諸將或遣婢詣省問，或齎酒送天子，侍中不通，喧呼罵詈」也。〉

translations.literal: The generals sometimes sent maids to the secretariat on business, or carried wine to present to the Son of Heaven; the palace attendant would not pass them through, and they shouted abuse" and so forth.〉
translations.idiomatic: generals sent servant girls to the ministries or barged in with wine until attendants blocked them and brawls broke out."〉

sentences.zh: 又遣太僕韓融至弘農，與傕、汜等連和。

translations.literal: Moreover he sent Grand Coach Han Rong to Hongnong to join peace with Jue, Si, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coach Han Rong was sent to Hongnong to negotiate peace with Li Jue and Guo Si.

sentences.zh: 傕乃放遣公卿百官，頗歸宮人婦女，及乘輿器服。

translations.literal: Jue thereupon released the dukes and hundred officials, to a degree returned palace women, and restored carriage goods and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue then freed the ministers, returned some palace ladies, and sent back part of the imperial baggage.

sentences.zh: 初，帝入關，三輔戶口尚數十萬，自傕汜相攻，天子東歸後，長安城空四十餘日，強者四散，羸者相食，二三年閒，關中無復人跡。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the emperor entered the passes, the Three Adjuncts' registered households were still several hundred thousand; from the time Jue and Si attacked each other, after the Son of Heaven returned east, the Chang'an city was empty forty-odd days; the strong scattered in four directions, the weak mutually ate one another; within two or three years, within the passes there was again no trace of people.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first entered the passes Guanzhong still counted hundreds of thousands of households. After Li Jue and Guo Si tore the region apart and the court fled east, Chang'an stood empty for forty days: the fit scattered while the weak cannibalized one another until, within two or three years, no human footprint remained in the heartland.

sentences.zh: 建安元年春，諸將爭權，韓暹遂攻董承，承奔張楊，楊乃使承先繕修洛宮。

translations.literal: In the first Jian'an year, spring, the generals vied for power; Han Xian thereupon attacked Dong Cheng; Cheng fled to Zhang Yang, and Yang thereupon ordered Cheng first to repair and restore the Luo palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Jian'an the warlords quarreled; Han Xian attacked Dong Cheng, who fled to Zhang Yang. Zhang Yang put him to work restoring the Luoyang palaces.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝還至洛陽，幸楊安殿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the emperor returned to Luoyang and favored Yang'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor reached Luoyang and took up residence in Yang'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 張楊以為己功，故因以「楊」名殿。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang took it as his own achievement; therefore he used "Yang" to name the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang named the hall for himself—Yang'an, "Yang's peace."

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：「舊時宮殿悉壞，倉卒之際，拾摭故瓦材木，工匠無法度之制，所作並無足觀也。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi qiju zhu states: "Formerly the palaces and halls were all ruined; in the hasty interval they gathered old tiles and timber; workmen had no regulated standards; what was made was altogether not worth viewing."〉
