translations.idiomatic: The court diary admits the rebuilt halls were a patchwork of scavenged tile and timber, built to no plan and scarcely presentable.〉

sentences.zh: 乃謂諸將曰：「天子當與天下共之，朝廷自有公卿大臣，楊當出扞外難，何事京師？

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to the various generals: "The Son of Heaven ought to be shared with all under Heaven; the court has its own dukes and great ministers—I ought to go out and ward off external peril—what business have I in the capital?
translations.idiomatic: He told the other generals, "The emperor belongs to the realm, not to me; Luoyang has its own ministers. I belong on the frontier warding off invaders, not loafing in the capital."

sentences.zh: 」遂還野王。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he returned to Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: With that he withdrew to Yewang.

sentences.zh: 楊奉亦出屯梁。

translations.literal: Yang Feng also went out to encamp at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng marched out to camp at Liang.

sentences.zh: 乃以張楊為大司馬，楊奉為車騎將軍，韓暹為大將軍，領司隸校尉，皆假節鉞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Yang was made Grand Marshal, Yang Feng General of Chariots and Cavalry, Han Xian Grand General, concurrently Colonel Director of Retainers—all were given credentials and axes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang became grand marshal, Yang Feng general of chariots and cavalry, Han Xian grand general with concurrent colonelship of the metropolitan region; each received the axe of command.

sentences.zh: 暹與董承並留宿衛。

translations.literal: Xian together with Dong Cheng both remained as night guards.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian and Dong Cheng stayed behind as night guards.

sentences.zh: 暹矜功恣睢，

translations.literal: Xian was arrogant over merit and acted wilfully,
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian swaggered on the strength of his past service,

sentences.zh: 〈恣睢，自任用之貌。

translations.literal: 〈Zisui is the appearance of self-willed use.
translations.idiomatic: zisui describes a man who follows only his own whim—

sentences.zh: 睢音火季反。〉

translations.literal: Sui is read huoji fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: sui is read huoji in fanqie.〉

sentences.zh: 干亂政事，董承患之，潛召兗州牧曹操。

translations.literal: meddled with and disordered government affairs; Dong Cheng was troubled by it and secretly summoned Governor of Yan province Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: meddled in policy until Dong Cheng, alarmed, secretly summoned Cao Cao, governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 操乃詣闕貢獻，稟公卿以下，因奏韓暹、張楊之罪。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon went to the palace gate to present tribute, reported to the dukes and ministers downward, and thereupon memorialized the crimes of Han Xian and Zhang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appeared at court with gifts, paid his respects to the ministers, and memorialized the crimes of Han Xian and Zhang Yang.

sentences.zh: 暹懼誅，單騎奔楊奉。

translations.literal: Xian feared execution and, alone on horseback, fled to Yang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian, fearing arrest, galloped alone to Yang Feng.

sentences.zh: 帝以暹、楊有翼車駕之功，詔一切勿問。

translations.literal: The emperor because Xian and Yang had the merit of winging the carriage host, ordered that in all matters they not be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned them for shielding the throne during the flight.

sentences.zh: 於是封衛將軍董承、輔國將軍伏完等十餘人為列侯，贈沮儁為弘農太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he enfeoffed General Who Guards the Palace Dong Cheng, General Who Supports the State Fu Wan, and more than ten others as full marquises, and posthumously appointed Ju Jun Grand Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng was enfeoffed as general who guards the palace, Fu Wan as general who supports the state, and a dozen others as marquises; Ju Jun was honored posthumously as grand administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏紀曰：「誅議郎侯祈、尚書馮碩、侍中臺崇，討有罪也。

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Annals states: "They executed Gentleman Consultant Hou Qi, Masters of Writing Feng Shuo, Palace Attendant Tai Chong—punishing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong also records the execution of Hou Qi, Feng Shuo, and Tai Chong for conspiracy—

sentences.zh: 封衞將軍董承、輔國將軍伏完、侍中丁沖、种輯、尚書僕射鍾繇、尚書郭溥、御史中丞董芬、彭城相劉艾、馮翊韓斌、東郡太守楊衆、議郎羅邵、伏德、趙蕤為列侯，賞有功也。

translations.literal: They enfeoffed General Who Guards the Palace Dong Cheng, General Who Supports the State Fu Wan, Palace Attendant Ding Chong, Zhong Ji, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Zhong Yao, Masters of Writing Guo Pu, Palace Secretary Dong Fen, Chancellor of Pengcheng Liu Ai, Han Bin of Fengyi, Grand Administrator of Dong commandery Yang Zhong, Gentleman Consultants Luo Shao, Fu De, and Zhao Rui as full marquises—rewarding merit.
translations.idiomatic: while a long list of loyalists including Dong Cheng, Fu Wan, Ding Chong, Zhong Ji, Zhong Yao, Guo Pu, Dong Fen, Liu Ai, Han Bin, Yang Zhong, Luo Shao, Fu De, and Zhao Rui received marquisates for merit.

sentences.zh: 贈射聲校尉沮儁為弘農太守，旌死節也。」〉

translations.literal: They posthumously appointed Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at a Sound Ju Jun Grand Administrator of Hongnong—commending death for principle."〉
translations.idiomatic: Ju Jun was again posthumously named grand administrator of Hongnong to honor his martyrdom."〉

sentences.zh: 曹操以洛陽殘荒，遂移帝幸許。

translations.literal: Cao Cao because Luoyang was ruined and desolate, thereupon moved the emperor to favor Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Luoyang a ruin, Cao Cao transferred the court to Xu.

sentences.zh: 楊奉、韓暹欲要遮車駕，不及，曹操擊之，

translations.literal: Yang Feng and Han Xian wished to intercept the carriage host but did not overtake; Cao Cao struck them,
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng and Han Xian tried to cut off the train but arrived too late; Cao Cao attacked them,

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：「車駕出洛陽，自轘轅而東，楊奉、韓暹引軍追之。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiandi chunqiu states: "When the carriage host left Luoyang, east from Huanyuan, Yang Feng and Han Xian led troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiandi chunqiu describes the court leaving Luoyang east through Huanyuan with Yang Feng and Han Xian in pursuit—

sentences.zh: 輕騎旣至，操設伏兵要於陽城山峽中，大敗之。」〉

translations.literal: Light cavalry having arrived, Cao laid ambush troops to intercept them in the Yangcheng mountain defile and greatly defeated them."〉
translations.idiomatic: until Cao Cao's ambush in the Yangcheng gorge broke their light horse."〉

sentences.zh: 奉、暹奔袁術，遂縱暴楊、徐閒。

translations.literal: Feng and Xian fled to Yuan Shu, thereupon ran riot between Yang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The pair fled to Yuan Shu and raided across Yang and Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 明年，左將軍劉備誘奉斬之。

translations.literal: The next year, General of the Left Liu Bei lured Feng and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year General of the Left Liu Bei lured Yang Feng in and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 暹懼，走還并州，道為人所殺。

translations.literal: Xian was afraid, fled back to Bing province, and on the road was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian bolted for Bing province and was murdered on the road.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：「暹失奉，孤特，與千餘騎欲歸并州，為張宣所殺。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Jiuzhou chunqiu states: "Xian, having lost Feng, was isolated; with more than a thousand cavalry he wished to return to Bing province and was killed by Zhang Xuan."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jiuzhou chunqiu says Han Xian, abandoned by Yang Feng, tried to reach Bing with a thousand riders and fell to an officer named Zhang Xuan.〉

sentences.zh: 胡才、李樂留河東，才為怨家所害，樂自病死。

translations.literal: Hu Cai and Li Le remained in Hedong; Cai was harmed by a personal enemy, Le died of illness himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Cai stayed in Hedong and was killed by a private foe; Li Le died of sickness.

sentences.zh: 張濟飢餓，出至南陽，攻穰，戰死。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, hungry, went out to Nanyang, attacked Rang, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, starving, marched into Nanyang, besieged Rang, and died in the assault.

sentences.zh: 郭汜為其將伍習所殺。

translations.literal: Guo Si was killed by his officer Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si was murdered by his subordinate Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 三年，使謁者僕射裴茂詔關中諸將段煨等討李傕，夷三族。

translations.literal: In the third year he ordered Supervisor of the Household Pei Mao by edict to order the Guanzhong generals such as Duan Wei to attack Li Jue and exterminate three clans.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jian'an the court ordered Pei Mao to command Duan Wei and other Guanzhong generals to destroy Li Jue and extirpate his clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：「傕頭至，有詔高縣之。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe states: "When Jue's head arrived, there was an edict to hang it high."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe notes that Li Jue's head was hung on public display.〉

sentences.zh: 以段煨為安南將軍，封閺鄉侯。

translations.literal: Duan Wei was made General Who Pacifies the South and enfeoffed Marquis of Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wei was named general who pacifies the south and enfeoffed marquis of Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 〈闅鄉，今虢州縣也。

translations.literal: 〈Wenxiang is now a county in Guo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate centered on Wenxiang, in the old Guozhou region—

sentences.zh: 說文「闅」，今作「閿」，流俗誤也。〉

translations.literal: The Shuowen writes 闅; now it is written 閿—vulgar usage is mistaken.〉
translations.idiomatic: though vulgar texts often misspell the placename graph.〉

sentences.zh: 四年，張楊為其將楊醜所殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhang Yang was killed by his officer Yang Chou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jian'an Zhang Yang was assassinated by his officer Yang Chou.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰：「楊素與呂布善。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states: "Yang had always been on good terms with Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei zhi says Zhang Yang had long been Lü Bu's friend—

sentences.zh: 曹公之圍布，楊欲救之不能，乃出兵東巿，遙為之埶。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao besieged Bu, Yang wished to rescue him but could not; thereupon he sent troops east to the market, remotely making a show for him.
translations.idiomatic: when Cao Cao besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi, Zhang Yang tried to raise a relief column in the eastern market to distract the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 其將楊醜殺楊以應曹公。」〉

translations.literal: His officer Yang Chou killed Yang to respond to Lord Cao."〉
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chou slew him to curry favor with Cao Cao."〉

sentences.zh: 以董承為車騎將軍，開府。

translations.literal: Dong Cheng was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and opened a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng was promoted general of chariots and cavalry with his own bureau.

sentences.zh: 自都許之後，權歸曹氏，天子緫己，百官備員而已。

translations.literal: After the capital was established at Xu, power returned to the Cao clan; the Son of Heaven gathered himself in, and the hundred officials were mere filled posts.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court settled at Xu, real power passed to the Caos; the emperor ruled in name only and the ministries were hollow shells.

sentences.zh: 帝忌操專偪，乃密詔董承，使結天下義士共誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor resented Cao's exclusive pressure and thereupon secretly edicted Dong Cheng, ordering him to join righteous knights of all under Heaven to execute him together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, chafing at Cao Cao's grip, issued a secret belt edict to Dong Cheng, bidding him league loyalists across the realm to kill the warlord.

sentences.zh: 承遂與劉備同謀，未發，會備出征，承更與偏將軍王服、長水校尉种輯、議郎吳碩結謀。

translations.literal: Cheng thereupon plotted together with Liu Bei; before it issued, it happened that Bei went on campaign; Cheng further with Major General Wang Fu, Colonel of the Eternal Waters Zhong Ji, and Gentleman Consultant Wu Shuo knotted a plot.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng allied with Liu Bei, but before they could strike Liu Bei marched away; Dong Cheng then conspired with Wang Fu, Zhong Ji, and Wu Shuo to renew the plot.

sentences.zh: 事泄，承、服、輯、碩皆為操所誅。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Cheng, Fu, Ji, and Shuo were all executed by Cao.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered; Cao Cao executed Dong Cheng, Wang Fu, Zhong Ji, and Wu Shuo.

sentences.zh: 韓遂、馬騰

translations.literal: Han Sui; Ma Teng
translations.idiomatic: The narrative turns to Han Sui and Ma Teng.

sentences.zh: 韓遂與馬騰自還涼州，更相戰爭，乃下隴據關中。

translations.literal: Han Sui and Ma Teng from themselves returned to Liangzhou, mutually made war, then descended Long and occupied Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Liangzhou, Han Sui and Ma Teng turned on each other, then swept down Long Mountain to seize the Guanzhong plain.

sentences.zh: 操方事河北，慮其乘閒為亂，七年，乃拜騰征南將軍，遂征西將軍，並開府。

translations.literal: Cao Cao was at that time engaged north of the Yellow River and feared they would exploit a gap to make disorder; in the seventh year he therefore appointed Teng General Who Campaigns South and Sui General Who Campaigns West, both opening bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Busy with the Hebei campaigns, Cao Cao bought peace in the northwest: in the seventh year of Jian'an he named Ma Teng general who campaigns south and Han Sui general who campaigns west, each with his own staff.

sentences.zh: 後徵段煨為大鴻臚，病卒。

translations.literal: Later he summoned Duan Wei to be Grand Herald; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wei was later recalled as grand herald and died in office.

sentences.zh: 復徵馬騰為衛尉，封槐里侯。

translations.literal: Again he summoned Ma Teng to be Commandant of the Guards and enfeoffed him Marquis of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng was summoned to the capital as commandant of the guards and enfeoffed as marquis of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 騰乃應召，而留子超領其部曲。

translations.literal: Teng thereupon answered the summons but left his son Chao to command his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng obeyed the call but left his son Ma Chao in command of his army.

sentences.zh: 十六年，超與韓遂舉關中背曹操，操擊破之，遂、超敗走，騰坐夷三族。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Chao with Han Sui raised Guanzhong in rebellion against Cao Cao; Cao struck and broke them; Sui and Chao fled in defeat; Teng by judgment suffered extermination of three clans.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Ma Chao and Han Sui rebelled in Guanzhong against Cao Cao, were crushed, and fled; Ma Teng paid with the extermination of his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 超攻殺涼州刺史韋康，

translations.literal: Chao attacked and killed Inspector of Liangzhou Wei Kang,
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao besieged and killed Inspector Wei Kang of Liangzhou—

sentences.zh: 〈太僕端之子也。

translations.literal: 〈He was the son of Grand Coach Wei Duan.
translations.idiomatic: the son of Grand Coach Wei Duan—

sentences.zh: 弟誕，魏光祿大夫。〉

translations.literal: Younger brother Dan was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness in Wei.〉
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wei Dan later served Cao Wei as grand master of splendid happiness.〉

sentences.zh: 復據隴右。

translations.literal: Again he occupied Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao again dominated Longyou.

sentences.zh: 十九年，天水人楊阜破超，

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Yang Fu of Tianshui defeated Chao,
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Yang Fu of Tianshui broke Ma Chao's power,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰：「阜字義山，天水兾人也。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states: "Fu, courtesy name Yishan, was a man of Ji in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei zhi identifies Yang Fu, style Yishan, as a native of Ji in Tianshui—

sentences.zh: 韋康以為別駕。

translations.literal: Wei Kang had appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: whom Wei Kang had employed as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 馬超率萬餘人攻兾城，阜率國士大夫及宗族子弟勝兵者千餘人，使弟岳於城上作偃月營，與超接戰。

translations.literal: Ma Chao led more than ten thousand to attack Ji city; Fu led the state's gentlemen and clan youths who could bear arms, over a thousand, sent his younger brother Yue on the wall to form a crescent moon camp, and joined battle with Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao brought ten thousand men against Ji. Yang Fu rallied over a thousand gentry and kinsmen fit to bear arms, posted his brother Yang Yue on the walls in a crescent formation, and fought Ma Chao month after month.

sentences.zh: 自正月至八月拒守，而救兵不至。

translations.literal: From the first month to the eighth month they held the defense, but relief troops did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month through the eighth they held the walls, yet no relief column came.

sentences.zh: 超入，拘岳於兾，殺刺史太守。

translations.literal: Chao entered, detained Yue at Ji, and killed the inspector and grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Ma Chao seized Yang Yue and executed both the inspector and the grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 阜內有報超之志，而未得其便。

translations.literal: Fu inwardly harbored the will to avenge Chao but had not yet found the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu nursed a secret vow to destroy Ma Chao but waited for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 外兄姜敘屯歷城，阜少長詣敘家，見敘母，說前在兾中時事，歔欷悲甚。

translations.literal: His cousin Jiang Xu was encamped at Licheng; Fu, from youth grown up, went to Xu's home, saw Xu's mother, and spoke of what had happened before in Ji, weeping and sobbing in great grief.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Jiang Xu held Licheng. Yang Fu went to Jiang Xu's house, told Xu's mother the story of Ji's fall, and wept until she wept with him.

sentences.zh: 敘曰：『何為爾？

translations.literal: Xu said: "Why are you like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu asked why he wept so bitterly.

sentences.zh: 』阜曰：『守城不能完，君亡不能死，亦何面目以視息天下？

translations.literal: Fu said: "I could not preserve the city to completion; our lord perished and I could not die with him—what face have I to draw breath under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu answered, "I failed to save Ji or die with Wei Kang—what right have I to live?"

sentences.zh: 』時敘母慨然勑從阜計。

translations.literal: At that Xu's mother sighed greatly and ordered them to follow Fu's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu's mother rose, wiped her eyes, and bade them follow Yang Fu's plan.

sentences.zh: 超聞阜等兵起，自將出襲歷城，得敘母。

translations.literal: When Chao heard that Fu and others had raised troops, he personally led a force out to raid Licheng and captured Xu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao marched on Licheng and took Jiang Xu's mother hostage.

sentences.zh: 敘母罵之曰：『若背父之逆子，殺君之桀賊，天地豈乆容，敢以面目視人乎？

translations.literal: Xu's mother reviled him saying: "You unfilial son who betrayed your father, tyrant who murdered his lord—will Heaven and earth long endure you? How dare you show your face before men?"
translations.idiomatic: She screamed at him, "Patricide, regicide—how long will Heaven shelter you? How dare you look any honest man in the eye?"

sentences.zh: 』超怒，殺之。

translations.literal: " Chao in anger killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao cut her down in fury.

sentences.zh: 阜與戰，身被五創，宗族昆季死者七人，超遂南奔張魯。」〉

translations.literal: Fu fought him; his body received five wounds; of his clan brothers seven died; Chao thereupon fled south to Zhang Lu."〉
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu gave battle, took five wounds, and lost seven kinsmen before Ma Chao broke and fled south to Zhang Lu."〉

sentences.zh: 超奔漢中，降劉備。

translations.literal: Chao fled to Hanzhong and surrendered to Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanzhong Ma Chao went over to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀志》曰：「超字孟起。

translations.literal: 〈The Shu Records states: "Chao, courtesy name Mengqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu zhi gives his style as Mengqi—

sentences.zh: 旣奔漢中，聞備圍劉璋於成都，密書請降。

translations.literal: Having fled to Hanzhong, he heard that Bei was besieging Liu Zhang at Chengdu and secretly sent a letter begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: while in Hanzhong he learned that Liu Bei was investing Chengdu and sent a secret offer of defection.

sentences.zh: 備遣迎超，將兵徑到城下。

translations.literal: Bei sent to welcome Chao; he led troops straight to the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei welcomed him; Ma Chao marched his column straight to Chengdu's gates.

sentences.zh: 漢中震怖，璋即稽首。」〉

translations.literal: Hanzhong trembled in terror; Zhang immediately bowed his head."〉
translations.idiomatic: The shock broke Liu Zhang's nerve and he capitulated at once."〉

sentences.zh: 韓遂走金城羌中，為其帳下所殺。

translations.literal: Han Sui fled to Jincheng among the Qiang and was killed by his tent followers.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui fled among the Jincheng Qiang and was murdered by his own men.

sentences.zh: 初，隴西人宗建在枹罕，自稱「河首平漢王」，

translations.literal: At the beginning, Zong Jian of Longxi at Fuhan styled himself "River-Head Prince Who Pacifies Han,"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Longxi adventurer named Zong Jian had seized Fuhan and styled himself "Prince Who Pacifies the Han from the River's Head,"

sentences.zh: 〈建以居河上流，故稱「河首」也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Because Jian dwelt upriver on the Yellow River he was called "river head."〉
translations.idiomatic: a boast drawn from his perch on the upper Yellow River.〉

sentences.zh: 署置百官三十許年。

translations.literal: He set up a full bureaucracy for some thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: where he played emperor for some thirty years.

sentences.zh: 曹操因遣夏侯淵擊建，斬之，涼州悉平。

translations.literal: Cao Cao thereupon sent Xiahou Yuan to strike Jian, beheaded him, and Liangzhou was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Yuan to crush him; Zong Jian died on the block and Liangzhou was quiet again.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰：「泉字妙才，沛國人也，為征西護軍，魏太祖使帥諸將討建，拔之。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states: "Yuan, courtesy name Miaocai, was a man of Pei; he was Colonel Protecting the West, and Wei Taizu ordered him to lead the various generals to attack Jian and capture him."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wei zhi credits Xiahou Yuan, style Miaocai of Pei, as the western shield colonel whom Cao Cao sent to take Zong Jian's stronghold.〉

sentences.zh: 論曰：董卓初以虓闞為情，

translations.literal: The evaluation states: Dong Zhuo at first made tiger-fierce rage his temper,
translations.idiomatic: The historian's verdict: Dong Zhuo began as a roaring tiger—

sentences.zh: 〈《詩·大雅》曰：「闞如虓虎。

translations.literal: 〈The Classic Poetry, "Da Ya," states: "Fierce as a roaring tiger."
translations.idiomatic: the Odes say "fierce as a roaring tiger"—

sentences.zh: 」毛傳曰：「虎怒之貌也。」〉

translations.literal: " The Mao commentary states: "The appearance of an angry tiger."〉
translations.idiomatic: Mao's gloss means a face twisted with animal fury.〉

sentences.zh: 因遭崩剝之埶，

translations.literal: and encountered the momentum of collapse and stripping.
translations.idiomatic: He rode the collapse of Han authority,

sentences.zh: 〈剝猶亂也。

translations.literal: 〈Bo means disorder.
translations.idiomatic: bo meaning "to strip away" or disorder—

sentences.zh: 《左傳》曰：「天實剝亂。」〉

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition states: "Heaven truly strips and disorders."〉
translations.idiomatic: as the Zuo zhuan says when Heaven unmakes a dynasty.〉

sentences.zh: 故得蹈藉彝倫，毀裂畿服。

translations.literal: Therefore he could trample the constant human relations and tear apart the royal domain and the nine zones.
translations.idiomatic: so he could trample every moral tie and rip the king's domain to shreds.

sentences.zh: 〈彝，常也。

translations.literal: 〈Yi means constant.
translations.idiomatic: Yi is "constant,"

sentences.zh: 倫，理也。

translations.literal: Lun means pattern.
translations.idiomatic: lun "pattern" or right order—

sentences.zh: 書云：「我不知其彝倫攸敘。

translations.literal: The Documents states: "I do not know how its constant patterns should be ordered."
translations.idiomatic: the Documents confess when the pattern of rule is lost—

sentences.zh: 」《左傳》曰：「裂冠毀冕。

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition states: "Tearing caps and destroying crowns."
translations.idiomatic: the Zuo zhuan speaks of tearing caps and smashing crowns—

sentences.zh: 」畿謂王畿也。

translations.literal: Ji means the king's domain.
translations.idiomatic: ji is the royal demesne around the capital,

sentences.zh: 服，九服也。〉

translations.literal: Fu means the nine service zones.〉
translations.idiomatic: fu the nine concentric zones of tribute.〉

sentences.zh: 夫以刳肝斮趾之性，

translations.literal: With a nature inclined to slice out livers and chop off toes,
translations.idiomatic: With a temper that flayed men as Zhou of Shang flayed men—

sentences.zh: 〈刳，剖也。

translations.literal: 〈Ku means to cut open.
translations.idiomatic: ku means to disembowel,

sentences.zh: 斮，斬也。

translations.literal: Zhuo means to sever.
translations.idiomatic: zhuo to hack off—

sentences.zh: 紂刳剔孕婦，剖比干之心，斮朝涉之脛。〉

translations.literal: Zhou cut open pregnant women, carved out Bi Gan's heart, and severed the morning ford-wader's shins."〉
translations.idiomatic: the tyrant Zhou's mutilations of the pregnant, of Bi Gan, of the river-crosser at dawn."〉

sentences.zh: 則群生不足以厭其快，然猶折意縉紳，遲疑陵奪，

translations.literal: then the myriad creatures were not enough to glut his pleasure—yet still he bent his will to the gentry, hesitated before usurpation,
translations.idiomatic: Not even endless cruelty could sate him—yet he still courted great ministers, still paused before claiming the throne,

sentences.zh: 〈折，屈也。

translations.literal: 〈Zhe means to bend.
translations.idiomatic: zhe meaning to force down his temper—

sentences.zh: 謂忍性屈情，擢用鄭泰、蔡邕、何顒、荀爽等。〉

translations.literal: It means he endured his nature and bent his feelings to promote Zheng Tai, Cai Yong, He Yong, Xun Shuang, and others.〉
translations.idiomatic: enough to elevate men such as Zheng Tai, Cai Yong, He Yong, and Xun Shuang.〉

sentences.zh: 尚有盜竊之道焉。

translations.literal: and still retained something of the robber's Way.
translations.idiomatic: so that even he still observed a bandit chieftain's code.

sentences.zh: 〈《莊子》曰：「跖之徒問於跖曰：『盜亦有道乎？

translations.literal: 〈The Zhuangzi states: "A disciple of Robber Zhi asked Zhi, 'Does the robber too have a Way?'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi's Robber Zhi lists the "Way" of brigandage—

sentences.zh: 』跖曰：『何適無有邪？

translations.literal: " Zhi said: 'Where can you go without it?
translations.idiomatic: the art of guessing a hoard,

sentences.zh: 夫妄意室中之藏，聖也；

translations.literal: To guess the hoard in the house is sagehood;
translations.idiomatic: of leading the rush in,

sentences.zh: 入先，勇也；

translations.literal: to enter first is courage;
translations.idiomatic: of covering the retreat,

sentences.zh: 出後，義也；

translations.literal: to exit last is righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: of knowing when to strike and when to quit,

sentences.zh: 知可否，智也；

translations.literal: to know what can and cannot be done is wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: of dividing spoils fairly—

sentences.zh: 分均，仁也：五者不備而能成大盜者，天下未之有也。』」〉

translations.literal: to divide evenly is benevolence: without these five no one under Heaven can become a great robber.'"〉
translations.idiomatic: five "virtues" without which no great outlaw succeeds."〉

sentences.zh: 及殘寇乘之，

translations.literal: When the remnant bandits rode the opportunity,
translations.idiomatic: When lesser wolves—Li Jue and Guo Si—

sentences.zh: 〈殘寇謂傕、汜等。〉

translations.literal: 〈"Remnant bandits" means Jue, Si, and the like.〉
translations.idiomatic: seized their chance,

sentences.zh: 倒山傾海，昆岡之火，自茲而焚，

translations.literal: they overturned mountains and poured out seas; the fire on Kunlun's slope—henceforth it burned,
translations.idiomatic: they overturned mountain and sea; the blaze on Kunlun's slope,

sentences.zh: 〈《書》曰：「火炎崑岡，玉石俱焚。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Documents states: "Fire blazes on Kun's slope; jade and stone burn together."〉
translations.idiomatic: where jade and common stone burn as one—

sentences.zh: 版蕩之篇，於焉而極。

translations.literal: and the poems of perdition reached their utmost here.
translations.idiomatic: found its image in the age of Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 〈《詩．大雅》曰：「上帝版版，下人卒癉。

translations.literal: 〈The Classic Poetry, "Da Ya," states: "God is contrary; the people below are all ill.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes' "God is contrary" and "How vast, High God"—

sentences.zh: 」毛萇注：「版，反也。

translations.literal: " Mao Chang's commentary: "Ban means contrary.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's gloss on ban,

sentences.zh: 癉，病也。

translations.literal: Dan means sick.
translations.idiomatic: dan as sickness—

sentences.zh: 言厲王為政，反先王之道，下人盡病也。

translations.literal: It means that King Li's government reversed the way of former kings and the people below were all sick."
translations.idiomatic: King Li's misrule—

sentences.zh: 」又《蕩之什》曰：「蕩蕩上帝，下人之辟，疾威上帝，其命多辟。

translations.literal: " Also the "Dang" ode states: "Vast, vast High God—the people below are wicked; swift and terrible High God—his commands are many and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: the "Dang" ode's vision of lawless Heaven—

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「蕩蕩，法度廢壞之貌。」〉

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "Dangdang is the appearance of laws ruined and broken."〉
translations.idiomatic: all describe an age as broken as this."〉

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，人之生也難矣！

translations.literal: Alas—human life is indeed hard!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—human life is a brittle thing.

sentences.zh: 〈《左傳》曰：「人生實難，其有不獲死乎？」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Zuo Tradition states: "Human life is truly hard—is there not the failure to obtain death?"〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo zhuan asks whether death itself is not sometimes denied the suffering.〉

sentences.zh: 天地之不仁甚矣！

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are unkind in the extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth seem heartless indeed.

sentences.zh: 〈《老子》曰：「天地不仁，以萬物為芻狗。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Laozi states: "Heaven and earth are not benevolent; they treat the myriad things as straw dogs."〉
translations.idiomatic: Laozi says they treat all creatures as straw dogs.〉

sentences.zh: 贊曰：百六有會，

translations.literal: The encomium states: The hundred-six cycle has its conjunction,
translations.idiomatic: The closing hymn: When the hundred-six calamity falls—

sentences.zh: 〈前書《音義》曰：「四千五百歲為一元，一元之中有九戹，陽戹五，陰戹四。

translations.literal: 〈The Former Documents Sound and Meaning states: "Four thousand five hundred years make one yuan; within one yuan there are nine e; five are yang e and four are yin e.
translations.idiomatic: Han glosses explain that every forty-five centuries form a cosmic "yuan" riven by nine disasters—

sentences.zh: 陽為旱，陰為水。

translations.literal: Yang means drought; yin means flood.
translations.idiomatic: five yang scourges of drought, four yin scourges of flood—

sentences.zh: 」初入元百六歲有陽戹，故曰「百六之會」。〉

translations.literal: " At the first entry into a yuan, at the hundred-sixth year there is a yang e; therefore it is called "the hundred-six conjunction."〉
translations.idiomatic: and the hundred-sixth year of the cycle marks the deadliest yang e, the "hundred-six meeting."〉

sentences.zh: 過、剝成災。

translations.literal: Excess and stripping become calamity.
translations.idiomatic: —the hexagrams of Excess and Stripping spell ruin.

sentences.zh: 〈《易》曰大過：「棟撓，本末弱也。

translations.literal: 〈The Changes, Da guo: "The ridge-beam bends; root and tip are weak."
translations.idiomatic: The Da guo hexagram warns that the ridge-pole sags—

sentences.zh: 」剝：「不利有攸往，小人長也。」〉

translations.literal: " Bo: "Unfavorable to have somewhere to go; the little man grows.""〉
translations.idiomatic: Bo that the petty man waxes while the roof falls."〉

sentences.zh: 董卓滔天，干逆三才。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo overflowed heaven and violated the three powers.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo swelled until he drowned Heaven, Earth, and Man.

sentences.zh: 〈滔，漫也。

translations.literal: 〈Tao means to flood.
translations.idiomatic: Tao means to overspread,

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「象龔滔天。」〉

translations.literal: The Documents states: "Xiang and Gong flooded to Heaven."〉
translations.idiomatic: as the Documents say of the flood ministers.〉

sentences.zh: 方夏崩沸，

translations.literal: The four quarters and Hua-Xia boiled over;
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters and the heartland boiled together—

sentences.zh: 〈方，四方；

translations.literal: 〈Fang means the four directions;
translations.idiomatic: fang the four directions,

sentences.zh: 夏，華夏也。

translations.literal: Xia means Hua-Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Xia the civilized core—

sentences.zh: 《詩．小雅》云：「百川沸騰，山冢崒崩。」〉

translations.literal: The Classic Poetry, "Xiao Ya," states: "The hundred rivers boil; hill tombs topple and collapse."〉
translations.idiomatic: as a lesser ode cries when mountains slide into foaming rivers."〉

sentences.zh: 皇京烟埃。

translations.literal: The royal capital smoked with dust.
translations.idiomatic: until the royal capital choked on dust.

sentences.zh: 無禮雖及，餘祲遂廣。

translations.literal: Though the impious man himself met his end, the lingering evil thereafter spread wide.
translations.idiomatic: The tyrant fell, yet the evil he uncorked rolled on.

sentences.zh: 〈《左傳》曰：「多行無禮，必自及。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Zuo Tradition states: "Much unrighteousness is sure to rebound on oneself."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo zhuan promises that wanton crime returns on the sinner.〉

sentences.zh: 矢延王輅，兵纏魏象。

translations.literal: Arrows reached the king's chariot; soldiers wound about the Wei altars.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows whistled round the emperor's carriage; spearmen ringed the Wei ancestral temple—

sentences.zh: 〈《周禮》巾車氏掌王之五輅。

translations.literal: 〈The Rites of Zhou: the Jin-che office holds the king's five lu chariots.
translations.idiomatic: the Zhou li speaks of the five imperial chariots—

sentences.zh: 纏，遶也。

translations.literal: Chan means to wind around.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss: chan means to encircle or coil about.

sentences.zh: 魏象，闕也。〉

translations.literal: Wei xiang means the gate tower.〉
translations.idiomatic: Wei xiang refers to the twin gate-towers of the Wei ancestral shrine.〉

sentences.zh: 區服傾回，人神波蕩。

translations.literal: The regional zones overturned and reeled; men and spirits surged like waves.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal domains reeled; human order and the spirits alike were cast adrift.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation record
translations.idiomatic: Editorial collation notes

sentences.zh: 二三一九頁 三行 董卓字仲穎 按：刊誤謂依注則「穎」當作「穎」。

translations.literal: Page 2319 line 3: Dong Zhuo's courtesy name Zhongying. Note: Kanwu argues the main text's ying graph should match the form used in the commentary gloss.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: editors harmonize the ying character between text and commentary.

sentences.zh: 二三二０頁 三行 殺護羌校尉泠征 按：沉家本謂靈紀「泠」作「伶」。

translations.literal: Page 2320 line 3: killed Colonel Who Protects the Qiang Ling Zheng. Note: Shen Jiaben says the Lingji writes ling as ling.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: variant spelling of the colonel's name Ling versus Ling.

sentences.zh: 二三二一頁 二行 涼州義從宋建王國等反 「涼」原作「梁」，各本同，逕改正。

translations.literal: Page 2321 line 2: Liangzhou volunteer followers Song Jian, Wang Guo, and others rebelled. "Liang" (for Liangzhou) was originally miswritten as "Liang" (the graph for the unrelated Liang region) in all editions; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: misprint Liang for Liangzhou emended throughout.

sentences.zh: 按：《种暠傳》「後涼州羌動，以暠為涼州刺史」，汲本、殿本「涼」並作「梁」，集解引陳景雲說，謂「梁」當作「涼」，漢無梁州，至晉始置耳。

translations.literal: Note: the Biography of Chong Hao says "Later when Liangzhou Qiang rose in revolt, Hao was made inspector of Liangzhou"; Jiben and Dianben miswrite the province name with the graph Liang (Liang). Jijie cites Chen Jingyun that it must be Liang (Liang)—Han had no province written with the other Liang until Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the graphs for Liangzhou versus the unrelated Liang region are confused in early editions.

sentences.zh: 二三二一頁 二行 太守陳懿勸之使*

translations.literal: Page 2321 line 2: Grand Administrator Chen Yi urged him to send*
translations.idiomatic: Collation: damaged line on Chen Yi's memorial—

translations.literal: (Wang)
translations.idiomatic: —insertion mark for emendation—

sentences.zh: **[往]* 按：刊誤謂此「王」當作「往」，陳懿勸約使往也。

translations.literal: **[to go]* Note: Kanwu says this "wang" should be "wang" (to go)—Chen Yi urged the covenant to send someone.
translations.idiomatic: —reading wang "to go" for the graph wang.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted in the critical text.

sentences.zh: 二三二一頁 三行 國等扶以到護羌營 按：校補謂作「扶」無義，當是「挾」之訛。

translations.literal: Page 2321 line 3: Guo and others supported him to reach the Protect-the-Qiang camp. Note: Jiaobu says "support" makes no sense; it must be a corruption of "seize."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: fu "support" emended to xie "drag along" or "seize."

sentences.zh: 二三二二頁 七行 又無壯事 按：殿本「事」作「士」，疑訛。

translations.literal: Page 2322 line 7: also no zhuang deeds. Note: Dianben writes "shi" as "shi" for soldier—possibly a scribal error.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: zhuang shi versus zhuang shi in Dong Zhuo's memorial.

sentences.zh: 二三二二頁一四行 濁亂海內 按：集解引王補說，謂袁紀「濁」作「汨」。

translations.literal: Page 2322 line 14: fouled and disordered within the seas. Note: Jijie cites Wang Bu that Yuan ji writes fou as gu.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: variant graphs fou versus gu in Dong Zhuo's memorial.

sentences.zh: 二三二三頁 二行 中常侍段珪 「段」原作「弃」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Page 2323 line 2: Palace Attendant Duan Gui. "Duan" was originally written qi; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Duan Gui's surname miswritten as qi in some blocks.

sentences.zh: 下同，不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Same below; not every instance is noted in the collation.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent identical corrections are silently applied.

sentences.zh: 二三二三頁 八行 晉趙鞅取晉陽之甲以逐荀寅與士吉射*[荀寅與士吉射]*者曷為*[者也]* 注有脫文，不可句讀，今據公羊傳補。

translations.literal: Page 2323 line 8: Jin Zhao Yang took the armor of Jinyang to expel Xun Yin and Shi Jishe—[why were Xun Yin and Shi Jishe]*[what sort of men were they]* The commentary had lacunae and could not be parsed; now supplied per the Gongyang zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: restored missing words in the Gongyang quotation from the received Gongyang text.

sentences.zh: 二三二三頁一一行 下數百萬膏腴美田 按：沉家本謂「下」字不可解，當依魏志董卓傳注作「京畿諸郡」四字。

translations.literal: Page 2323 line 11: below several million fertile fields. Note: Shen Jiaben says "below" is unintelligible; Wei zhi Dong Zhuo commentary should read "the several commanderies around the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "below" emended to a longer phrase about the capital region in the Wei zhi parallel.

sentences.zh: 二三二五頁 八行 今岐州縣 按：「岐」原作「歧」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Page 2325 line 8: now Qi prefecture county. Note: "Qi" was originally written qi; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: placename Qi versus qi.

sentences.zh: 二三二五頁 九行 置*

translations.literal: Page 2325 line 9: established*
translations.idiomatic: Collation: office title—

translations.literal: (cheng)
translations.idiomatic: —insertion—

sentences.zh: *令*[丞]* 刊誤謂漢書內皆言「令丞」，此不合倒之。

translations.literal: *ling*[cheng]* Kanwu says the Han shu always says "ling and cheng" in that order; here the inversion is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: order of "grand administrator" and "chancellor" titles corrected.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted.

sentences.zh: 按：魏志卓傳作「置家令丞」。

translations.literal: Note: Wei zhi Dong Zhuo biography reads "established household chancellor and grand administrator."
translations.idiomatic: Parallel in Wei zhi confirms the wording.

sentences.zh: 二三二六頁一二行 漢陽周珌 按：集解引錢大昕說，謂章懷注引英雄記，雲周毖武威人，此與蜀志許靖傳俱云「漢陽」，未知孰是。

translations.literal: Page 2326 line 12: Hanyang Zhou Bi. Note: Jijie cites Qian Daxin that Zhanghuai's Yingxiong ji quotes Zhou Bi as a Wuwei man, while this and Shu zhi Xu Jing disagree.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Zhou Bi's home commandery varies between sources.

sentences.zh: 又引惠棟說，謂袁宏紀云「侍中周毖」，魏志亦作「毖」。

translations.literal: Also cites Hui Dong that Yuan Hong ji writes "Palace Attendant Zhou Bi," and Wei zhi also writes Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Further variants of the name Bi versus Bi.

sentences.zh: 二三二六頁一二行 侍中汝南伍瓊 按：集解引惠棟說，謂魏志云「城門校尉汝南伍瓊」。

translations.literal: Page 2326 line 12: Palace Attendant Wu Qiong of Runan. Note: Jijie cites Hui Dong that Wei zhi says "Colonel of the City Gates Wu Qiong of Runan."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Wu Qiong's office title differs in Wei zhi.

sentences.zh: 二三二七頁 六行 獻帝春秋咨作資 按：魏志亦作「資」。

translations.literal: Page 2327 line 6: Xiandi chunqiu writes zi as zi. Note: Wei zhi also writes zi.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: zi versus zi in a quotation.

sentences.zh: 二三二七頁一五行 悉燒宮廟官府居家 按：集解引惠棟說，謂魏志引續漢書「居家」作「民家」。

translations.literal: Page 2327 line 15: entirely burned palaces, government offices, and dwellings. Note: Jijie cites Hui Dong that Wei zhi citing Xù Han shu writes "commoners' homes" for "dwellings."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "dwellings" versus "people's houses" in parallel texts.

sentences.zh: 二三二八頁一一行 聚兵於陝 「陝」原作「陜」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Page 2328 line 11: gathered troops at Shan. "Shan" was originally written Shan; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Shan versus Shan (homophone error).

sentences.zh: 下同。

translations.literal: Same below.
translations.idiomatic: Applied throughout.

sentences.zh: 二三二九頁 五行 從東第三門 按：刊誤謂案文少「名宣陽」三字。

translations.literal: Page 2329 line 5: third from the east. Note: Kanwu says the text lacks the three characters "named Xuanyang."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: lacuna supplying the gate name Xuanyang.

sentences.zh: 二三二九頁 七行 *

translations.literal: Page 2329 line 7 *
translations.idiomatic: Collation: damaged—

translations.literal: (gong)
translations.idiomatic: —emendation—

sentences.zh: **[弃]*饋周急 據殿本改。

translations.literal: **[qi]* ji zhou ji Dianben emendation.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: gong versus qi in "presented tribute and relieved distress."

sentences.zh: 按：王先謙謂作「弃」是。

translations.literal: Note: Wang Xianqian says writing qi is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Editor prefers qi.

sentences.zh: 二三二九頁一四行 今俗以事干人者謂之相竿摩 汲本「相竿摩」之「竿」作「干」。

translations.literal: Page 2329 line 14: vulgar speech today calls importuning people "mutual pole-rubbing." Jiben writes the gan of gan-mo as the gan of "interfere."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: gan versus gan in the slang phrase gan-mo.

sentences.zh: 按：校補謂注本通竿於干，承上「干人」來，作「干」為長。

translations.literal: Note: Jiaobu says the commentary puns gan with the preceding gan "interfere"; writing gan is preferable.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial preference for gan.

sentences.zh: 二三三０頁 一行 卓施帳幔飲設 按：校補謂：案《魏志》原文本無「設」字，此「飲設」當作「設飲」。

translations.literal: Page 2330 line 1: Zhuo spread curtains and hangings and drink provisions. Note: Jiaobu says the Wei zhi original lacks "provisions"; yin-she should read she-yin "set out a banquet."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: word order yin she versus she yin.

sentences.zh: 二三三０頁 二行 偃轉*

translations.literal: Page 2330, line 2: yan zhuan «writhed and turned»—the trailing asterisk marks a broken graph continued on the following line.
translations.idiomatic: Collation headline for page 2330, line 2: the compound yan zhuan is split mid-character; the next line prints the damaged graph, which editors normalize to bei «cup» in the phrase «among cups and cases.»

translations.literal: (bei)
translations.idiomatic: —graph—

sentences.zh: **[杯]*案閒 按：「柸」非「杯」字，各本並訛，今改正。

translations.literal: **[bei]* among cases Note: bei is not the bei "cup"; all editions err; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: bei "cup" for wrong graph in "cups and cases."

sentences.zh: 二三三一頁一一行 騎都尉李肅 按：通鑒考異謂袁紀作「李順」。

translations.literal: Page 2331 line 11: Chief of Cavalry Li Su. Note: Zizhi tongjian kaoyi says Yuan ji writes Li Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Li Su versus Li Shun.

sentences.zh: 二三三一頁一四行 主簿田儀 按：魏志作「田景」。

translations.literal: Page 2331 line 14: Registrar Tian Yi. Note: Wei zhi writes Tian Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Tian Yi versus Tian Jing.

sentences.zh: 二三三二頁 五行 瑞字君榮 殿本考證謂：何焯校本「榮」改「策」。

translations.literal: Page 2332 line 5: Rui's courtesy name Junrong. Dianben kaozheng: He Zhuo's collated edition changes rong to ce.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Junrong versus Junce in Shisun Rui's name.

sentences.zh: 按：王允傳作「策」。

translations.literal: Note: Wang Yun biography writes ce.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun chapter uses ce.

sentences.zh: 二三三二頁 五行 封子萌津亭侯 按：殿本「津」作「車」。

translations.literal: Page 2332 line 5: enfeoffed his son Meng Marquis of Jinting. Note: Dianben writes "che" for "jin" in Jinting.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Jinting versus Cheting marquisate name.

sentences.zh: 二三三二頁 九行 俠叉卓車 汲本「俠」作「挾」。

translations.literal: Page 2332 line 9: flanked and forked Zhuo's carriage. Jiben writes xia as xie.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: xia versus xie for "pin with halberds."

sentences.zh: 按：俠與挾通。

translations.literal: Note: xia and xie are interchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: The two graphs are cognate variants.

sentences.zh: 二三三三頁一三行 弃尉種拂 按：集解引錢大昕說，謂案獻帝紀、種拂傳皆云「太常」，非「弃尉」也。

translations.literal: Page 2333 line 13: Commandant of the Guards Zhong Fu. Note: Jijie cites Qian Daxin that Xiandi ji and Zhong Fu biography both say "Grand Master of Ceremonies," not commandant of the guards—the graphs for the two offices were confused in transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Zhong Fu held the post of grand master of ceremonies at death; "commandant of the guards" is a textual error.

sentences.zh: 二三三四頁 五行 袁宏紀曰 「紀」原作「記」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Page 2334 line 5: Yuan Hong ji says "ji" was originally written "ji"; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: ji versus ji for "annals."

sentences.zh: 按：注中紀記互誤，各本多有，以後徑改正，不出校記。

translations.literal: Note: ji and ji are confused in commentary throughout editions; hereafter corrected silently.
translations.idiomatic: Standing policy on this misprint.

sentences.zh: 二三三五頁 四行 右中郎將劉范 集解引惠棟說，謂本紀及種劭傳皆云「左中郎將」。

translations.literal: Page 2335 line 4: General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the Right Liu Fan. Note: Jijie cites Hui Dong that the annals and Zhong Shao biography say "General of the Left."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: left versus right general for Liu Fan.

sentences.zh: 按：沈家本謂魏志卓傳、蜀志劉焉傳並作「左中郎將」。

translations.literal: Note: Shen Jiaben says Wei zhi Dong Zhuo and Shu zhi Liu Yan both say "General of the Left."
translations.idiomatic: Further support for "left."

sentences.zh: 二三三五頁 五行 前涼州刺史種劭 按：「劭」原作「邵」，各本並訛，徑改正。

translations.literal: Page 2335 line 5: former Inspector of Liangzhou Zhong Shao. Note: "Shao" was originally written Shao in all editions; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Zhong Shao versus homophone misprint.

sentences.zh: 二三三六頁 二行 便忿憤恚怒 按：「恚」原作「喜」，逕據汲本、殿本改正。

translations.literal: Page 2336 line 2: then resented and raged. Note: "hui" was originally written xi; corrected from Jiben and Dianben.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: hui "resent" versus xi "joy" scribal error.

sentences.zh: 二三二六頁 七行 皆詣省閣謝 按：刊誤謂案文「閣」當作「合」。

translations.literal: Page 2326 line 7: all went to the sheng-ge to apologize. Note: Kanwu says ge should be he "compound gate."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: sheng-ge versus sheng-he for the secretariat gate.

sentences.zh: 二三三七頁一三行 尋復欲徙帝於池陽黃白城 按：「徙」原作「徒」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Page 2337 line 13: soon again wished to move the emperor to Chiyang Huangbai walled town. Note: "move" was originally written "follower"; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: xi "move" versus tu scribal error.

sentences.zh: 二三三八頁 九行 歌謳擊鼓下神祭 按：沈家本謂魏志裴注引獻帝起居注，「祭」上有「祠」字，此奪。

translations.literal: Page 2338 line 9: singing, beating drums, descending gods, sacrifice. Note: Shen Jiaben says Wei zhi Pei commentary citing Xiandi qiju zhu has an extra si "offer cult" before ji.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: lacuna of si in Li Jue's shamanic ritual list.

sentences.zh: 二三三八頁一０行 左中郎將李國持節拜傕為大司馬 按：沈家本謂魏志注「李國」作「李固」。

translations.literal: Page 2338 line 10: General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the Left Li Guo bearing credentials invested Jue as Grand Marshal. Note: Shen Jiaben says Wei zhu writes Li Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Li Guo versus Li Gu.

sentences.zh: 又 按：「持」原作「特」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Also note: "bearing" was originally written "special"; corrected directly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: chi "bear" versus te misprint.

sentences.zh: 二三三九頁 二行 濟使太官令孫篤校尉張式 按：校補引柳從辰說，謂袁紀作「太官令狐篤、綏民校尉張裁」。

translations.literal: Page 2339 line 2: Ji ordered Grand Provisioner Sun Du and Colonel Zhang Shi. Note: Jiaobu cites Liu Congchen that Yuan ji writes Grand Provisioner Linghu Du and suimin colonel Zhang Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: names and offices in Zhang Ji's embassy.

sentences.zh: 二三三九頁 三行 是天子非 按：袁紀作「此天子非也」。

translations.literal: Page 2339 line 3: is this the Son of Heaven or not. Note: Yuan ji reads "This is not the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: wording of the bridge challenge.

sentences.zh: 沈家本謂魏志注「非」作「邪」。

translations.literal: Shen Jiaben says Wei zhi commentary writes fei as ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei zhi uses ye particle instead of fei.

sentences.zh: 二三四０頁一一行 拜胡才征東將軍 按：校補謂案照下文「征」上亦應有「為」字。

translations.literal: Page 2340 line 11: appointed Hu Cai General Who Strikes the East. Note: Jiaobu says per the wording below, wei "as" should also appear before zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: missing wei before military title.

sentences.zh: 二三四０頁一五行 儁年二十五 按：「儁」原作「俊」，逕據汲本、殿本改正。

translations.literal: Page 2340 line 15: Jun was twenty-five. Note: "Jun" was originally written jun; corrected from Jiben and Dianben.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Ju Jun versus homophone.

sentences.zh: 二三四０頁一五行 其督戰訾寶 按：校補引柳從辰說，謂袁紀「訾寶」作「訾置」。

translations.literal: Page 2340 line 15: his battle supervisor Zi Bao. Note: Jiaobu cites Liu Congchen that Yuan ji writes Zi zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Zi Bao versus Zi zhi.

sentences.zh: 二三四一頁 二行 有三十六難 按：袁紀同。

translations.literal: Page 2341 line 2: there are thirty-six perils. Note: Yuan ji agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: nan "perils" reading.

sentences.zh: 汲本、殿本「難」作「灘」，魏志注引獻帝紀同。

translations.literal: Jiben and Dianben write nan as tan; Wei zhi commentary citing Xiandi ji agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Variant nan versus tan "rapids" for the Yellow River hazards.

sentences.zh: 二三四一頁 二行 舊故*[有]*河師猶時有傾危 「舊故河師」不成文理，今據袁紀補一「有」字。

translations.literal: Page 2341 line 2: old river pilots*[have]*—"old river pilots" was ungrammatical; now supplemented one you "have" per Yuan ji.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: inserted you for grammar in Yang Biao's speech.

sentences.zh: 按：魏志注作「有師猶有傾覆」。

translations.literal: Note: Wei zhi commentary reads "with pilots there are still capsizings."
translations.idiomatic: Parallel wording in Wei zhi.

sentences.zh: 二三四一頁 五行 按：校補謂此注當在上文「唯皇后、宋貴人俱」下。

translations.literal: Page 2341 line 5: Note: Jiaobu says this commentary should stand below "only the empress and Honored Lady Song accompanied."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: misplaced commentary block noted for reordering.

sentences.zh: 二三四一頁一０行 魏*

translations.literal: Page 2341, line 10: Wei with a trailing asterisk—showing the citation title is fractured and completed on the next line.
translations.idiomatic: Collation headline for page 2341, line 10: the word Wei begins a lacuna that the following line closes with zhi, yielding the book title Wei shu «Documents of Wei» cited from Wang Chen.

translations.literal: (zhi)
translations.idiomatic: —emendation—

sentences.zh: **[書]*曰 據惠棟補注改。

translations.literal: **[shu]* says Emended per Hui Dong's supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: citation header Wei shu for Wang Chen's text.

sentences.zh: 按：注所引乃王沈魏書文，魏志董卓傳裴注亦引之。

translations.literal: Note: the quoted passage is from Wang Chen's Wei shu; Wei zhi Dong Zhuo Pei commentary also cites it.
translations.idiomatic: Source identification for the Wei shu quotation.

sentences.zh: 二三四一頁一０行 諸將或遣婢詣省問 刊誤謂「問」當作「合」。

translations.literal: Page 2341 line 10: generals sometimes sent maids to the secretariat on business. Kanwu says "wen" should be he.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: wen versus he for "secretariat compound."

sentences.zh: 今 按：魏志董卓傳裴注引正作「合」。

translations.literal: Now: Wei zhi Dong Zhuo Pei commentary correctly writes he.
translations.idiomatic: Wei zhi has he.

sentences.zh: 集解引周壽昌說，謂此時天子居棘籬中，尚有何省合可詣乎？

translations.literal: Jijie cites Zhou Shouchang: at this time the Son of Heaven dwelt in a thorn hedge—what secretariat gate remained to visit?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shouchang's objection to the he emendation.

sentences.zh: 省問即存問，恐魏書本如是，不必作「合」字也。

translations.literal: "Secretariat inquiry" means to inquire after welfare; perhaps Wei shu originally read wen and need not be changed to he.
translations.idiomatic: Alternative: keep wen as "inquire."

sentences.zh: 二三四二頁 七行 明年左將軍劉備誘奉斬之 按：李慈銘謂案三國誌先主傳，是時尚為鎮東將軍，未拜左將軍也。

translations.literal: Page 2342 line 7: next year General of the Left Liu Bei lured Feng and beheaded him. Note: Li Ciming says checking Sanguo zhi Xiandi zhuan, at this time Liu Bei was still General Who Guards the East, not yet General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Liu Bei's rank at the time of Yang Feng's death.

sentences.zh: 二三四二頁一０行 侍中*

translations.literal: Page 2342, line 10: Palace attendant—asterisk shows the office title is broken and completed on the following line.
translations.idiomatic: Collation headline for page 2342, line 10: the title shi zhong «palace attendant» is split here; the next line supplies the graphs for tai «podium» in the name Tai Chong, correcting a miswritten hu «jar».

translations.literal: (tai)
translations.idiomatic: —graph—

sentences.zh: **[台]* 崇集解引惠棟說，謂「壺」當作「台」，詳見獻帝紀。

translations.literal: **[tai]* Chong Note: Jijie cites Hui Dong that hu should be tai—see Xiandi ji.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Palace Attendant Tai Chong versus Hu Chong.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted.

sentences.zh: 二三四三頁 四行 四年張楊為其將楊丑所殺 集解引錢大昕說，謂案獻帝紀，在三年十二月。

translations.literal: Page 2343 line 4: fourth year Zhang Yang was killed by his officer Yang Chou. Note: Jijie cites Qian Daxin that checking Xiandi ji, the event falls in twelfth month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: dating of Zhang Yang's death—third versus fourth year.

sentences.zh: 按：校補謂袁紀亦屬之三年，與獻紀合。

translations.literal: Note: Jiaobu says Yuan ji also places it in the third year, matching the annals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan ji agrees with third year.

sentences.zh: 又「楊丑」袁紀作「眭固」，亦異。

translations.literal: Also "Yang Chou" Yuan ji writes Sui Gu—another discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: killer's name Yang Chou versus Sui Gu.

sentences.zh: 二三四三頁一五行 太僕端之子也 按：殿本「端」作「瑞」。

translations.literal: Page 2343 line 15: son of Grand Coach Duan. Note: Dianben writes "duan" as "rui."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Wei Duan versus Wei Rui for Wei Kang's father.

sentences.zh: 二三四四頁 二行 使弟岳於城上作偃月營 按：「岳」原作「岳」，而下文又作「岳」，今據汲本、殿本徑改為「岳」，俾前後一致，與魏志亦合。

translations.literal: Page 2344 line 2: ordered younger brother Yue on the wall to form a crescent camp. Note: "Yue" was originally written yue; below also yue; now uniformly emended to yue per Jiben and Dianben for consistency with Wei zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Yang Yue name graphs unified.

sentences.zh: 二三四四頁 三行 阜少長*

translations.literal: Page 2344, line 3: Fu shao zhang «Yang Fu from youth grew up»—asterisk marks a lacuna before the next line’s graphs.
translations.idiomatic: Collation headline for page 2344, line 3: the phrase shao zhang is interrupted at the asterisk; later editors wrongly inserted yu «go to» before qi jia «in Xu’s household» in the following sentence, a gloss the Wei zhi biography of Yang Fu does not support.

translations.literal: (yu)
translations.idiomatic: —erroneous insertion—

sentences.zh: *弃家刊誤謂此言阜自少長於弃家，後人不曉，妄加一「詣」字。

translations.literal: *at Qi home Kanwu says this means Fu grew up from youth in Qi's household; later readers did not understand and wrongly added yu "go to."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: deletion of spurious yu before qi jia.

sentences.zh: 按：《魏志·楊阜傳》亦作「阜少長弃家」，今據刪。

translations.literal: Note: Wei zhi Yang Fu biography also reads "Fu from youth grew up in Qi's household"; now deleted per that.
translations.idiomatic: Wei zhi supports text without yu.

sentences.zh: 二三四四頁 五行 得棄母*[棄母]*罵之曰 按：不重「弃母」二字，則文意不明，今據魏志楊阜傳補。

translations.literal: Page 2344 line 5: captured Xu's mother*[Xu's mother]* reviled him saying Note: without repeating "Xu's mother" the sense is unclear; now supplemented per Wei zhi Yang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: duplicated phrase for clarity in Ma Chao scene.

sentences.zh: 二三四四頁一０行 泉字妙才汲本、殿本「泉」作「淵」。

translations.literal: Page 2344 line 10: Quan, courtesy name Miaocai—Jiben and Dianben write "quan" as "yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Xiahou Yuan name taboo—Tang avoidance left yuan for yuan.

sentences.zh: 按：此避唐諱，漏未追改。

translations.literal: Note: Tang taboo incompletely restored in later printings.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note on incomplete reversal of the Tang taboo change.
